commits.title: Allow API-key accounts to use Daybreak in the TUI (#50433)
commits.message:
Allow API-key accounts to use Daybreak in the TUI (#50433)

## What changed

Allow accounts using an API key with the OpenAI provider to access `/daybreak` and Daybreak policy notices. Model availability and the connected server still determine program access.

Use the same eligibility checks for turn submission, continuation, and retries. For API-key accounts, send the selected `cyberAccessProgram` when Daybreak is enabled and omit it when Daybreak is off.

## Testing

Extend session lifecycle coverage to check API-key turn parameters with Daybreak enabled and disabled. Add an API-key `/daybreak` help snapshot and update the signed-out error snapshot.

GitOrigin-RevId: ab6d4313c430f316ef9835d4facb878aab0b9725

commits.title: Add keyboard copy selection to the owned transcript (#50434)
commits.message:
Add keyboard copy selection to the owned transcript (#50434)

## What changed

- Make `/copy` select the latest completed response directly in the owned transcript. Navigate user messages, code blocks, and blockquotes with arrow keys or `j`/`k`, use `g`/`G` to jump to the ends, and press Enter to copy or Escape to close.
- Highlight selected blocks and keep surrounding context visible during navigation and resizing. Preserve source payloads for code and quotes, including rendered Mermaid diagrams and fenced Markdown tables.
- Pause queued submissions until copy mode closes, and report clipboard results in the transcript footer.

## Testing

Add tests for copy routing, keyboard navigation, highlighting and resize behavior, source whitespace and line endings, clipboard completion, and queued-input resumption.

GitOrigin-RevId: bd4f58ec17568f95d0e91014e5ddba33ca8bd57c

commits.title: Persist additional tool definitions in rollout history (#50435)
commits.message:
Persist additional tool definitions in rollout history (#50435)

## Why

`additional_tools` response items were excluded from rollout persistence, dropping their tool definitions from saved history.

## What changed

- Persist `additional_tools` items in both legacy and paginated history modes.
- Expose the variant in generated JSON schemas, TypeScript types, and Python models, with an optional `id`, a `role`, and arbitrary JSON tool definitions.

## Testing

Add a recorder round-trip test that verifies tool definitions survive recording and loading in both history modes without parse errors.

GitOrigin-RevId: 0e7c7b1c10401ec6513fb744de642a1cf9e461d7

commits.title: Add a CLI command to uninstall the legacy Windows sandbox (#50437)
commits.message:
Add a CLI command to uninstall the legacy Windows sandbox (#50437)

## What changed

Add `codex sandbox uninstall` to remove machine-wide legacy Windows sandbox accounts and network rules with administrator privileges. Run cleanup without loading configuration, preserving Codex home, sandbox directories, and filesystem permissions. Reject the command on other platforms.

Keep commands after `--` forwarded to the sandbox, including `codex sandbox -- uninstall --help`.

## Testing

Add parsing coverage for the uninstall subcommand and command separator. Add an integration test verifying that help and invalid arguments work with malformed configuration and leave configuration and credentials unchanged.

GitOrigin-RevId: d2b02ef7bc0a05742dd5eb3c47292ad517d46664

commits.title: Support ordered response items in world-state context updates (#50441)
commits.message:
Support ordered response items in world-state context updates (#50441)

## Why

World-state sections could return only a single optional text fragment, with message separation controlled by the fragment itself. They could not contribute explicit `ResponseItem` values alongside instructions.

## What changed

- Let sections return ordered `WorldStateUpdate` values containing fragments or response items, with `Prefix`, `Standalone`, or `Mergeable` placement.
- Preserve explicit item boundaries when grouping context updates, and place prefix updates first when assembling initial context.
- Move standalone-message decisions from fragments to world-state updates and retain snapshot handling.

## Testing

Add tests for mixed fragment/item ordering, role and standalone boundaries, initial-context prefix placement, and snapshot restoration without repeated updates.

GitOrigin-RevId: c2514c3c98538da83f5140c10a9d89f531de6549

commits.title: Preserve native USD amounts in thread usage responses (#50442)
commits.message:
Preserve native USD amounts in thread usage responses (#50442)

## What changed

Add optional `native_usage_usd_micros` fields to thread usage totals and breakdown groups, and carry backend values through the client alongside existing credit and USD estimates. Missing or null native amounts remain `None`, while explicit zero amounts remain `Some(0)`.

## Testing

Add coverage for native totals and group amounts, mixed batches with legacy responses, and the distinction between missing, null, and zero native group amounts.

GitOrigin-RevId: 53891fc95807138e2eccb99d4cda1520b857dba4

commits.title: Stabilize paused-time code-mode service tests (#50443)
commits.message:
Stabilize paused-time code-mode service tests (#50443)

## Why

Tokio's paused clock can auto-advance while tests await the V8 thread. The service tests need explicit control over time when checking yield limits and grace periods.

## What changed

- Hold virtual time with a blocking-task guard that is released when dropped.
- Replace bounded polling loops with tool-start notifications and direct awaits of response tasks.
- Return an error from the test helper if the cell closes before a nested tool starts.

## Testing

Add tests covering tool-start acknowledgement when a cell throws or is terminated before invoking a nested tool, including assertions on the resulting cell responses.

GitOrigin-RevId: c221c0501ec0354052102c0211cc651008babff3

commits.title: Assert that only direct tool calls emit timing events (#50445)
commits.message:
Assert that only direct tool calls emit timing events (#50445)

## What changed

Strengthen `tool_call_timing_guard_ignores_code_mode_source` to capture tracing output and assert that direct and nested code-mode calls together emit exactly one `codex.tool_call` event. Disable ANSI formatting and keep callsite interest independent of untraced parallel test threads.

GitOrigin-RevId: cbf0c9bf6d4e5a72b6a1eb08e6aac43e257f2dcb

commits.title: Bundle rollout attachments into a gzip tar archive (#50446)
commits.message:
Bundle rollout attachments into a gzip tar archive (#50446)

## What changed

- Combine file-backed rollouts and buffered rollout prefixes into `rollouts.tar.gz`, keeping diagnostics as separate attachments.
- Bound the archive and its upload envelope by the existing size limit, skip invalid or duplicate archive filenames, and fall back to individual rollout attachments if archiving fails.
- Add `rollout_archive_filename` to the report thread index so rollout filenames identify archive entries or fallback attachments.

## Testing

Add an upload test that extracts the archive and verifies the filenames and contents of both a compressed file-backed rollout and a buffered rollout. Update the thread index test to check the archive filename.

GitOrigin-RevId: 973da6eec2249b04ef7992b5e1e4fd27f044b80f

commits.title: Remove the provider capability gate for tool namespaces (#50447)
commits.message:
Remove the provider capability gate for tool namespaces (#50447)

## What changed

- Remove `namespace_tools` from `ProviderCapabilities` and `namespaceTools` from `ModelProviderCapabilitiesReadResponse`, updating generated schemas and SDK types.
- Preserve tool namespaces and configured collaboration tool namespaces without a provider capability check, and always use Responses Lite tool serialization for Responses Lite requests.
- Gate tool search on `supports_search_tool` and retain the existing image generation and web search checks without requiring a namespace capability.

GitOrigin-RevId: ae1843563736765a40e03a02c41ff5e470018a93

commits.title: Measure rollout persistence size reductions (#50454)
commits.message:
Measure rollout persistence size reductions (#50454)

## What changed

- Record original and persisted item sizes in `codex.rollout.persistence.item_bytes_v2`, distinguished by stage, and record positive size reductions in `codex.rollout.persistence.bytes_removed`. Count the full original size as removed for dropped items.
- Use explicit histogram boundaries from 1 KiB to 64 MiB for item sizes, bytes removed, and `codex.rollout.persistence.turn_bytes_v2`. Larger values remain represented in the overflow bucket and histogram sum.
- Align item and turn size stages and report a measurement error when a kept item's persisted size cannot be measured.

GitOrigin-RevId: 6487acf1c6f2c041ab9680ab398491d3c1541388

commits.title: Truncate oversized MCP results in paginated thread history (#50458)
commits.message:
Truncate oversized MCP results in paginated thread history (#50458)

## Why

Paginated thread history can persist large MCP results in completed tool-call items. Bound these stored results to avoid retaining multi-megabyte payloads.

## What changed

Apply a 64 KiB preview budget when persisting oversized MCP results in paginated history. Replace the result with a truncated text preview of its serialized JSON, preserving `is_error` and clearing `structuredContent` and `_meta`. Leave small results unchanged.

Share the truncation helper with the existing MCP tool-call event path.

## Testing

Add helper tests for unchanged small results and oversized results with structured content and metadata. Add a thread-history test verifying that persisted MCP results contain a bounded preview with the beginning, end, and truncation marker while preserving tool arguments.

GitOrigin-RevId: 09dce73c70bfd357c9b9630f456e9e5c1d8492cf

commits.title: Add capability overrides for custom model providers (#50459)
commits.message:
Add capability overrides for custom model providers (#50459)

## What changed

Allow Responses-compatible providers to configure live web access and remote compaction under `model_providers.<id>.capabilities`:

```toml
[model_providers.custom.capabilities]
external_web_access = false
remote_compaction = "v2"
```

`external_web_access = false` keeps hosted web search from accessing the live web. `remote_compaction` accepts `v2` to send `compaction_trigger` items through the Responses endpoint, or `unsupported` to use local compaction. Omitted capabilities retain existing provider defaults.

## Testing

Add unit coverage for preserving unspecified defaults and a request-snapshot scenario verifying cached web search and V2 compaction for a custom provider.

GitOrigin-RevId: fbcc4870aa51c112af575d711679a3941d1e7878

commits.title: Populate thread previews from delegated task inputs (#50462)
commits.message:
Populate thread previews from delegated task inputs (#50462)

## Why

Delegated turns can begin without a user message, leaving threads without a task preview. Populate the preview from delegated input so these threads are discoverable before a user follow-up.

## What changed

- Extract previews from completed `create_thread` and `send_message_to_thread` outputs in the `codex_app` and `codex_tui` namespaces.
- Unwrap recognized `<codex_delegation>` inputs and decode their escaped task text for display, preserving model content. Keep plain or unrecognized wrappers as text and ignore blank inputs.
- Fill missing previews in state metadata extraction and live thread metadata updates without replacing existing previews or setting the title or `first_user_message`.

## Testing

Add tests for delegation decoding and tool filtering, preview-only metadata updates, preservation of later user-message metadata, and database listing before a user follow-up in both legacy and paginated history modes.

GitOrigin-RevId: f7b3c60ef75e08c76b4084d043e3967bf2bade22

commits.title: Add the `incremental_tools` feature flag (#50464)
commits.message:
Add the `incremental_tools` feature flag (#50464)

Register `incremental_tools` as an under-development feature that is disabled by default, and expose it in the configuration schema for top-level and profile feature settings.

GitOrigin-RevId: 9579822c745e9fce598085bdc5ef8da6aabb06d7

commits.title: Retry registry authentication outages and jitter executor reconnects (#50465)
commits.message:
Retry registry authentication outages and jitter executor reconnects (#50465)

## Why

Remote executors need to recover from confirmed authentication-service outages and spread reconnect attempts after a shared outage. Registration retries must remain limited to confirmed failures before a write, since replaying an ambiguous request can replace a newer registration.

## What changed

- Retry registry responses with HTTP 502 and `authentication_service_unavailable`, alongside the existing HTTP 503 `registration_conflict` retries.
- Accept structured registry errors in `detail`, keeping the canonical `error` authoritative when both are present.
- Randomize reconnect delays between half and all of the current exponential backoff, retaining the 30-second cap.

## Testing

Add coverage for reconnect jitter bounds, authentication-outage retry cancellation, error-envelope precedence, and preservation of Noise identity and initialized sessions across retries. Make the HTTP-header helper cleanup test wait for the helper PID before cancellation and verify process termination when the provider is dropped.

GitOrigin-RevId: 35fdb57732d17b0bbfeca8a4dc557a0988e29a31

commits.title: Copy transcript selections as literal text while preserving rich HTML (#50467)
commits.message:
Copy transcript selections as literal text while preserving rich HTML (#50467)

## Why

Copying rendered transcript selections added Markdown formatting and escapes to the plain-text clipboard payload. Selecting bold text such as `hello` could paste as `**hello**`.

## What changed

Separate the literal selection text from the Markdown source used to render clipboard HTML. Plain-text copies omit inline formatting delimiters, added code fences, and Markdown escapes while retaining list and table structure. Rich-text pastes continue to preserve formatting through HTML.

## Testing

Update clipboard and transcript selection tests to verify literal text alongside rich HTML, including lists, inline code, paths with Markdown punctuation, hard breaks, streamed code blocks, and tables across layout widths.

GitOrigin-RevId: 980ee2ed0b0e201b581a3a301fa04d796c65af2e

commits.title: Account for JSON overhead when truncating MCP tool results (#50470)
commits.message:
Account for JSON overhead when truncating MCP tool results (#50470)

## Why

Truncating the preview alone can leave the serialized MCP tool result above its byte budget because JSON escaping and the result wrapper add bytes.

## What changed

Measure the complete serialized replacement and progressively reduce the preview budget until the result fits or the preview is empty.

## Testing

Strengthen the regression test with quotes, backslashes, and newlines. Assert that the serialized result fits within the 1,024-byte budget and that truncating it again returns the existing result unchanged.

commits.title: Enable Ultrafast service tiers for Amazon Bedrock Astra models (#50472)
commits.message:
Enable Ultrafast service tiers for Amazon Bedrock Astra models (#50472)

## Why

Bedrock catalogs cleared all service-tier metadata, and requests omitted every selected tier. This prevented users from selecting `ultrafast` or using tiers defined in custom catalogs.

## What changed

- Advertise `ultrafast` for `openai.gpt-6-astra` on Mantle and the `global.openai.gpt-6-astra` and `us.openai.gpt-6-astra` Runtime variants, while retaining the implicit default tier unless users select otherwise.
- Preserve custom catalog speed tiers, service-tier definitions, and defaults while continuing to normalize Bedrock web search compatibility.
- Send selected service tiers only when the Bedrock model advertises them, including `flex`.

## Testing

Add coverage for `model/list` tier discovery, custom catalog preservation, configured and per-turn HTTP request tiers, and TUI slash-command selection, toggling, and model switching.

GitOrigin-RevId: 4793e7af7b9f604a6b7812611030da6adb8acd35

commits.title: Use the app-server default output cap for TUI workspace commands (#50477)
commits.message:
Use the app-server default output cap for TUI workspace commands (#50477)

## What changed

Remove the fixed 64 KiB output cap from `WorkspaceCommand` and send
`output_bytes_cap: None` in `command/exec` requests so bounded commands use
the app-server default. Preserve `disable_output_cap` for commands that need
uncapped output, including Git diffs.

GitOrigin-RevId: 6f2ed0d127d9ff2317670851894ae4988f7c7508

commits.title: Skip managed config loading for registered Windows sandbox refreshes (#50480)
commits.message:
Skip managed config loading for registered Windows sandbox refreshes (#50480)

## Why

Registration-only refreshes retain the existing sandbox, so package maintenance should not require another cloud-policy fetch.

## What changed

Skip managed configuration loading when a provisioning request has both `registered_core` and `refresh_only` set. The registered-runtime transaction still checks the existing owner, accounts, and unchanged settings under the setup lock. Other provisioning requests continue to enforce managed policy.

## Testing

Update the invalid-impersonation-token test to cover all four flag combinations, verifying that only registered refreshes succeed without loading configuration.

GitOrigin-RevId: e65ba1359be65e6314fa483b24fb66ed57a444ac

commits.title: Include installer stderr in daemon update failures (#50499)
commits.message:
Include installer stderr in daemon update failures (#50499)

## Why

Daemon updates discard installer stderr, leaving failed installs with only an exit status and no installer diagnostics.

## What changed

Capture the last 2 KiB of installer stderr and append it to errors when the installer exits unsuccessfully. Drain stderr concurrently and wait at most one second after failure so subprocesses holding the pipe open cannot delay error reporting indefinitely. Keep captured details within the manual update response limit, and configure PowerShell output as UTF-8 to preserve non-ASCII diagnostics.

## Testing

Add coverage for stderr tail truncation, bounded draining when a subprocess keeps stderr open, and manual update responses containing heavily escaped diagnostics. Extend the Windows installer test to check non-ASCII error text.

GitOrigin-RevId: d0da19b233006f97770d3f7f5f057e5e98fd2913

commits.title: Use Enter to accept transcript Find results and Escape to cancel (#50503)
commits.message:
Use Enter to accept transcript Find results and Escape to cancel (#50503)

## Why

Accepting a Find result must not let a held `Enter` submit the composer draft, including when terminals report repeated keys as fresh presses.

## What changed

- Make `Enter` accept the displayed result for reading, while `Ctrl+P` and `Ctrl+N` navigate older and newer matches.
- Make `Escape` cancel query editing and restore the pre-search presentation; after acceptance, it returns to the latest transcript content.
- Consume unmodified `Enter` while reading a result, but let modified `Enter` reach configured composer bindings.
- Update footer hints to show acceptance, cancellation, and the active Find state.

## Testing

Extend input-routing coverage for repeated `Enter` presses and modified composer bindings. Update search tests and footer snapshots for acceptance, cancellation, and result navigation.

GitOrigin-RevId: 2a2b7c389240ffa941e3623d7fb7d877455fa9a5

commits.title: Center TUI confirmations over their retained backdrop (#50504)
commits.message:
Center TUI confirmations over their retained backdrop (#50504)

## What changed

Render confirmation dialogs as centered overlays while preserving the composer or parent picker behind them. Share dialog sizing and cursor placement across stacked views and full transcript rendering, with input still routed exclusively to the active dialog.

Use the shared confirmation preset for prompts including full access, session archive/delete, goal changes, and log upload consent.

## Testing

Add coverage for backdrop retention and cursor routing at multiple terminal sizes, and for preserving the compact viewport and composer draft after dismissing a confirmation without replaying history. Update confirmation snapshots to show the retained backdrop.

GitOrigin-RevId: 026af89904ec345e2b330317b8cc844512125d0e

commits.title: Keep Command Center selection adjacent after task removal (#50505)
commits.message:
Keep Command Center selection adjacent after task removal (#50505)

## Why

Archiving or deleting the selected task could make Command Center selection jump to the current task instead of a neighboring task in the displayed list.

## What changed

Choose the next surviving task in displayed order before removing tasks, falling back to the previous task when needed. Apply this selection behavior to archive, delete, and hide actions, respecting filtering and grouping.

Preserve the pending selection across view rebuilds, batched removals, and duplicate server notifications. Allow selection to fall back when a rename target disappears while retaining the existing notice about its unsubmitted title.

## Testing

Add regression tests and snapshots for archive/delete selection across project, status, and model grouping, with and without filtering. Cover removal of the attached task, external removal notifications, removal of a pending successor, repeated repaints, and an empty task list. Update the disappeared-rename-target snapshot to verify that the remaining selection is preserved.

GitOrigin-RevId: ca93d664fadbc602993fbdae316c7a375b449345

commits.title: Record Windows sandbox service stop diagnostics (#50507)
commits.message:
Record Windows sandbox service stop diagnostics (#50507)

## What changed

Persist the service's last reported lifecycle reason and numeric HRESULT in the existing service registry key. Distinguish requested stops, shutdown, owner removal, startup failure, broker failure, and interrupted registration, and reset the record on startup. Recording is best-effort and does not affect the service lifecycle.

Emit `codex.windows_sandbox.service_stopped` when a provisioning client observes a stopped service, including the recorded reason, HRESULT, and Windows service exit codes. Recheck the service status and registry record before emitting to avoid pairing inconsistent evidence during a concurrent restart. The metric counts observations, not unique outages; the recorded reason is advisory.

Update the cached service status only after `SetServiceStatus` succeeds. Extract diagnostic error codes from typed errors without collecting error text or user data.

## Testing

Add a test covering Win32-to-HRESULT conversion, preservation of Windows HRESULTs through error context, and a zero fallback for untyped error text.

GitOrigin-RevId: d0d39d091410e2b5499a0803475804d12235f836

commits.title: Require GovCloud guidance acknowledgment after Bedrock setup (#50510)
commits.message:
Require GovCloud guidance acknowledgment after Bedrock setup (#50510)

## What changed

After successful Amazon Bedrock setup, check whether the configuration uses AWS GovCloud. If detected, show application configuration and security guidance with a terminal hyperlink and require an explicit Enter press to continue. Allow scrolling in short panes while keeping the acknowledgment visible.

Continue onboarding without the warning for non-GovCloud configurations, failed checks, or checks that exceed the 15-second timeout.

## Testing

Add snapshots and tests for the checking and warning screens, explicit acknowledgment, guidance hyperlinks, and scrolling in short panes, including a one-row content viewport.

commits.title: Add scenario coverage for remote `/compact` context preservation (#50516)
commits.message:
Add scenario coverage for remote `/compact` context preservation (#50516)

## What changed

Add a scenario test and snapshot covering the request before remote `/compact`, the compaction request, the persisted replacement history, and the first subsequent user turn.

Capture the replacement history before the next turn can update its context, and assert that the compaction request contains one `compaction_trigger` and the next request includes the returned encrypted checkpoint.

commits.title: Reject unknown TUI keys in strict config validation (#50525)
commits.message:
Reject unknown TUI keys in strict config validation (#50525)

## Why

Flattened notification settings prevent `serde_ignored` from detecting unknown keys in `[tui]`, allowing them to pass `--strict-config` validation.

## What changed

Detect unknown TUI keys by comparing configured keys with a serialized `Tui`, keeping accepted keys derived from the configuration type. Apply this check to config files and `-c`/`--config` overrides so keys such as `tui.bogus_key_xyz` produce an unknown-field error while valid notification settings remain accepted.

## Testing

When `flush_transcript_tail_on_session_end` is enabled, remaining speech must be available in thread history as soon as realtime closure is reported, even while a model response is still running. Saving that transcript should not trigger another model request.

## What changed

Record the transcript tail directly in model and client history, attaching it to the active turn or creating a completed history turn when idle. Flush persistence before emitting `RealtimeConversationClosed`, and keep realtime context active until recording finishes so the return to text instructions follow the transcript.

Changing a deferred tool's output schema could add or remove the shared MCP type preamble from the `exec` description.

## What changed

Include the default or configured MCP TypeScript preamble whenever `code_mode_only` is enabled, regardless of the available tools' output schemas. Preserve an empty preamble override as a way to omit the section.

Send the initial catalog once, then append only added or changed definitions while preserving earlier request history. Emit developer notices for removed tools and namespace instruction changes.

## Why

The managed daemon writes an executable and Unix-style state beneath `CODEX_HOME`. Windows-mounted WSL filesystems (DrvFS/9p) do not reliably support the required permission semantics, which can cause startup to fail before the TUI opens.

## What changed

Detect WSL homes on 9p filesystems, checking an existing ancestor when `CODEX_HOME` does not yet exist. Keep the TUI in embedded mode instead of automatically starting the shared background server, and show a startup warning explaining the exclusion.

## Why

`AbsolutePathBuf::relative_to_current_dir` previously read the current directory even for absolute paths, causing resolution to fail if the current directory had been deleted.

Route absolute inputs through `from_absolute_path` without querying the current directory. Relative inputs continue to resolve against the current directory.

commits.title: Distinguish daemon release identity from executable contents (#50559)
commits.message:
Distinguish daemon release identity from executable contents (#50559)

## Why

Releases can contain different resources while shipping identical executable bytes. The daemon must recognize those release changes, while a stale updater should be able to hand off without restarting an already-current daemon.

## What changed

- Include a digest of the resolved executable path in `ExecutableIdentity` to distinguish release generations with identical binaries.
- Keep content-only comparisons for package preparation and manual update reporting.
- Check the running daemon's identity and version before restarting during updater adoption, manual updates, and production restoration. Preserve scheduled retries when the daemon is not ready.

## Testing

Add coverage for path-sensitive identity, scheduled no-op updates that preserve the daemon, and resource-only release updates that restart it despite identical executable bytes.

Windows Terminal's `sendInput` mapping delivers `ESC[13;2u` as individual console key events. Decode it as `Shift+Enter` so the mapping inserts a newline in the composer.

commits.message:

MCP startup notifications from unrelated threads could create TUI event channels, allowing subsequent approval requests from those threads to appear in the current session.

## What changed

Check the parent of an untracked subagent before accepting its MCP startup notifications. Read thread metadata with bounded retries for threads that are not yet found or loaded, and ignore notifications unless the parent belongs to the TUI.

commits.message:

Executable scanners can briefly hold newly staged files without delete sharing, causing the rename that publishes a managed daemon release to fail on Windows.

## What changed

Retry publication on permission-denied or sharing-violation errors at 50 ms intervals, up to 100 retries. Report the staging and release paths if publication fails.

commits.title: Recover malformed Windows deny-read ACL state safely (#50940)
commits.message:

## Why

Malformed `deny_read_acl_state.json` previously caused deny-read ACL reconciliation to fail. Recovery must restore bookkeeping without removing unknown existing restrictions or modifying a linked file's contents.

## What changed

- Retry malformed reads for up to two seconds, then rebuild bookkeeping only after excluding active writers and successfully applying current deny-read ACLs. Preserve unknown historical denies and continue propagating I/O errors.
- Validate the opened state file before reading or writing, rejecting reparse points and files with multiple hard links.
- Write state in place without truncating before validation, preserving file identity and permissions. Retry sharing violations during writes while preventing replacement through delete access.

## Testing

Add Windows tests for corrupt-state recovery, linked-file rejection, concurrent writer and delete-handle behavior, file identity and ACL preservation, and subsequent permission-profile changes. Use issuing-step context for Guardian MCP elicitation reviews (#51067)

## Why

MCP elicitation reviews used turn-start context, which could omit remote environments that became ready before the tool invocation and use stale environment permissions.

## What changed

Capture the issuing step's Guardian review context with each live MCP invocation and reuse it for elicitation reviews. Fall back to turn context when no matching live invocation is available, and preserve the captured context for in-flight actions.

## Testing

Extend the deferred-executor regression test to cover MCP elicitations, checking that Guardian receives the newly ready remote environment and its denied paths, excludes stale local denied paths, and returns the denial to the parent model.

commits.title: Preserve trusted-tool context in Guardian Decisions requests (#51070)
commits.message:
Preserve trusted-tool context in Guardian Decisions requests (#51070)

## Why

The Decisions adapter rejected developer messages, including host-annotated trusted-tool context. Requests containing that context could not be classified.

## What changed

Append developer text annotated with `TrustedTool::KIND` to the classification rubric, preserving its authority while keeping user evidence in the input messages. Accept only a single text part with a single matching annotation; continue rejecting other developer messages and unsupported evidence.

## Testing

Add a regression test covering trusted-tool context alongside untrusted user text, plus rejection of incorrect roles, missing or mismatched annotations, multiple annotations or content parts, and image content.

commits.title: Install full context in compaction replacement history (#51117)
commits.message:
Install full context in compaction replacement history (#51117)

## Why

Manual, pre-turn, and post-turn compaction previously deferred rebuilding initial context until the next turn. Their saved replacement history could omit refreshed instructions and skill catalogs.

## What changed

- Install initial context during local and remote compaction, before the last real user message or summary, keeping the compaction summary last.
- Persist matching full world-state and turn-context baselines with every replacement instead of retaining only partial extension metadata.
- Build replacement context and recompute token usage for the current model even when the previous model performs compaction. Reuse that captured context for eligible current-model retries.
- Capture manual compaction context centrally and propagate preparation errors to the task runner.

## Testing

Update assertions and snapshots for context ordering, refreshed instructions, resume and fork history, current-model checkpoint baselines, and cloud skill catalog retention across compaction and resume.

commits.title: Clarify incremental tool namespace updates in Responses Lite (#51119)
commits.message:
Clarify incremental tool namespace updates in Responses Lite (#51119)

## Why

Incremental namespace declarations contain only changed or added tools. Their descriptions need to make clear that previously declared tools remain available unless explicitly marked unavailable, and that redefinitions replace earlier definitions.

## What changed

Append this guidance to updates of existing namespaces, preserving any namespace description. Leave initial declarations and catalog hashes unchanged.

## Testing

Extend unit and request-history coverage for the namespace hint, unchanged turns that append no tool definitions, and MCP tool removals that append a standalone notice without rewriting history or repeating the notice on the next turn.

commits.title: Add promise settlement streaming helpers to code mode (#51126)
commits.message:
Add promise settlement streaming helpers to code mode (#51126)

## What changed

Expose two JavaScript globals for consuming results as inputs settle:

- `as_settled(promises)` returns an async iterator of fulfilled and rejected records in settlement order, preserving queued results while the consumer is busy.
- `stream_settled(promises, emit)` delivers those records to a callback, awaiting each invocation and propagating callback errors.

Records include an `index`, a `status`, and either a `value` or a `reason`. Iterable inputs use positional indices; `Map` inputs retain their keys. Both helpers accept promises, thenables, and plain values.

## Testing

Add runtime coverage for ordering, input types, object identity, callback behavior, early iteration exit, and termination. Add stdio and gRPC host tests for partial results across waits, plus a scenario snapshot verifying fulfilled and rejected records reach the model.

commits.title: Allow Guardian Decisions to fall back to `OPENAI_API_KEY` (#51133)
commits.message:
Allow Guardian Decisions to fall back to `OPENAI_API_KEY` (#51133)

## What changed

Use `OPENAI_API_KEY` for the Guardian Decisions sampler when `CODEX_GUARDIAN_DECISIONS_API_KEY` is absent, the provider is `openai`, and no custom base URL is configured. Preserve dedicated-key precedence, including empty values, and do not fall back for other providers or custom base URLs.

## Testing

Add a credential-selection test covering fallback, dedicated-key precedence, empty dedicated keys, and provider and base URL restrictions.

commits.title: Recover Guardian reviews from parent checkpoints (#51137)
commits.message:
Recover Guardian reviews from parent checkpoints (#51137)

## Why

Reviewer compaction can invalidate previously admitted transcript evidence. When a parent checkpoint is available, restarting from that checkpoint preserves the captured parent context instead of relying on a lossy reviewer summary.

## What changed

- Restart an invalidated reviewer once from the action-time parent checkpoint, within the original review deadline.
- Preserve fresh checkpoints during startup and fit review input using the existing budget selection.
- Select transcript evidence from the checkpoint actually loaded by the reviewer. Track the transcript source so cursors remain valid across legacy-history eviction and reset when the source changes.
- Resume transcript deltas after successful recovery, including authorization added after the parent checkpoint.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for checkpoint recovery, post-checkpoint authorization, resumed deltas, and stopping after one restart. Extend history tests to cover both legacy retention and parent-checkpoint reuse, and update the checkpoint-migration snapshot.

GitOrigin-RevId: bc20fb9489afaad963303beff1c79f62fa5023f7

commits.title: Force fresh Guardian sessions for parent-checkpoint recovery (#51139)
commits.message:
Force fresh Guardian sessions for parent-checkpoint recovery (#51139)

## Why

A Guardian review restarting from the parent checkpoint must bypass cached reviewer sessions and snapshots, even when another review is using the cached session.

## What changed

- Add `ReviewerRequest::requires_fresh_session` and enable it for parent-checkpoint recovery.
- Replace an idle cached session with a fresh reusable session, or start a fresh ephemeral session when the cached session is busy. Neither recovery path inherits a cached snapshot.
- Reserve the review permit before validating a cached session and before exposing a newly spawned session to concurrent requests.

## Testing

Add tests covering recovery with idle and busy cached sessions, verifying that recovery receives no cached snapshot and that subsequent reviews reuse the appropriate session.

GitOrigin-RevId: 894f685736da54312336932aa2037e74a20629d9

commits.title: Isolate Guardian checkpoint recovery flags per review attempt (#51140)
commits.message:
Isolate Guardian checkpoint recovery flags per review attempt (#51140)

## What changed

Give the initial Guardian review and its checkpoint recovery attempt separate recovery flags instead of resetting a shared flag. Keep the single restart under the original review deadline.

Represent reviewer selection explicitly with `ReuseIfAvailable` and `FreshParentCheckpoint`, so recovery requires a fresh session and ignores reusable fork snapshots.

releaseNotes.body:
## New Features

- GPT-6.1 Sol is now the default model in the bundled and Amazon Bedrock catalogs. (#49318, #49339)
- Amazon Bedrock supports multi-agent V2 and Ultra reasoning on compatible models; Bedrock Mantle also accepts AWS GovCloud regions. (#49345, #49813)
- Sign in to MCP servers from an active terminal session with `/mcp login <name>`. (#49290)
- Choose your microphone, speaker, and microphone input channels for voice conversations, with preferences saved locally. (#49437, #49836)
- Daybreak is opt-in through `--enable cli_daybreak` or `features.cli_daybreak=true`; `daybreak=true` alone is insufficient. By default, controls and indicators are hidden, `/daybreak` is unavailable, and automatic Cyber routing is omitted—even for saved Daybreak threads. Saved preferences remain intact. Opt-in routing requires eligible ChatGPT sign-in, the OpenAI provider, and advertised model/program support. (#49856, #49858, #49859, #49861, #51207)
- Select a Cyber access program per turn with `codex exec --cyber-access-program` or the TypeScript SDK’s `cyberAccessProgram` option. The explicit exec override remains available with `cli_daybreak` disabled and leaves the saved choice unchanged. (#49939, #51207)

## Bug Fixes

- Approved filesystem escalation can now grant broader write access while preserving denied reads and network restrictions. Background tasks retain their originating turn’s permissions. (#49353, #49880)
- Explicit launch permissions survive terminal reconnects and new sessions, while implicit client settings no longer overwrite server or saved-thread web-search settings. (#49809, #49799)
- Elevated Windows terminal sessions can start using an embedded server, and sandboxed PowerShell preserves relative paths beneath protected user profiles. (#49855, #49690)
- Enter correctly submits buffered input after paste detection expires, including in Vim insert mode. (#49810)
- Thread resume includes the latest committed history. Startup detects recoverable SQLite corruption earlier and preserves damaged databases as backups. (#49599, #49701)
- Responses retries and WebSocket-to-HTTP fallback honor server retry guidance, reducing premature failures during overload. (#49441)

## Documentation

- Authentication guidance now accounts for keyring storage instead of implying credentials always reside in `auth.json`. (#49361)

## Chores

- Publishing an older alpha or hotfix no longer moves npm alpha tags backward. (#49704)

commits.message:
Honor Retry-After in WebSocket error events (#51440)

## Why

WebSocket rate-limit and overload errors ignored `Retry-After` advice and ended turns even when the server supplied a retry delay.

## What changed

Extract retry advice from nested `error.headers`, falling back to top-level `headers` when nested advice is missing or invalid. Use the shared HTTP header validation and retry-delay parser, and preserve the delay when mapping WebSocket errors.

## Testing

Add coverage for nested-header precedence, malformed headers, HTTP header validation, and recovery after an advised rate limit. Retry realtime sideband attachment while an existing call activates (#51460)

## Why

Instant Connect can return a call ID before ICE activates the call, causing sideband attachment to briefly fail with HTTP `404` while the client connects media.

## What changed

Retry `404` responses from `connect_existing_call_sideband` up to three times, waiting 100, 300, and 800 milliseconds. Return the error once this activation retry budget is exhausted, and preserve the existing handling of other errors.

Add WebSocket coverage for successful attachment after three `404` responses, failure after four `404` responses, and no retry on HTTP `410`. Verify that successful attachment does not overwrite the prepared session configuration.

commits.title: Add an optional JSON transcript format for Guardian (#51465)
commits.message:
Add an optional JSON transcript format for Guardian (#51465)

## Why

Transcript content can contain forged role headers, transcript boundaries, or claims of user approval. Guardian needs to distinguish that content from host-assigned authorship metadata.

## What changed

- Add `features.guardianv2.transcript_mode` with `line` (the default) and `json` options for synchronous review and asynchronous scoring.
- Render JSON transcript entries with host-assigned metadata and escaped `text`, and prepend matching provenance instructions to reviewer and classifier prompts.
- Preserve JSON metadata when budget recovery shortens historical text, and keep provenance instructions outside the configured classifier prompt limit.

## Testing

Add coverage for forged roles and approvals remaining within their original entries, JSON metadata surviving budget recovery, and provenance instructions surviving prompt limits. Extend review and scoring integration tests to verify JSON evidence and matching instructions.

commits.title: Add correlated, credential-free rendezvous connection diagnostics (#51483)
commits.message:
Add correlated, credential-free rendezvous connection diagnostics (#51483)

## Why

Rendezvous connection warnings report only a generic WebSocket error, while debug logs include raw error text. Structured diagnostics make failures easier to investigate without logging potentially sensitive error payloads.

## What changed

- Generate a request ID for each connection attempt, send it as `x-request-id`, and include it in the connection span and connection, disconnection, and failure logs alongside the attempt count.
- Replace raw error logging with typed error categories, I/O error kinds, HTTP status codes, and allowlisted values from `x-codex-rendezvous-rejection-reason`.
- Ignore unknown rejection reasons and response bodies.

## Testing

Add tests for rejection-header allowlisting, typed I/O failures, and a rejected WebSocket handshake that verifies the request ID header and preserves the HTTP status and known rejection reason.

commits.title: Classify executor capability root ownership independently of parsing (#51491)
commits.message:
Classify executor capability root ownership independently of parsing (#51491)

## Why

A malformed plugin manifest still marks a capability root as plugin-owned. Discovery or metadata failures must not be treated as evidence that a root is standalone.

## What changed

- Add `ExecutorPluginProvider::root_ownership` and export `PluginRootOwnership` to distinguish plugin-owned roots from standalone roots before capability parsing.
- Use discovery results when conclusive; otherwise probe manifest files at the selected root and its ancestors using the supplied filesystem sandbox. Nested plugin manifests do not establish ownership of their parent root.
- Share manifest lookup with plugin resolution and pipeline up to 256 metadata probes while preserving ancestor and manifest priority, including error ordering.

## Testing

Add tests for malformed ancestor manifests, discovery failures, ancestor versus nested ownership, concurrent probe ordering, and sandboxed metadata checks without reading manifest contents.

GitOrigin-RevId: 3512452cf1df22f52c2a2b422f96c760d98c24ac

commits.title: Remove obsolete fields from persisted turn context (#51492)

commits.title: Bind capability roots to environment selections (#51493)
commits.message:
Bind capability roots to environment selections (#51493)

## Why

Capability discovery needs the roots captured with each environment snapshot. Threads sharing an executor can select different roots, and changing environment order must preserve executor skill aliases.

## What changed

- Attach the receiving thread's capability roots when constructing `TurnEnvironmentSelection` at startup and settings updates, including roots loaded from saved history.

Add regression coverage for root ordering across environment states and configuration changes, independent root selections on a shared executor, reselection with startup or saved roots, active turn updates, and pending configuration failures reaching child and grandchild threads.

commits.title: Bound relay connection attempts and handle pongs during blocked writes (#51502)
commits.message:
Bound relay connection attempts and handle pongs during blocked writes (#51502)

## Why

A stalled rendezvous WebSocket upgrade can prevent reconnects, while short-lived connections reset reconnect backoff too early. Blocked relay writes also prevent received pongs from clearing their heartbeat deadline.

## What changed

- Bound rendezvous WebSocket connection attempts with `DEFAULT_REMOTE_EXEC_SERVER_CONNECT_TIMEOUT`.
- Retain exponential reconnect backoff across short-lived connections, resetting it only after a connection lasts at least 120 seconds.
- Process pongs during blocked data writes while preserving the in-flight send and its independent write timeout. Prefer queued pongs over an expired heartbeat deadline.
- Abort the relay writer when its owning connection task is dropped.

## Testing

Add coverage for pongs arriving during blocked writes, missing and queued pongs, independent write timeouts, and writer cancellation. Extend reconnect tests to cover stalled WebSocket upgrades without re-registration and backoff reset after a stable session.

GitOrigin-RevId: 0efa350c2b4ada9b89e23df8909063fbb69f33dc

commits.title: Expose selected environments to MCP contributors (#51503)
commits.message:
Expose selected environments to MCP contributors (#51503)

## Why

MCP contributors need the complete executor selection to distinguish an unavailable primary executor from a ready secondary. Ready capability roots alone do not preserve pending or failed selections.

## What changed

Add `with_selected_environments` and `selected_environments` to `McpServerContributionContext`, and pass the captured selections during thread MCP resolution and model-step plugin selection. Preserve priority order and pending or failed entries. Use `None` for threadless discovery and `Some(&[])` for an explicitly empty selection.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for executor ordering with pending and failed selections, environment context in model-step plugin selection, and the distinction between absent and explicitly empty selections.

GitOrigin-RevId: 2c1222fae72c7e2c75b2f40abfad3b2048cf9316

commits.title: Preserve live TUI settings when configuration reloads fail (#51510)
commits.message:
Preserve live TUI settings when configuration reloads fail (#51510)

## Why

Live preferences can be newer than the last successful configuration load. Starting a new thread after a reload failure could overwrite those preferences with stale settings.

## What changed

Carry local settings alongside the new-session configuration, retaining the live settings when reloading fails and applying the staged settings when the new thread starts. During resume and agent selection, replace staged local settings only when the directory-trust check actually reloads configuration.

## Testing

Add a regression test that changes a live rendering preference, writes invalid `config.toml`, and verifies that loading a new thread's configuration preserves the live local settings.

GitOrigin-RevId: 4ac3c70de6d627e1609cc0a5d4ba5df5a61a8b20

commits.title: Fix Windows 10 drive-letter opens for no-follow filesystem operations (#51511)
commits.message:
Fix Windows 10 drive-letter opens for no-follow filesystem operations (#51511)

## Why

On Windows 10, strict native opens can reject the DOS drive alias itself as a reparse point, preventing no-follow filesystem operations on ordinary drive-letter paths.

## What changed

Retry rejected drive-letter opens relative to a verified local volume root. Require the root to resolve to a physical disk volume directory without reparse attributes, and retain `OBJ_DONT_REPARSE` for paths beneath it so junctions remain blocked.

## Testing

Add Windows tests for file creation and reading through the volume fallback, opening the drive root, and rejecting junction traversal and creation. Validate accepted volume-root names and verify that named pipes are rejected without establishing a client connection.

GitOrigin-RevId: 51ffde4f77d2af45d18dfc4cb026d73a0e69b061

commits.title: Align Windows sandbox temp permissions with the child environment (#51512)
commits.message:
Align Windows sandbox temp permissions with the child environment (#51512)

## Why

Windows temp grants could fall back to host `TEMP`/`TMP` values and bypass read-only or denied subpaths. Sandbox permissions must match the environment passed to the child process.

## What changed

- Resolve `:tmpdir` from absolute `TEMP`/`TMP` paths in the completed workload environment, preserving access modes and missing-path rules without falling back to host values.
- Deduplicate Windows environment keys case-insensitively in a deterministic order so permission resolution and the child environment select the same value.
- Use the resolved temp policy for elevated sandbox overrides across core execution, exec-server, and direct spawning.
- Launch direct-spawn sandbox wrappers with the supplied Codex executable, materializing an inner helper only when it is that executable.

## Testing

Add Windows regression coverage for temp-only writes, read-only and denied carveouts, mixed-case and duplicate environment keys, unavailable temp paths, and empty or missing write-root overrides. Exercise core execution and direct spawning, and extend exec-server RPC coverage to the elevated backend with temp values set through the environment policy.

GitOrigin-RevId: 16b8bd4702cc434fd743a08c75a3e4515780bff3

commits.title: Expose detailed agent tree shutdown failure reports (#51515)
commits.message:
Expose detailed agent tree shutdown failure reports (#51515)

## Why

Agent tree shutdown previously returned a generic error without identifying which operation or thread failed, making cleanup failures difficult to diagnose.

## What changed

- Add `AgentTreeShutdown::wait_detailed()` and public report types while preserving the existing `wait()` result and error message.
- Record operation, optional thread ID, and either an abandoned teardown guard or a failed phase with a payload-free error category across session cleanup, child spawn cleanup, and resident eviction.
- Give each tree a correlation ID, log each failure, and retain up to 64 failures with a count of additional failures omitted. Record failures before releasing tree membership so all completed waiters observe the same report.

## Testing

Add unit coverage for aborted and completed teardown, cloned guard context, concurrent and repeated waiters, omitted failure counts, and report formatting without raw error payloads. Extend integration coverage for successful tree shutdown and persistence writer failures, including compatibility with `wait()`.

GitOrigin-RevId: 68784af28b63e875b00a55d78729f0cc5b01ac15

commits.title: Pass thread persistence intent to attachment uploads (#51517)
commits.message:

commits.title: Preserve the CLI MXC preference in executor config reads (#51525)
commits.message:
Preserve the CLI MXC preference in executor config reads (#51525)

## Why

## What changed

- Include the explicit CLI `features.prefer_mxc` value in `environmentConfig/read` as a `session-flags` layer, above project config and below legacy managed file and MDM config.
- Retain only this preference from startup overrides.
- Expose `windows_mxc_allowed_by_config` to share MXC eligibility checks after callers resolve the active permission profile.

User ripgrep configuration can suppress the file list used to construct Linux sandbox deny masks. For example, `--quiet` in `RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH` can leave files matching deny globs unmasked.

Extend the multiple-denied-files regression test with a ripgrep configuration containing `--quiet`, checking that denied files remain unreadable and unwritable while allowed files remain accessible. Skip the ripgrep-specific case when no protected `rg` executable is available.

commits.title: Enable parallel execution for read-only tools (#52245)
commits.message:
Enable parallel execution for read-only tools (#52245)

## Why

Tools that do not opt into parallel execution acquire an exclusive scheduler lock, serializing independent reads.

## What changed

Allow skill listing and reading, memory listing, reading and searching, conversation history search and reading, plugin listing, agent listing, current time, remaining context, and `get_goal` to run in parallel. Keep goal creation and updates serialized.

## Testing

Add `cloud_skill_reads_run_in_parallel`, which uses a barrier to require two cloud skill reads to overlap and verifies that each returns the expected resource contents.

commits.title: Preserve UTF-8 byte semantics in network domain matching (#52277)
commits.message:
Preserve UTF-8 byte semantics in network domain matching (#52277)

## Why

Domain wildcards need to retain the byte-based behavior of `globset`. Counting Unicode scalar values changes how `?` matches non-ASCII hosts.

## What changed

Match domain patterns against UTF-8 bytes so `?` consumes exactly one byte. For example, `api??.com` matches `apié.com`. Match hosts through borrowed byte slices, avoiding the per-match character-vector allocation.

Document ASCII case insensitivity and the absence of IDNA conversion: hosts supplied as Punycode require patterns using their Punycode spelling.

## Testing

Compare Unicode wildcard cases against `globset` for both allowlists and denylists, including multibyte characters, combining marks, Punycode, and case sensitivity. Update the exhaustive dynamic-programming comparison and retry-boundary tests to operate on bytes.

## Testing

Cover exporter selection across explicit and default analytics preferences. Update app-server and daemon telemetry tests to verify custom metrics export with analytics disabled, and worktree tests to disable metrics through the exporter setting.

commits.title: Preserve inherited context in prediction forks (#53678)
commits.message:
Preserve inherited context in prediction forks (#53678)

## Why

Prediction forks need to retain their parent's context even when it exceeds the automatic compaction threshold. Compaction or context resets can otherwise replace the history used for the prediction.

## What changed

- Apply a thread-local `AutoCompactionDisabled` policy to experimental prediction forks without changing model or skill budgets.
- Skip automatic compaction before, during, and after turns, including context-limit recovery, and suppress new token-budget reminders.
- Reject `new_context` requests for these threads and report context-limit failures without compacting their history.

## Testing

Add regression tests for legacy and paginated prediction forks across compaction thresholds, unchanged parent compaction and skill/tool inputs, context-limit failures, and rejected context resets. Add a request-history snapshot verifying inherited context and reminders survive without compaction or additional reminders after a tool call.

commits.title: Constrain API-key model access programs to server support (#53689)
commits.message:
Constrain API-key model access programs to server support (#53689)

## Why

Servers can advertise cyber access programs without accepting them for API-key accounts. The TUI must account for server support before exposing those programs.

## What changed

- Check `features.api_key_cyber_access_programs` at startup and when loading models for API-key accounts, clearing `available_access_programs` when forwarding is unavailable.
- Use thread-scoped feature settings after thread creation and honor feature requirements and CLI overrides at startup.
- Refresh account-scoped models when switching to or from API-key authentication or changing API-key thread context, clearing cached access programs while the refresh is pending.

## Testing

Extend session tests to cover enabled and disabled server settings, CLI overrides, and catalog filtering before and after thread creation. Update account-change tests to handle the model refresh.

commits.title: Account for replay caches in encrypted compaction budgets (#53691)
commits.message:
Account for replay caches in encrypted compaction budgets (#53691)

## Why

Encrypted compaction payloads can include sampled-token replay caches that increase their size roughly threefold. Budgeting them as ordinary text can reject checkpoints that fit the model context budget.

## What changed

Use a shared estimate of one token per twelve ciphertext bytes, rounded up, for encrypted `Compaction` and `ContextCompaction` items in history and Guardian context budgeting. Guardian continues to count framing and metadata separately.

Check parent compactions against the configured token budget and a separate hard wire-size limit. Preserve the complete encrypted checkpoint when it fits. The token estimate remains a heuristic and can underestimate legacy checkpoints without replay caches.

## Testing

Add coverage for token-estimate rounding, parent compaction token and wire-size limits, and reviewer continuation with a cached compaction preserved intact.

commits.title: Interrupt and drain canceled classifier responses before socket reuse (#53698)
commits.message:
Interrupt and drain canceled classifier responses before socket reuse (#53698)

## Why

Canceled classifier requests need bounded cleanup that preserves received token usage and returns only safe WebSocket connections to the pool.

## What changed

- Own classifier response streams and connection leases together, interrupting dropped responses with a one-second cleanup deadline.
- Require a matching interruption acknowledgement and response completion before reusing a canceled response's socket. Retire sockets on rejection, invalid acknowledgements, or timeout while preserving any received completion and token usage.
- Skip requests canceled before dispatch and return their unused sockets to the pool.
- Distinguish cancellation from ordinary steering, which continues draining without requiring an interruption acknowledgement.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for cancellation, acknowledgement ordering and failures, cleanup timeouts, socket reuse, and token accounting under backpressure. Extend steering tests to cover rejected and missing acknowledgements.

commits.title: Cancel Guardian V2 classifications that exceed the tool-call lag window (#53699)
commits.message:
Cancel Guardian V2 classifications that exceed the tool-call lag window (#53699)

## Why

Pending classifications can outlive the `max_tool_call_lag` window in which their scores are reusable, keeping metadata waits or classifier transports active after the result becomes stale.

## What changed

- Expire pending classifications when tool-call progress exceeds the configured lag allowance, preserving the wrapper discount while nested code-mode actions remain active.
- Cancel metadata waits and sampling in snapshot and conversation modes, including snapshot response drains after an early score.
- Treat expiry as supersession, preserving cached scores and the last completed conversation checkpoint and transcript cursor.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for lag boundaries, active wrapper discounts, transport cancellation before and after early scores, expired requests skipping preparation, and conversation history and transcript deltas surviving cancellation.

commits.title: Fix cancellation of macOS user-verification prompts (#53790)
commits.message:
Fix cancellation of macOS user-verification prompts (#53790)

## Why

Keychain signing reconstructs its own authentication context, so invalidating the caller's context does not reliably cancel the context that owns the biometric prompt.

## What changed

Evaluate the stored key's access-control policy explicitly with `LAContext` before signing. On cancellation, invalidate that context and wait for its authorization callback before releasing the lifecycle lock, rejecting any late success. Reload the key with the authorized context and disable further interaction so signing cannot open another prompt.

## Testing

Update unit tests to cover waiting for cancellation completion and rejecting completed authorization after cancellation. Add an ignored macOS hardware test and setup instructions covering persisted Secure Enclave key reuse, signature verification, cancellation, retry signing, and cleanup.

commits.title: Retain rollout migration locks across worker cancellation (#53794)
commits.message:
Retain rollout migration locks across worker cancellation (#53794)

## Why

Cancelling an async migration caller can leave its blocking compression or decompression worker running. Releasing migration locks before that worker finishes allows other writers or migrations to access files still being processed.

## What changed

Share maintenance, cross-process writer, and local writer locks with blocking workers during migration and recovery. Keep those locks held until file work completes, releasing cross-process locks before allowing local writers to proceed.

## Testing

Add a regression test for cancelled compression and decompression callers that verifies locks remain held until the worker finishes and the output is complete. Preserve the Unix check that decompression temporaries have owner-only permissions.

commits.message:

## Why

Workspace routing reported generic requirements load and reload failures, hiding the cause. Raw configuration errors can contain secrets, so exposing their messages directly is unsafe.

## What changed

Include a safe reason in configuration load and reload errors: file locations or non-file line and column numbers, cloud error categories and HTTP status codes, known network policy denials, or OS error details. Exclude raw parser messages, configuration contents, and backend-supplied policy names and IDs.

commits.title: Support daemon installation from Windows WinGet packages (#53811)
commits.message:
Support daemon installation from Windows WinGet packages (#53811)

## Why

WinGet archives place the CLI and code mode host at the package root, while daemon installation expects them under `bin/`. This layout mismatch prevents installing the daemon from a WinGet CLI package.

## What changed

Validate WinGet packages in their original layout before converting the staged copy to the daemon layout. Move the executables under `bin/`, update the package entrypoint and optional voice manifest checksum key, and hash the final tree for release reuse. Leave the source package unchanged.

## Testing

Add a Windows integration test covering daemon startup, repeated `update --from-cli --yes` calls, rewritten manifests, and rejection of an incomplete package without changing the selected release or source manifests.

items.text: 0.163.0. New Features Open /config to search preferences across categories, change supported settings immediately, and see which changes require a restart. ( #52990 , #53429 ) Send a follow-up while Codex is responding to steer it immediately. Interrupting a turn also stops active Code Mode cells and their nested tool calls. ( #51812 , #51835 ) Configure a leader key in /keymap . The default is Ctrl+X , shortcut hints stay open until you choose or cancel, and voice mute moves to F9 . ( #52273 ) Restart a managed background server from /daemon . Codex warns about work the restart could interrupt, then reconnects automatically. ( #53173 ) Codex can run independent read-only tools in parallel, including skill, memory, and conversation-history lookups. ( #52245 ) Daybreak is enabled by default for eligible accounts. codex exec can also select it with an OpenAI API key when the server offers access. ( #53701 , #53717 ) Bug Fixes Resuming a saved thread restores its permissions and network approvals, while respecting explicit overrides and current managed policy. ( #53150 , #53419 , #53424 ) The network proxy now checks permission before a DNS lookup, rejects duplicate Host headers, and prevents credential aliases from bypassing inspection hooks. ( #51650 , #52661 , #53506 ) Return to an existing side conversation with /side after switching threads. Answers to pending prompts also go back to the thread that asked. ( #52184 , #53436 ) On Windows, Ctrl+V and Shift+Insert paste text as well as images. On WSL, repeated pastes reuse the clipboard reader, and copy attempts time out instead of hanging. ( #53224 , #52967 , #53453 ) Local commands finish promptly when a child keeps an output pipe open. Remote commands preserve late-arriving output so the final poll can still collect it. ( #52652 , #53331 , #53622 ) codex exec no longer prints the same file diff again after an unrelated command. ( #53444 ) Documentation Updated the bundled OpenAI Docs guidance for migrations to the GPT-6 family, including model-specific reasoning, tool use, and data residency considerations. ( #51768 ) Clarified how the Linux sandbox uses bubblewrap for filesystem isolation and seccomp for syscall filtering. ( #52610 ) Chores Codex now uses its standard shell executor and no longer bundles a patched zsh . Configurations using the retired shell flags receive a migration notice. ( #52160 , #52213 ) Reduced Linux and macOS release package size by stripping symbols from packaged binaries while preserving them in the original build outputs. releaseNotes.body:
## New Features

- Open `/config` to search preferences across categories, change supported settings immediately, and see which changes require a restart. (#52990, #53429)
- Send a follow-up while Codex is responding to steer it immediately. Interrupting a turn also stops active Code Mode cells and their nested tool calls. (#51812, #51835)
- Configure a leader key in `/keymap`. The default is `Ctrl+X`, shortcut hints stay open until you choose or cancel, and voice mute moves to `F9`. (#52273)
- Restart a managed background server from `/daemon`. Codex warns about work the restart could interrupt, then reconnects automatically. (#53173)
- Codex can run independent read-only tools in parallel, including skill, memory, and conversation-history lookups. (#52245)
- Daybreak is enabled by default for eligible accounts. `codex exec` can also select it with an OpenAI API key when the server offers access. (#53701, #53717)

## Bug Fixes

- Resuming a saved thread restores its permissions and network approvals, while respecting explicit overrides and current managed policy. (#53150, #53419, #53424)
- The network proxy now checks permission before a DNS lookup, rejects duplicate `Host` headers, and prevents credential aliases from bypassing inspection hooks. (#51650, #52661, #53506)
- Return to an existing side conversation with `/side` after switching threads. Answers to pending prompts also go back to the thread that asked. (#52184, #53436)
- On Windows, `Ctrl+V` and `Shift+Insert` paste text as well as images. On WSL, repeated pastes reuse the clipboard reader, and copy attempts time out instead of hanging. (#53224, #52967, #53453)
- Local commands finish promptly when a child keeps an output pipe open. Remote commands preserve late-arriving output so the final poll can still collect it. (#52652, #53331, #53622)
- `codex exec` no longer prints the same file diff again after an unrelated command. (#53444)

## Documentation

- Updated the bundled OpenAI Docs guidance for migrations to the GPT-6 family, including model-specific reasoning, tool use, and data residency considerations. (#51768)
- Clarified how the Linux sandbox uses bubblewrap for filesystem isolation and seccomp for syscall filtering. (#52610)

## Chores

- Codex now uses its standard shell executor and no longer bundles a patched `zsh`. Configurations using the retired shell flags receive a migration notice. (#52160, #52213)
- Reduced Linux and macOS release package size by stripping symbols from packaged binaries while preserving them in the original build outputs. (#52178)

commits.title: Bind plugin hook approval to plugin contents (#54619)
commits.message:
Bind plugin hook approval to plugin contents (#54619)

## Why

A plugin's scripts can change without changing its hook declaration. Declaration-only approval therefore lets changed plugin code run under an existing hook approval.

## What changed

- Fingerprint plugin bundle contents and include the content hash in the approval value returned by `hooks/list`. Persist it as `trusted_content_hash`, keeping `trusted_hash` compatible with older clients.
- Verify contents before each command or MCP hook execution, within the hook's timeout, and require renewed approval when approved contents change.
- Migrate legacy declaration-only approvals to a shared, immutable content baseline per plugin and config home.
- Exclude generated Python bytecode, `.venv`, and `.egg-info` entries from fingerprints. Run app-server hook listing on blocking tasks.

## Testing

Extend integration coverage for plugin upgrades and rollbacks requiring approval, same-turn script changes preventing further hook execution, shared legacy approval baselines, and generated Python artifacts preserving trust.

GitOrigin-RevId: faaf7658210d8adb2534ddd614c72ec993920840

commits.title: Resolve stable releases dynamically for exec-server compatibility tests (#54623)
commits.message:
Resolve stable releases dynamically for exec-server compatibility tests (#54623)

## What changed

Replace fixed release pins for app-server/exec-server compatibility tests with the latest stable version and the stable release published closest to 60 days ago. Exclude drafts and prereleases, and prefer the higher version when publication dates are equally close.

Resolve release versions and SHA-256 asset digests before Linux Bazel CI runs, passing them through `CODEX_COMPAT_RELEASES` to the release archive repositories. Reuse the argument comment lint action so it also prepares compatibility releases. Add bounded retries for transient GitHub release reads.

## Testing

Add unit coverage for stable release filtering, version ordering, nearest publication dates, tie-breaking, and deduplication when both selections resolve to the same release.

GitOrigin-RevId: 5a8cf8bdabd77ab3fa89bbb711367b5d9ce8044b

commits.title: Preserve disconnect reasons in Noise handshake errors (#54637)
commits.message:
Preserve disconnect reasons in Noise handshake errors (#54637)

## Why

Noise handshake failures before connection readiness returned a generic error even when the transport had reported a specific disconnect reason. No `RpcClient` was reading the connection event channel at that point.

## What changed

Read the pending disconnect event when a Noise rendezvous handshake fails and append its reason to the handshake error when available.

## Testing

Add a regression test covering unexpected text frames and relay stream resets, checking that each produces the expected transport reason in the handshake error.

GitOrigin-RevId: 9b8ef9c8dcba75b46d51dc67784af46d4ca74b85

commits.title: Stream rollout records during thread history materialization (#54639)
commits.message:
Stream rollout records during thread history materialization (#54639)

## Why

Thread history materialization allocated a buffer for the entire unread rollout suffix before processing records, increasing memory use for large rollouts.

## What changed

Read records incrementally with a buffered reader bounded to the captured file end. Reuse the line buffer, preserve trailing partial records for the next pass, and report unexpected EOF if the rollout shrinks during reading.

## Testing

Extend the partial-line boundary test with 64 KiB of padding per record to verify byte offsets and deferred processing until the final newline is durable.

GitOrigin-RevId: c0426e3e364748b117285b248f6988a4fe064b94

commits.title: Retry npm release publishing and match macOS verification runners (#54641)
commits.message:
Retry npm release publishing and match macOS verification runners (#54641)

## What changed

- Attempt each `npm publish` up to three times, with 10- and 20-second delays and fresh OIDC credentials on each attempt. Continue skipping already-published versions.
- Enable verbose npm logging and retain debug logs as artifacts for seven days, including on failure.
- Use `macos-15-intel` to verify provisioned `x86_64-apple-darwin` packages, while keeping `aarch64-apple-darwin` verification on `macos-15-xlarge`.

GitOrigin-RevId: 1876c66993ecd8cdb44088ab17a3363d21135ec4

commits.title: Make remote-control conflict retry tests deterministic (#54647)
commits.message:
Make remote-control conflict retry tests deterministic (#54647)

## What changed

Wait for the rejected socket to close before advancing Tokio's clock through
capped retry delays. Keep socket I/O on real time so pending handshakes cannot
auto-advance their own timeouts.

Return bodyless HTTP 409 responses in the test server, check that neither
rejection restarts fast retries, and assert that recovery preserves the expected
reconnect attempt count. Both cursor and cursorless cases use the updated helper.

- Add the disabled-by-default `mcp_tool_list_changed` feature for ordinary MCP servers.

commits.title: Batch thread history materialization into SQLite (#55244)
commits.message:
Batch thread history materialization into SQLite (#55244)

## Why

History catch-up collected the entire durable rollout prefix before applying it in one SQLite transaction. Large rollouts therefore required buffering all projection steps and committing them together.

## What changed

Stream projection batches through a bounded queue and commit each batch with its checkpoint. Flush between complete records after reaching 1 MiB of source data or 256 projection steps, keeping ordinal gaps with their following records and allowing oversized records to remain intact.

Wait for batches before opening SQLite transactions so an idle reader does not hold the writer. Preserve committed progress across later failures or cancellation, allowing retries to resume from the last checkpoint.

## Testing

Add coverage for reader and writer failures under backpressure, atomic batch rollback, retries without replaying committed records, and unrelated writes while projection is paused. Verify that producer disconnection and consumer cancellation retain committed progress.

## Why

Replacing rollout files can lose Unix ownership or macOS ACLs, changing who can read or append to a transcript. An ACL can also permit appending while denying explicit timestamp updates.

## What changed

- Preserve Unix ownership, permissions, modification times, and macOS ACLs before publishing compressed or restored rollouts, and verify the replacement can be reopened.
- Abort replacement on metadata failures, reject macOS delete-deny ACLs to keep temporary files removable, and detect Unix access metadata changes through `ctime` checks.
- Use managed restoration temporary files whose names avoid stale `*.tmp` cleanup.
- Allow appending when refreshing the rollout's modification time returns `PermissionDenied`.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for macOS ACL preservation, inherited ACL removal, deletion-protected rollouts, append access despite denied timestamp changes, Unix group preservation, and restoration temporary files surviving stale-file cleanup.

## What changed

Add a federated `Auth` variant that exchanges JWT subject tokens for OpenAI access tokens using identity provider and service account IDs. Serialize concurrent exchanges, cache credentials, and renew proactively with a fresh subject token.

Validate token types, bearer credentials, payload sizes, and lifetimes. Bound caching by both relative and absolute expiry, discard cached credentials before renewal, and disable redirects for federated requests. Keep credential buffers zeroizing and diagnostics free of secrets.

commits.title: Refresh rejected proxy credentials and back off failed renewals (#55299)
commits.message:
Refresh rejected proxy credentials and back off failed renewals (#55299)

## Why

The Responses API proxy could reuse a federated credential after an upstream `401`, and concurrent requests could each retry a failed token exchange.

## What changed

- Invalidate the rejected credential so the next request obtains a fresh token. Forward the `401` without replaying the request or waiting for an ongoing renewal; leave credentials intact on `403`.
- Track rejection per token issuance so a late `401` cannot invalidate a newer credential.
- Back off failed exchanges exponentially from 1 to 30 seconds, starting when the exchange fails. Reject requests during backoff without reusing the old token, and reset the delay after a successful exchange.

## Testing

Add tests for response forwarding without replay, late and concurrent rejections, shared renewal failures, backoff timing and reset, and credential-safe renewal errors without following redirects.
