commits.message:
Add configured thread environment inheritance for subagents (#55375)

## Why

Temporary environment attachments for a parent turn should not become a
subagent's persistent environments. Children also need to retain their
configured executor bindings when their runtime is evicted and reloaded.

## What changed

- Add the disabled-by-default `subagent_thread_environments` feature flag.
  When enabled, both subagent implementations inherit configured thread
  environments captured with the invoking step, excluding turn-only attachments.
- Track configured bindings separately from active turn attachments, preserving
  pending configuration ownership and sharing completed executor startup.
- Retain configured selections and bindings across idle eviction. Reload children
  using retained bindings when the parent changes workspace, while continuing to
  validate current parent roots and permissions for matching workspaces.

## Testing

Extend regression coverage for configured, empty, forked, pending, and legacy
inheritance; temporary attachment removal across eviction; and reload behavior
with changed workspaces, deferred startup, and restricted permissions.

commits.title: Handle response body failures in OpenAI docs downloads (#55379)
commits.message:
Handle response body failures in OpenAI docs downloads (#55379)

## Why

Response body reads could outlive the manual download timeout or fail outside the existing fallback and retry handlers.

## What changed

- Read successful manual response bodies within the fetch timeout and transport fallback so stalled or failed reads fall back to `curl`. Leave `HEAD` responses unconsumed.
- Await model metadata response bodies inside the retry handler so read failures use the existing three-attempt retry loop.

## Testing

Add regression tests for manual body timeouts and truncated bodies falling back to `curl` before caching, plus model metadata body failures succeeding on retry or stopping after three attempts. All four tests pass with `node --test codex-rs/skills/tests/openai_docs_downloads.test.mjs`.

commits.title: Preserve thread metadata before rollout files are materialized (#55380)
commits.message:
Preserve thread metadata before rollout files are materialized (#55380)

## Why

A live thread can have updated SQLite metadata before its rollout file exists.
Reading metadata from the missing file loses creation details such as fork and
parent relationships and triggers unnecessary filesystem discovery and retries.

## What changed

- Read deferred `SessionMeta` through the rollout writer, ordered with persistence.
  Return no in-memory metadata once the rollout is materialized or resumed.
- Combine that creation metadata with SQLite metadata for reads that exclude
  history, and use it to determine the canonical history mode during updates.
- Keep untouched threads without a stored record unavailable for fork and resume.

## Testing

Add coverage for metadata reads and updates before persistence in both legacy and
paginated history modes, including equality with metadata read after persistence.
Verify the recorder exposes creation metadata only while deferred, and expand
fork/resume rejection tests across history modes and resume turn inclusion.

## What changed

Add a `BackendSessions` collection to own app-server sessions and poll their events fairly with cancellation-safe receives. Track listening state per backend so pausing or closing one stream leaves the others available, and resume polling after reconnect. Shut down all registered sessions on exit.

## Testing

Add coverage for polling three sessions, paused and closed stream isolation, cancellation, and session replacement after reconnect. Extend event ownership coverage to verify that background lifecycle and account events leave the displayed connection and rate-limit state untouched.

commits.title: Reject replaceable symlinks in pre-sandbox executable lookup (#55384)
commits.message:
Reject replaceable symlinks in pre-sandbox executable lookup (#55384)

## Why

A read-only executable target does not make its lookup path trustworthy: a symlink or ancestor directory may still be replaceable through writes allowed by the filesystem policy.

## What changed

Check the original lookup path, resolved parent aliases, and canonical target before selecting a pre-sandbox executable such as `bwrap`. Account for sticky directory ownership when deciding whether a child can be replaced, while preserving read-only mount carveouts.

Resolve `PATH` entries individually, including relative entries when the working directory contains a colon.

## Testing

Add regression tests for writable symlinks to read-only executables and symlinked search directories into writable roots. Extend search-path coverage to relative entries and a working directory containing a colon, and update the protected system installation test to use a direct executable path.

commits.title: Deduplicate native agent messages in Guardian review context (#55391)
commits.message:
Deduplicate native agent messages in Guardian review context (#55391)

## Why

Full-transcript fallback can select encrypted agent messages already present in the reviewer's history. These duplicates should not consume the input budget or displace new evidence.

## What changed

- Reconcile native agent messages with the effective reviewer history and earlier messages in the pending input before budgeting, including after compaction.
- Deduplicate messages with nonempty IDs while preserving messages without IDs. Allow delivery again when the prior copy is absent from the current history.
- Reject conflicting authors, recipients, or content under the same ID without modifying the pending context.

## Testing

Add coverage for duplicate admission, conflicting payloads, redelivery after history removal, and retained reviewer requests. Extend the history eviction regression to verify that full-transcript fallback reuses the reviewer and preserves a single encrypted agent message.

## Why

Cancelled or timed-out Guardian reviews can admit transcript evidence without completing a review. Reusing that session can leave subsequent reviews without the evidence they need.

## What changed

Mark interrupted reviews for rollback to the last completed review instead of reusing their live context. Preserve committed review history and replay pending evidence on the next review.

commits.title: Prefetch sibling rollout paths when reading history pages (#55396)
commits.message:
Prefetch sibling rollout paths when reading history pages (#55396)

## Why

Resolving a history page's rollout lineage performs a separate filesystem lookup for each ancestor. Ancestors stored alongside the current rollout can share a lookup traversal.

## What changed

- Prefetch paths for up to 64 sibling rollout IDs belonging to the same thread when listing history turns or items.
- Resolve candidates in the normal lookup order to preserve first-match selection for duplicate rollout IDs.
- Validate prefetched paths before use and fall back to normal lookup for missing or stale paths. Treat prefetch failures as optional and continue with normal resolution.

## Testing

Add a regression test verifying that sibling prefetch selects the same first match for a duplicate rollout ID as normal lookup.

commits.title: Record OAuth provenance and login identity for account tokens (#55397)
commits.message:
Record OAuth provenance and login identity for account tokens (#55397)

## Why

Token refresh needs the issuer and client ID used at login. Unverified token claims cannot establish that authority, and OAuth error bodies may echo credentials.

## What changed

- Save `oauth_provenance` and a new `login_owner_id` on browser and device-code login. Preserve the login identifier through token rotation.
- Refresh using the recorded issuer and client ID, retaining the existing endpoint override and fallback behavior for legacy records. Clear provenance when an override changes the endpoint or when a response without token rotation encounters a concurrently replaced refresh token.
- Keep both metadata fields optional for older records without inferring provenance from token claims.
- Remove backend token error details from structured logs and refresh error messages.
- Box large futures in token refresh, MCP initialization, and embedded app-server test startup to reduce surrounding async frame sizes.

## Testing

Add coverage for legacy record compatibility and metadata round trips, browser and device-code login persistence, refresh using recorded OAuth settings, metadata preservation through rotation, and provenance clearing for a superseded refresh token.

Defer environment disconnect notifications until recovery fails (#55401)

## Why

A temporary exec-server transport loss could emit a thread environment disconnect notification while the session was still recovering.

## What changed

- Add `EnvironmentConnectionState::Recovering` for interrupted transports and pending session recovery.
- Suppress thread lifecycle notifications during recovery, emit a connected notification after successful recovery, and report disconnection when recovery fails.
- Ignore recovery callbacks from retired clients so they cannot overwrite the connection state during refresh.

Add coverage for fast and near-deadline recovery, recovery timeout, rejected session resume, and retired-client callbacks. Extend app-server coverage to verify one lifecycle notification per selected thread and usable `environment/info` after recovery.

commits.title: Retry TUI startup after a server shutdown refusal (#55409)
commits.message:
Retry TUI startup after a server shutdown refusal (#55409)

## Why

A remote server can refuse the initial `thread/start` while shutting down. An explicit refusal establishes that no thread was created, allowing the TUI to retry without risking duplicate startup submissions.

## What changed

- Wait for the draining connection to close, reconnect within a shared two-minute deadline, and retry startup once.
- Preserve the initial prompt, confirmed draft, model, and reasoning effort across recovery. Keep drafts editable and allow cancellation of a pending submission.
- Restore input without submitting if recovery fails or startup is refused again. Continue treating a lost startup reply as uncertain and avoid automatic resubmission.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for successful reconnection with exactly one prompt submission, repeated refusal, disconnect event ordering, and draft cancellation, editing, and paste provenance during recovery.

commits.title: Track credential sources separately from auth owners (#55410)
commits.message:
Track credential sources separately from auth owners (#55410)

## Why

A new OAuth login can belong to the same account as an earlier session, while token refreshes can change credentials within one session. Auth consumers need to distinguish these cases when deciding whether a runtime can be reused.

## What changed

- Add `source_generation` to `AuthChangeState` and expose `AuthManager::auth_change_state_for` to check whether selected credentials still match the manager's current source.
- Preserve source continuity across OAuth refreshes only when session, issuer, and identity claims match. Advance the source revision for new sessions, credential replacements, and logout.
- Keep agent identity persistence from replacing cached credentials with credentials read from disk; credential publication remains managed by `AuthManager`.

## Testing

Add tests for refresh continuity, new logins, identity and workspace changes, sessionless tokens, API key replacement, logout, and identity persistence followed by an explicit credential reload.

Check daemon feature overrides and prompt for mismatch recovery (#55442)

## Why

A fixed feature allowlist excluded other boolean feature overrides from daemon use. Feature mismatches could also silently fall back to embedded mode, while automatic startup could persist enabled overrides without confirmation.

## What changed

- Allow boolean feature overrides without a fixed allowlist and compare explicit overrides with the daemon's reported settings. Ignore removed features, treat unreported features as disabled, and include only mismatches in restart settings.
- Preserve saved daemon settings during automatic startup. Prompt on feature mismatches even when embedded fallback is allowed, letting users run without the daemon, confirm a managed-daemon restart, or cancel.
- Detect managed daemons during recovery, mark available restarts as recommended, and limit the displayed feature list to three entries plus a remaining count.

## Testing

Update compatibility tests for mixed overrides, removed and unreported features, unreachable daemons, and required versus optional attachment. Update recovery snapshots and the TUI integration test to exercise explicit embedded-mode selection.

commits.message:

## Why

Polling a failed background compaction consumes the closed oneshot receiver.
Keeping that receiver in session state can cause a later await to panic instead
of falling back to foreground compaction.

## What changed

its result is still pending. Discard closed receivers so compaction can fall back
normally.

## Why

An in-flight token refresh or auth reload can outlive a login change or logout. Its result must not overwrite credentials for a different login or restore stale cached auth.

- Serialize in-process auth storage reads and writes that participate in credential updates.

- Keep account grant reads strict when the keyring is unavailable, while preserving ordinary auth fallback behavior.

  server types instead of falling back to unverified list metadata.

Add regression coverage for permission guards, queued prompts across successive
permission menus, invalidated and covered menus, model catalog propagation,
project changes on initial attachment, and name lookup across server pages with

## What changed

## Testing

Extend `brokered_shell_snapshot_fallback` coverage for disabled and failed snapshots, including managed feature settings. Verify the warning, successful execution with restored credentials, continued filesystem sandbox and network policy enforcement, and masking recovery after snapshot storage is repaired.

commits.title: Avoid redundant clones when sending app-server notifications (#55723)
commits.message:
Avoid redundant clones when sending app-server notifications (#55723)

## Why

Targeted notification delivery and broadcast routing clone the message for every recipient, then discard the original.

## What changed

Use `std::iter::repeat_n` to move the original message to the last recipient, avoiding one clone per nonempty recipient list while preserving delivery behavior.

## Testing

Expand notification tests to cover empty, single, and multiple recipient lists, checking payloads, target order, and shared timestamps. Add broadcast coverage for zero, one, and two eligible recipients, verifying that uninitialized clients, clients without the required experimental API support, and clients that opted out are skipped.

commits.message:

## Why

Sessions using the same MCP catalog can repeat schema normalization and retain duplicate tool specifications.

## What changed

Split immutable MCP tool metadata and normalized specifications from per-handler caches, and reuse matching definitions within each `McpManager`. Require matching tool metadata, agent-plugin mode, and schema budget before reuse.

Keep shared definitions behind weak references and prune expired entries on cache misses so completed sessions do not keep their schemas alive. Build definitions outside the shared index lock.

Reducing code cell lifecycle events discarded their response payload references and lost the initial response status when the runtime status changed.

## What changed

Store the initial response status and separate raw payload IDs for the initial response and final result on `CodeCell`. Carry payload references through queued lifecycle events so they survive replay when the source item arrives later.

Extend lifecycle tests to verify distinct initial and final payload IDs and the preserved initial status for yielded cells that complete and failed cells whose lifecycle events precede their source item.

Add `codex-utils-critical-path` to track shared dependency paths and attribute time to inference, automatic review, user waits, tools, overhead, and unknown work. Parallel joins retain the later-finishing branch, preserving its full history without double-counting overlapping work.

commits.title: Measure Guardian review latency once with a monotonic clock (#55846)
commits.message:
Measure Guardian review latency once with a monotonic clock (#55846)

## Why

Guardian review metrics derived duration from wall-clock timestamps, while analytics measured elapsed time when tracking the result. Clock changes and delayed tracking could produce inconsistent latencies.

## What changed

Capture one monotonic duration at review completion and pass it to both metrics and analytics. Preserve wall-clock timestamps for event ordering, and saturate analytics latency conversion at `u64::MAX`.

## Testing

Add a regression test covering skewed wall-clock timestamps and delayed tracking, verifying that the duration metric uses the captured interval and completion timestamps are preserved.

commits.message:
Bound retained turn analytics and clean up closed threads (#55847)

## Why

Dropped lifecycle facts can leave incomplete turns retaining analytics metadata indefinitely.

## What changed

- Limit retained turns to 256, evicting the oldest turn and its associated tool and review state when capacity is reached.
- Forward `ThreadClosed` notifications to analytics and discard the closed thread's turn and review state, including reviews received without turn lifecycle facts.

## Testing

Add regression tests covering metadata release after capacity eviction, continued reporting of new complete turns, cleanup isolated to the closed thread, and ignored approval responses after thread closure.

commits.title: Bound managed app-server and updater stderr logging (#55856)
commits.message:
Bound managed app-server and updater stderr logging (#55856)

## Why

Managed stderr logs previously retained a tail only before a new launch, allowing logs to grow during a long-running process. Direct stderr writes could also block lifecycle operations on disk I/O.

## What changed

- Route managed app-server and updater logs through a shared nonblocking worker with a bounded queue. Drop records when the queue is full or a record exceeds 16 KiB, and avoid waiting for the worker at shutdown.
- Prune live logs when they exceed 1 MiB, preserving the latest 256 KiB in `.log.previous` before truncating the current file. Keep inherited stderr handles usable after truncation.
- Pause predecessor pruning during Windows updater handoff and resume it after a failed handoff only when ownership has been restored.
- Keep ordinary stderr output when managed logging has not been initialized.

## Testing

Add regression tests for stalled workers and queue overflow, tail retention, inherited append and nonappend handles, and pruning exclusion during updater handoff.

commits.message:
Fix enterprise MCP credential selection and reauthentication (#55859)

## What changed

- Prefer an eligible account grant over saved enterprise credentials, with a fallback to saved enterprise sign-in during initial connection if the account grant is rejected.
- Remember rejected account grants per enterprise MCP registration across threads and report authentication failures as requiring reauthentication. Keep administrator configuration errors distinct from sign-in failures.
- Compare account grants independently of access and ID token rotation, recheck the latest identity eligibility after exchange, and retry once when the refresh grant changes.
- Make MCP authentication status reflect usable account grants, saved enterprise credentials, and completed connection failures.

## Testing

Extend regression coverage for enterprise sign-in failures and recovery, MCP authentication status, account grant identity across token refreshes, and retries after transient credential failures.

commits.title: Skip conversation scoring superseded by newer scores and history (#55913)
commits.message:
Skip conversation scoring superseded by newer scores and history (#55913)

## Why

A delayed conversation classification can reach execution after a newer request has already published a score and committed history, leaving it with no useful work to contribute.

## What changed

Pass the classification's sampling timestamp into conversation requests and check for newer scores and retained history before starting inference. Return `Superseded` only when both have advanced; keep requests that can still contribute either a score or history.

## Testing

Add regression tests covering supersession of scores and history separately and together, including a classification delayed by permissions. Verify skipped requests send no inference request and preserve cached scores, approvals, and score progress.

commits.title: Preserve thread model settings across resume and revert (#55923)
commits.message:
Preserve thread model settings across resume and revert (#55923)

## Why

Resuming a thread can replace saved model settings with global defaults. A selected service tier can also be lost when the current model does not support it.

## What changed

- Restore saved service tier, reasoning summary, and personality on resume unless the caller explicitly overrides them, respecting thread ownership of settings snapshots.
- Retain the selected service tier for persistence, settings notifications, and resume comparisons while filtering the effective tier against the current model's capabilities.
- Carry the runtime model, service tier, and personality into thread revert reconstruction.
- Persist initial thread settings before user input during MCP startup so an interrupted first turn retains its settings checkpoint.

## Testing

Extend regression coverage for cold resume and explicit overrides, unsupported service tiers, settings preservation during revert, and settings checkpoints before user input when MCP startup is interrupted.

commits.title: Add local diagnostic ZIP exports to the app server (#55940)
commits.message:
Add local diagnostic ZIP exports to the app server (#55940)

## What changed

Add a save RPC that accepts the existing report options and an absolute `savePath` on the server host. Save the report, selected attachments, and a manifest without uploading, and return `savedPath`, `threadId`, and `promptHash`. Local exports remain available when uploads are disabled by configuration.

Publish archives atomically without replacing existing files. Bound uncompressed contents to 200 MiB and attachments to 128, preserve duplicate attachment names safely, and fail without publishing a partial ZIP when a selected file cannot be read. Honor `includeLogs` and omit automatic rollouts for untouched threads without materializing them.

Update protocol schemas and generated TypeScript and Python types.

## Testing

Add coverage for local-only saves, disabled uploads, path validation, overwrite protection, log consent, archive budgets, duplicate names, missing files, and rollout selection before materialization and after writer shutdown.

commits.title: Bound remote installed-plugin inventory pagination (#55946)
commits.message:
Bound remote installed-plugin inventory pagination (#55946)

## Why

Installed-plugin inventory fetches could keep following pagination cursors
without an overall bound, delaying release of the plugin mutation gate.

## What changed

- Limit each inventory fetch to 60 seconds and 100 pages, and reject repeated
  pagination cursors.
- Request 200 items per page for scoped inventory fetches as well as all-scope
  fetches.
- Report overall fetch timeouts as `remote_catalog_timeout`.

## Testing

Add coverage for cursor cycles, completion at the page limit, and overall
timeout cancellation after successful pages. Verify that failed pagination
preserves the cached inventory and plugin files and releases the mutation gate.

commits.title: Refresh cloud plugin and skill catalogs after mid-turn auth changes (#55957)
commits.message:
Refresh cloud plugin and skill catalogs after mid-turn auth changes (#55957)

## Why

Authentication can change between model steps. Refresh cloud catalogs before the next step so plugin acceptance and skill instructions reflect the current auth scope, including plugins that are no longer available.

## What changed

- Add a `refresh_catalog_for_step` lifecycle hook and rebuild MCP when plugin catalogs change.
- Reuse successful discovery within a turn and auth scope, serialize concurrent refreshes, and allow retries after failures or cancellation. Limit cloud skill discovery warnings to once per turn.
- Skip cloud discovery during prewarm and other context-only captures, and check hosted plugins even when no executor roots are selected.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for mid-turn auth rotation and plugin removal, serialized refreshes and retries, stale discovery results, and prewarm boundaries.

commits.title: Preserve provider model catalogs when refreshes fail (#55958)
commits.message:
Preserve provider model catalogs when refreshes fail (#55958)

## Why

A failed provider catalog refresh could discard model metadata and disable tool search on subsequent turns, even after a successful discovery.

## What changed

Keep the last successful catalog, ETag, and original freshness when refreshes fail without an access rejection. Continue invalidating cached catalogs for HTTP `401`/`403`, rejected refresh tokens, and gateway credentials that require login. Distinguish `GatewayLoginRequired` from login in progress so only the former invalidates the catalog.

Successful empty responses remain authoritative, and cached catalogs remain scoped to the provider and authentication identity.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for catalog preservation across refresh errors and restarts, access rejection invalidation, identity isolation, and tool search and instruction stability on the next turn after a failed refresh.

commits.message:
Add managed Desktop workspace storage requirements (#55965)

## What changed

- Add `application.storage.default_project_parent` and `application.storage.projectless_workspace_root` requirements for new Desktop workspaces. Require absolute paths and reject unknown storage keys.
- Apply managed paths to `desktop.defaultProjectParent` and `desktop.projectlessWorkspaceRoot`, overriding local preferences and rejecting writes to managed settings or their containing table while preserving unrelated Desktop settings.
- Expose storage requirements through `config/requirements/read` and update generated JSON schemas, TypeScript types, and Python models.

Add coverage for storage validation, per-setting layer precedence, config overrides, write protection, and requirements API responses. Adjust daemon shutdown test deadlines and TUI test synchronization, paste handling, and future allocation.

commits.title: Back off failed cloud skill and plugin catalog refreshes (#55968)
commits.message:
Back off failed cloud skill and plugin catalog refreshes (#55968)

## Why

Failed cloud discovery previously retried before each model step. Apply a cooldown across steps and turns to avoid repeated discovery requests while a provider remains unavailable.

## What changed

- Share per-thread retry backoff logic between cloud skill and plugin catalogs, starting at 30 seconds and doubling to a maximum of 5 minutes.
- Scope cooldowns to authentication and MCP resource generations so account changes and reconnects permit immediate recovery.
- Clear backoff after successful discovery or configuration resets, while allowing cancelled refreshes to retry immediately.

## Testing

Update lifecycle and concurrency tests to cover shared cooldowns, reconnect recovery, and cancellation. Use paused time to verify exponential delays, the 5-minute cap, and backoff across turns.

commits.title: Drain WebSocket responses on mailbox preemption (#55969)
commits.message:
Drain WebSocket responses on mailbox preemption (#55969)

## Why

Mailbox preemption can discard completed response items and lose the response ID needed for incremental continuation. Buffered tool calls must also wait for queued agent messages to be read.

## What changed

- Gracefully interrupt and drain Responses Lite streams, retaining completed items and the response ID for the next request.
- Cancel buffered tool calls before dispatch and suppress partial items that may be discarded during the drain.
- Keep user steering queued until draining finishes. Include pending mail in follow-up requests after disconnects and preserve content-filter recovery guidance.

## Testing

Add WebSocket regression coverage for buffered completion, interrupts without acknowledgement, buffered tools and partial items, user steering during draining, disconnects, and content-filter recovery.

Add storage namespaces for local message boards (#55971)

## Why

Local message boards use a fixed database filename. Callers need separate storage for boards that share a session identity.

## What changed

- Add `LocalBoardOptions` with a validated `storage_namespace`, and support it when opening, configuring, and permanently deleting boards.
- Allow `LocalBoard::with_options` to select storage for its connections.

commits.message:
Allow consumers to select message-board tools (#55973)

## Why

`message_board_tools` always exposed all nine discussion tools. Consumers need a way to expose a subset, such as `read_thread` and `list_threads`, over the same board.

## What changed

Accept an ordered slice of the new `MessageBoardTool` enum and optional description overrides in `message_board_tools`. Use the enum for schemas and dispatch, and keep the agent extension's existing tool set and order through `MessageBoardTool::DISCUSSION`.

commits.title: Add an experimental command to migrate NFS databases to DELETE mode (#55975)
commits.message:
Add an experimental command to migrate NFS databases to DELETE mode (#55975)

## What changed

Add `codex migrate-nfs-db` to replace configured SQLite WAL databases in place with validated copies in `DELETE` journal mode, retaining the originals and their sidecar files in backup directories. Stage conversion locally, check database integrity before installation, and support resuming an interrupted replacement.

Require confirmation and exclusive access, with all Codex instances stopped on every host until migration succeeds. The NFS mount must support cross-client POSIX locks. Reject unsupported file permissions and ACLs, and serialize migrations with a migration lock.

Support configuration overrides, `--profile`, and `--staging-dir`. Skip the logs database when `log_dir` is explicitly configured and leave databases already in `DELETE` mode unchanged. Reject remote mode.

commits.title: Route SQLite logs to an explicitly configured `log_dir` (#55978)
commits.message:
Route SQLite logs to an explicitly configured `log_dir` (#55978)

## What changed

- Store `logs_2.sqlite` in `log_dir` when explicitly configured, unless a managed `sqlite_home` requirement applies. Keep other databases in `sqlite_home` and preserve the existing SQLite log location when `log_dir` is unset.
- Initialize and lock the selected log directory only when opening its database, so an unavailable directory does not prevent authentication commands from loading configuration. Share the cleanup lock across configuration clones and allow failed initialization to be retried.
- Leave existing logs in place. Read legacy logs for diagnostic submissions when the current query returns no logs, attaching them as `codex-logs-legacy.log`. Continue retention cleanup and page reclamation for both locations, with independent maintenance locks and filesystem checks.

Add coverage for configuration routing and managed requirements, deferred initialization and lock lifetimes, authentication with an unavailable log directory, legacy log attachments, and cleanup of current and legacy databases.

commits.title: Refresh remote exec-server credentials after unauthorized responses (#55987)
commits.message:
Refresh remote exec-server credentials after unauthorized responses (#55987)

## Why

Remote registry requests need to recover when credentials are rejected or rotated while `exec-server` is running. Concurrent requests should reuse refreshed credentials rather than refresh the replacement token again.

## What changed

- Add an `AuthProvider` recovery hook and retry registry registration, connection, and harness-key validation once after a `401` when the provider supplies replacement credentials.
- Use live ChatGPT authentication for remote `exec-server` and guard proactive and unauthorized refreshes so concurrent callers share the completed refresh.
- Allow executor credentials to retry when the parent has already supplied a valid replacement.
- Keep connection authentication, refresh, and retry within the original connection deadline.

## Testing

Add coverage for concurrent refreshes, stored and parent-supplied credential rotation, refresh failures, retry limits, and connection deadlines, plus a CLI integration test for refresh and credential reload in a running executor.

commits.title: Avoid double-counting retained reasoning in token usage (#55991)
commits.message:
Avoid double-counting retained reasoning in token usage (#55991)

## Why

Responses Lite includes retained reasoning in its reported token usage even without an `X-Reasoning-Included` header. Adding a separate reasoning estimate can trigger automatic compaction prematurely. Locally recomputed usage also already includes retained reasoning.

## What changed

Initialize reasoning accounting from `use_responses_lite` before each sampling or compaction request, while allowing server events to override it. Mark locally recomputed token usage as including reasoning.

## Testing

Update the compaction regression test to verify that Responses Lite usage without the header stays below an 81-token limit at 80 tokens and triggers compaction at 81 tokens.

commits.title: Preserve per-execution trace context in code-mode stdio callbacks (#55993)
commits.message:
Preserve per-execution trace context in code-mode stdio callbacks (#55993)

## Why

Callbacks from the shared stdio host need to retain each execution's trace context after it yields, without keeping the execution span open until its background cell closes.

## What changed

Capture a W3C trace-context snapshot for each execution and restore it as the parent of tool callback and notification spans. Instrument delegate invocation and its returned future so the context is available on entry and across awaits.

## Testing

Add an integration test with overlapping yielded cells completed in reverse order. Cover sampled, unsampled, and untraced callers, trace isolation, callback and notification parentage, and execution spans finishing while callbacks remain blocked.

commits.title: Add a Windows proxy authentication tunnel helper (#55994)
commits.message:
Add a Windows proxy authentication tunnel helper (#55994)

## What changed

Expose `connect_windows_proxy` for callers handling a CONNECT `407` response. Use libcurl with the signed-in Windows user's Negotiate or NTLM credentials, then return the authenticated connection with buffered data preserved.

Support HTTP and HTTPS proxies, with default or caller-provided TLS configuration. HTTPS proxies requiring authentication tokens bound to their TLS connection are unsupported.

commits.title: Retry proxy CONNECT challenges with Windows authentication (#56000)
commits.message:
Retry proxy CONNECT challenges with Windows authentication (#56000)

## Why

HTTPS requests and WebSocket connections on Windows need to authenticate when a proxy rejects `CONNECT` with status `407`.

## What changed

- Retry proxy challenges through the existing Windows authentication helper, using the signed-in user's Negotiate or NTLM credentials. Treat an origin `407` as a normal HTTP response.
- Bridge authenticated tunnels to the HTTP client through destination-specific named pipes, retaining redirect checks and TLS backend fallback without caching those tunnels across destinations.
- Carry explicit CA certificates and client identities into HTTPS proxy TLS configuration, and apply the configured connect timeout when opening authenticated HTTP tunnels.

commits.title: Support confidential OAuth clients for enterprise-managed MCP auth (#56001)
commits.message:
Support confidential OAuth clients for enterprise-managed MCP auth (#56001)

## Why

Enterprise-managed MCP authentication previously required public OAuth clients at both the identity provider and the MCP authorization server, preventing use of registrations that require client secrets.

## What changed

- Accept separate `client_secret` and `token_endpoint_auth_method` settings for the enterprise IdP and MCP server OAuth registration. Support `client_secret_basic` and `client_secret_post`, defaulting to Basic when a secret is configured.
- Validate the registered method against server metadata and use it for enterprise login and both ID-JAG exchanges.
- Require a configured `oauth.authorization_server_issuer` for confidential MCP registrations and reject empty secrets or authentication methods without secrets.
- Require the account OAuth client to match the configured IdP client before reusing an account grant with a provisioned secret; otherwise use dedicated enterprise login.

## Testing

Extend configuration, login, exchange, and app-server lifecycle tests to cover confidential registrations, separate IdP and resource credentials, authentication method validation, and exclusion of client secrets from authorization URLs, stored login grants, and logs.

commits.title: Scope MITM credential substitution to trusted origins and placeholders (#56003)
commits.message:
Scope MITM credential substitution to trusted origins and placeholders (#56003)

## Why

Credential substitution needs to authorize the destination and the original request before exposing host secrets. Project configuration must not redirect trusted credential policies, and older clients must reject scoped policies rather than silently apply unconditional injection.

## What changed

- Add hook `schemes` and `ports` constraints and an exact whole-header `placeholder` for secret substitution. Require `network.mitm.version = 2` for these options in permission profiles.
- Restrict placeholder substitution to HTTPS on port 443 and reject missing, mismatched, or duplicate placeholder headers.
- Reject project changes to trusted MITM definitions and their inheritance chains. Allow self-contained project header-stripping policies only when no trusted MITM policy exists.
- Reject ambiguous query values, value-constrained headers, and semicolon paths during authorization, and preserve case-sensitive extension methods.
- Mark resolved secret headers sensitive, reject secret injection into `User-Agent`, restrict substitution headers, and limit secret files to 64 KiB.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for scoped TOML resolution, legacy-format rejection, unknown fields, project policy restrictions, origin and placeholder denials, ambiguous request matching, secret redaction, and hook application after credential brokerage.

commits.title: Assert shell tool overlap directly in the parallelism test (#56006)
commits.message:
Assert shell tool overlap directly in the parallelism test (#56006)

## Why

A total-duration assertion does not prove that two shell commands overlap and depends on execution speed.

## What changed

Update `shell_tools_run_in_parallel` to wait for both commands to create start markers before releasing them through a shared file. Fail if both commands do not start within five seconds, and verify that each command exits successfully and returns its expected output.

Pause the Tokio clock before spawning the review in

commits.title: Add a critical-path timing recorder for direct tool calls (#56008)
commits.message:
Add a critical-path timing recorder for direct tool calls (#56008)

## What changed

Add the `codex-direct-tool-timing` crate to record tool execution, automated reviews, human waits, and dependency paths. Human waits take precedence over overlapping reviews, and dependency waits with unavailable history are recorded as unknown time.

Invocation guards complete each call once, explicitly or on drop. Separate invocation identities prevent late review or wait guards from affecting calls that reuse an ID; duplicate active IDs disable ambiguous path attribution. Batch timing exposes the last-finishing invocation's path once all calls complete.

## Testing

Add unit tests for parallel batch completion, duplicate and reused call IDs, cancellation, missing dependency history, overlapping reviews and human waits, and nested wait guards.

commits.title: Keep rollout trace terminal sessions distinct when process IDs are reused (#56011)
commits.message:
Keep rollout trace terminal sessions distinct when process IDs are reused (#56011)

## Why

Runtime process handles are recyclable and thread-local. Using them as terminal session identities can merge separate commands or associate `write_stdin` operations with the wrong exec.

## What changed

- Give each exec a distinct terminal session and track the latest session for each thread-local process handle.
- Record the exec selected by `write_stdin` at runtime and use it to correct session membership during replay, including when dispatch is delayed until a handle is reused.
- Fall back to the latest session for the thread and handle when replaying older traces without runtime target events.

## Testing

Extend reducer coverage for process ID reuse across threads and successive execs, stdin session membership, and delayed runtime target resolution.

commits.message:
Avoid nested CLI startup in the MCP OAuth persistence test (#56018)

Use `ConfigEditsBuilder` to persist a concurrent MCP server edit during OAuth discovery without launching another CLI process inside the HTTP timeout. Preserve coverage that the concurrent server and issuer-bound callback are saved, and assert that OAuth fails with the expected invalid authorization endpoint error.

commits.title: Allow thread sampling after failed or interrupted turns (#56020)
commits.message:
Allow thread sampling after failed or interrupted turns (#56020)

## Why

`thread/sample` previously required the latest source turn to have completed successfully, rejecting failed or interrupted turns even when the source was idle.

## What changed

Accept the latest completed, failed, or interrupted turn in both legacy and paginated history modes. Update the protocol documentation and validation error to reflect the accepted statuses, while continuing to reject stale or active sources.

## Testing

Expand integration coverage across all three terminal statuses and both history modes, checking that sampling preserves context and leaves the source unchanged. Also verify that sampling an active source is rejected before interrupting it.

commits.message:
Keep slash command prefixes in editable composer text (#56021)

## What changed

Keep the leading `/` in the textarea and render slash commands after the normal composer prompt, so `/model` appears as `› /model`.

Track the full `/command` token as a text element and remove stale slash-command elements when the draft changes. Update composer tests and snapshots for the new representation.

commits.title: Preserve config overrides across CLI subcommand boundaries (#56022)
commits.message:
Preserve config overrides across CLI subcommand boundaries (#56022)

## Why

When `-c` or `--config` appears at multiple command levels, Clap retains only the deepest scope's values, dropping earlier overrides.

## What changed

Collect config overrides from each command scope in order while preserving typed child arguments and their existing precedence. Arguments forwarded after `--` remain unchanged.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for overrides split across nested `mcp add` commands, forwarded `-c` arguments, and validation of an invalid override before `app-server` when another override follows it.

commits.message:
Group Bedrock API key entry with other AWS sign-in methods (#56023)

When AWS profiles or environment credentials are detected, move manual Bedrock API key entry under “Other AWS sign-in methods” and update its description to include API keys. Keep API key entry directly available when no credentials are detected.

Update onboarding method assertions and rendering snapshots to cover the grouped options and API key entry in the other sign-in methods menu.

commits.title: Limit decoded HTTP/3 response headers in the TCP tunnel (#56024)
commits.message:
Limit decoded HTTP/3 response headers in the TCP tunnel (#56024)

## Why

QPACK can expand compact response headers into large decoded field sections. Bound their size before `h3` constructs its capacity-limited `HeaderMap`.

## What changed

Set the HTTP/3 client's maximum field section size to 64 KiB so oversized responses are rejected with `HeaderTooBig`.

## Testing

Add a regression test that sends QPACK static references around the size limit and a much larger expansion. Verify that oversized responses are rejected and a subsequent valid response succeeds on the same connection.

commits.message:
Support client Responses API metadata in `thread/sample` (#56031)

## What changed

Add optional `responsesapiClientMetadata` to `ThreadSampleParams` and forward it to the sample turn's Responses API metadata. Update the experimental protocol schema.

## Testing

Extend the thread sample integration test to verify that client metadata appears in both the request header and body, preserves the explicit `turn_trigger` when client metadata supplies a conflicting value, and does not carry over to the next parent turn.

commits.title: Fix entrypoint lookup in package debug-symbol smoke tests (#56032)
commits.message:
Fix entrypoint lookup in package debug-symbol smoke tests (#56032)

## Why

Rust v0 symbols can mention `codex_code_mode_host` as the instantiating crate of a dependency's generic function, so matching the crate name alone can select the wrong function.

## What changed

Demangle `nm` output and match `codex_code_mode_host::main` exactly, preserving spaces within demangled names. Include local symbols in the Linux lookup by removing `--extern-only`.

commits.message:
Enable the Bedrock setup wizard by default (#56033)

## What changed

Promote `bedrock_setup_wizard` to stable and enable it by default for eligible onboarding. Users can still disable it with `features.bedrock_setup_wizard = false`.

## Testing

Update onboarding coverage to check the enabled default and explicit opt-out. Remove the explicit opt-in from daemon startup tests so they exercise the default configuration.

commits.title: Add request-scoped OAuth credentials and session lifecycle APIs (#56036)
commits.message:
Add request-scoped OAuth credentials and session lifecycle APIs (#56036)

## What changed

- Add `OAuthSessionRequest` to pair access tokens with their authorization identity and retain rejected-token recovery across transient failures and retries. New sign-ins receive an identity that survives token refresh.
- Expose explicit login, logout, and authorization identity lookup, plus a per-manager option to disable automatic browser login while allowing credential reuse and refresh.
- Move serializable `OAuthSessionConfig` into `codex-model-provider-info`, add an optional `device_authorization_url` field, and share endpoint URL validation through `codex-http-client`.
- Distinguish permission failures, transient token endpoint failures, and invalid responses using `io::ErrorKind`.

## Testing

Add coverage for sign-in identity preservation through refresh retries, removal of saved and cached credentials on logout, and suppression of automatic browser login. Extend token endpoint error classification coverage.

GitOrigin-RevId: ae9f72e787171e179fe139a3b840a9f7e1e46506

commits.title: Add a channel-backed cloud app-server client (#56037)
commits.message:
Add a channel-backed cloud app-server client (#56037)

## What changed

- Add `CloudClient` and integrate it with `AppServerClient` and `AppServerRequestHandle` for requests, notifications, server-request replies, events, and shutdown.
- Keep retained request and reply handles bound to their cloud backend, with event delivery independent of request completion and a timeout for shutdown.
- Return no platform or Codex home metadata for cloud clients, and reject TUI filesystem operations for this backend.

## Testing

Add tests for backend ownership of retained handles, independent event delivery, errors after the command receiver closes, and shutdown timeouts when the worker does not respond.

GitOrigin-RevId: 4cf308dc0ea6fa6e7b14dd4542d93e8030b0162d

commits.title: Enable executor cleanup hooks with V2 capability discovery (#56044)
commits.message:
Enable executor cleanup hooks with V2 capability discovery (#56044)

## Why

Executor hooks depended on V1 discovery snapshots, so plugins discovered through V2 could not run their cleanup hooks.

## What changed

Prepare executor hook sources during step setup from either V1 or V2 discovery and capture them in `StepContext` for stop, interrupt, and memory consolidation hooks. Restrict V2 sources to selected plugin installations while preserving plugin enablement, hook admission, MCP routing, and app tool policy checks.

## Testing

Add unit coverage for V2 hook admission, environment routing, disabled plugins, and failed discovery. Add integration coverage showing that `Stop` and `Interrupt` cleanup hooks run with V2 discovery alone and remain silent when the plugin is disabled.

GitOrigin-RevId: a4c0e9c56bdebcdf22cea63f02f8fb4c5eed358e

commits.title: Support configured credential providers in remote execution (#56049)
commits.message:
Support configured credential providers in remote execution (#56049)

## Why

Remote credential masking previously fell back to unmasked execution whenever custom credential providers were configured.

## What changed

- Transport configured provider rules to the executor-local network proxy, where credential values and destination context are resolved.
- Advertise `credentialMaskingCustomProviders` and negotiate masking support. Keep the warning and unmasked fallback for executors that support only built-in providers.
- Discard provider rules when masking is disabled and omit their contents from debug output.

## Testing

Extend coverage for capability compatibility, provider configuration round trips, and fallback on older executors. Exercise configured-provider masking in remote request history and verify that masked placeholders are restored to real credentials in upstream request headers.

GitOrigin-RevId: b036f56900b343ddccc17b5293c82bc1f3426237

commits.title: Require managed configuration from the configured server (#56055)
commits.message:
Require managed configuration from the configured server (#56055)

## Why

Local administrators need to require managed configuration from a specific customer-hosted server before a session can start.

## What changed

- Add a local managed `config_server` requirement with an HTTPS base URL and optional OAuth settings. Validate endpoints and derive the bundle route as `codex/config/bundle` beneath the base URL.
- Replace the entire `config_server` block when a higher-priority requirements layer supplies one, keeping the endpoint and OAuth settings together. Reject this setting in fetched policy.
- Track the applied server through configuration snapshots, role overrides, and refreshes. Reject session startup and managed refreshes when the applied server does not match the requirement; user refreshes retain the session's managed configuration.

## Testing

Add coverage for missing, mismatched, and matching server configuration at session startup, whole-block replacement, rejection of server settings in fetched policy, and preservation across role overrides and refreshes.

commits.title: Cache decrypted Codex auth and managed secrets (#56081)
commits.message:
Cache decrypted Codex auth and managed secrets (#56081)

## Why

Repeated reads of Codex auth and managed secrets repeat expensive scrypt decryption even when the encrypted file and keyring passphrase are unchanged.

## What changed

Extend the decrypted snapshot cache to `CodexAuth` and `ManagedSecrets`, keeping at most one snapshot per namespace. Reuse snapshots only when the file path, ciphertext, and passphrase match, and invalidate matching snapshots on writes. Every read still checks the file and keyring before reusing plaintext.

## Testing

Extend cache tests to cover concurrent reuse, writes, external file replacement, file removal, key rotation, keyring errors, invalid ciphertext, and isolation across homes and namespaces. Prime the auth cache before verifying fallback when the keyring fails.

commits.title: Honor server approval reviewer defaults on fresh TUI startup (#56090)
commits.message:
Honor server approval reviewer defaults on fresh TUI startup (#56090)

## Why

A saved client `approvals_reviewer` setting could override the app server's default when starting a fresh thread.

## What changed

Use explicit invocation overrides for the first thread's approval reviewer, leaving the selection to the server when no override is provided. Typed overrides take precedence over key-value overrides, and repeated key-value overrides use the last value. Explicit profile launches retain their resolved configuration behavior.

## Testing

Extend startup tests to cover server defaults, embedded startup, explicit override precedence, and profile launches. Verify that the first turn uses the reviewer returned by the server.

commits.title: Keep TUI preferences editable when execution settings are invalid (#56091)
commits.message:
Keep TUI preferences editable when execution settings are invalid (#56091)

## Why

Saving a local preference could succeed but fail to apply live because reloading the full configuration also resolved execution settings. An unknown `model_provider`, for example, prevented the preference from taking effect.

## What changed

Reload config-panel preferences from the configuration layer stack into `LocalSettings` without rebuilding execution settings. Preserve CLI overrides, loader overrides, cloud configuration, and the existing choice of working directory.

## Testing

Extend the offline remote-session preference test with an unknown `model_provider` override, verifying that automatic recap and paste detection preferences still persist and apply live.

commits.title: Prepare TUI startup to accept multiple backend sessions (#56097)
commits.message:
Prepare TUI startup to accept multiple backend sessions (#56097)

## What changed

- Add `InitialBackendSessions` to carry the initial session and additional sessions into the TUI event loop. Existing launches continue to supply a single session.
- Shut down all supplied sessions on startup errors, cancellation, and early exits.
- Register the under-development `tui_multi_backend` feature flag, disabled by default, and expose it in the configuration schema.

## Testing

Add a regression test that fails bootstrap and verifies that both initial backends receive shutdown requests. Update multi-source event polling coverage to use the new initialization path.

commits.title: Forward Guardian reviewer events to parent raw-event subscribers (#56124)
commits.message:
Forward Guardian reviewer events to parent raw-event subscribers (#56124)

## What changed

Add the disabled-by-default `guardian_recorded_items` feature to forward recorded reviewer items and interruptions through the parent's raw-event subscription, preserving reviewer thread and turn IDs without modifying the parent's history or completing its turn.

Emit reviewer items as `rawResponseItem/completed` notifications and interruptions as interrupted `turn/completed` notifications. Mark opted-in reviewer requests with `guardian_recorded_items` metadata.

## Testing

Extend Guardian integration tests to cover reviewer identity, recorded-item metadata replay, concurrent reviewer interruptions, independent parent completion, and behavior without the feature enabled.

commits.title: Avoid blocking EMA auth status checks on account refresh (#56127)
commits.message:
Avoid blocking EMA auth status checks on account refresh (#56127)

## Why

EMA MCP auth status checks acquired an account grant lease, making status inspection wait for account refresh coordination or an existing lease.

## What changed

Add `AuthManager::account_oauth_grant()` to inspect an owner-checked grant without acquiring the refresh lock. Use it for EMA status checks and share a single lazy read across servers, including missing grants and read errors. Keep refresh exclusion for token exchanges through `lease_account_oauth_grant()`.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for status checks across two EMA servers while an account lease is held. Extend account refresh tests to verify inspection completes with a lease held and refresh queued, and returns no grant after logout.

commits.title: Cancel MCP tool requests when response futures are dropped (#56132)
commits.message:
Cancel MCP tool requests when response futures are dropped (#56132)

## Why

Dropping a local tool-call future did not notify the MCP server that the request was cancelled, leaving remote work running.

## What changed

- Send a cancellation notification for the request when its response future is dropped, covering both ordinary tool calls and tool-input rounds.
- Preserve write order for stdio and in-process transports so cancellation cannot arrive before its tool request, without waiting for tool responses.

## Testing

Add regression tests for cancellation on drop, request-before-cancellation ordering under reversed send polling and exhausted task budgets, and continued use of the shared connection after cancellation.

commits.title: Defer agent mail after empty final answers (#56133)
commits.message:
Defer agent mail after empty final answers (#56133)

## Why

An explicit `final_answer` with empty or whitespace-only text could allow queued agent mail to restart the turn instead of leaving it queued for the next turn.

## What changed

Treat explicit `final_answer` messages as terminal regardless of visible text in both completed-item handling and turn-item finalization. Untagged messages still require visible text to defer mailbox delivery; `commentary` and `partial_answer` messages do not defer it.

## Testing

Extend regression coverage for empty and whitespace-only final answers, delivery of queued agent mail on the next turn, and message board notifications arriving before or after an empty final answer.

releaseNotes.body:
## New Features

- Save reusable prompts and slash commands in ten numbered `/presets` slots, with a keyboard menu for quick access. (#54380, #54381)
- Set model, reasoning effort, speed, and permission profiles directly with inline `/model` and `/permissions` arguments. (#54378, #54383)
- Preview viewed and generated images in the fullscreen transcript on terminals supporting Kitty or Sixel graphics. (#54216)
- Authenticate enterprise MCP connections using eligible Codex account grants or dedicated sign-in, including OAuth clients requiring secrets. (#55334, #55859, #56001)
- Mask credentials during supported remote Bash commands and Zsh snapshot sessions, including credentials from custom providers. (#54309, #54432, #56049)
- The Amazon Bedrock setup wizard is now enabled by default, with API key entry grouped alongside other AWS sign-in methods when credentials are detected. (#56033, #56023)

## Bug Fixes

- Failed compaction no longer leaves partial summaries in conversation history, and background compaction failures fall back without panicking. (#53932, #55581)
- Resuming sessions now finds compressed histories and restores saved thread settings instead of replacing them with global defaults. (#54008, #55923)
- Windows HTTPS and WebSocket connections now handle proxy authentication challenges using the signed-in user’s Negotiate or NTLM credentials. (#55994, #56000)
- CLI configuration overrides are preserved when `-c` or `--config` appears at multiple subcommand levels. (#56022)
- Queued prompts now wait for pending permission selections to resolve before continuing. (#55682)
- Hardened sandbox checks for case-variant metadata paths on macOS and replaceable symlinks used to locate executables. (#54273, #55384)

## Chores

- Reduced disk usage by pruning unused installations, cleaning abandoned marketplace checkouts, and bounding daemon logs. (#53827, #55149, #55689, #55690, #55856)
- Updated the embedded JavaScript runtime with safety checks for optimized `Array.sort` operations. (#54519)

## Changelog

Full Changelog: https://github.com/openai/codex/compare/rust-v0.163.0...rust-v0.164.0

- #53725 Render Markdown web links as labels in Rex @bc-openai
- #53728 Preserve the remote cwd filter in the in-app resume picker @fcoury-oai
- #53732 Reuse compiled search patterns across compressed rollouts @ethernetdan-openai

commits.title: Cache decrypted Codex auth and managed secrets (#56081)
commits.message:
Cache decrypted Codex auth and managed secrets (#56081)

## Why

Repeated reads of Codex auth and managed secrets repeat expensive scrypt decryption even when the encrypted file and keyring passphrase are unchanged.

## What changed

Extend the decrypted snapshot cache to `CodexAuth` and `ManagedSecrets`, keeping at most one snapshot per namespace. Reuse snapshots only when the file path, ciphertext, and passphrase match, and invalidate matching snapshots on writes. Every read still checks the file and keyring before reusing plaintext.

## Testing

Extend cache tests to cover concurrent reuse, writes, external file replacement, file removal, key rotation, keyring errors, invalid ciphertext, and isolation across homes and namespaces. Prime the auth cache before verifying fallback when the keyring fails.

GitOrigin-RevId: eaf802ef4cfdbe482b56423807a1fe0fe3def2cd

commits.title: Honor server approval reviewer defaults on fresh TUI startup (#56090)
commits.message:
Honor server approval reviewer defaults on fresh TUI startup (#56090)

## Why

A saved client `approvals_reviewer` setting could override the app server's default when starting a fresh thread.

## What changed

Use explicit invocation overrides for the first thread's approval reviewer, leaving the selection to the server when no override is provided. Typed overrides take precedence over key-value overrides, and repeated key-value overrides use the last value. Explicit profile launches retain their resolved configuration behavior.

## Testing

Extend startup tests to cover server defaults, embedded startup, explicit override precedence, and profile launches. Verify that the first turn uses the reviewer returned by the server.

GitOrigin-RevId: 19d4d75bb8fbe522fb9495bd9c6951513f8ac4d2

commits.title: Keep TUI preferences editable when execution settings are invalid (#56091)
commits.message:
Keep TUI preferences editable when execution settings are invalid (#56091)

## Why

Saving a local preference could succeed but fail to apply live because reloading the full configuration also resolved execution settings. An unknown `model_provider`, for example, prevented the preference from taking effect.

## What changed

Reload config-panel preferences from the configuration layer stack into `LocalSettings` without rebuilding execution settings. Preserve CLI overrides, loader overrides, cloud configuration, and the existing choice of working directory.

## Testing

Extend the offline remote-session preference test with an unknown `model_provider` override, verifying that automatic recap and paste detection preferences still persist and apply live.

GitOrigin-RevId: 2377a01c77f3cb978a7ee6cd67c1fe89361131fb

commits.title: Avoid blocking EMA auth status checks on account refresh (#56127)
commits.message:
Avoid blocking EMA auth status checks on account refresh (#56127)

## Why

EMA MCP auth status checks acquired an account grant lease, making status inspection wait for account refresh coordination or an existing lease.

## What changed

Add `AuthManager::account_oauth_grant()` to inspect an owner-checked grant without acquiring the refresh lock. Use it for EMA status checks and share a single lazy read across servers, including missing grants and read errors. Keep refresh exclusion for token exchanges through `lease_account_oauth_grant()`.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for status checks across two EMA servers while an account lease is held. Extend account refresh tests to verify inspection completes with a lease held and refresh queued, and returns no grant after logout.

commits.title: Cancel MCP tool requests when response futures are dropped (#56132)
commits.message:
Cancel MCP tool requests when response futures are dropped (#56132)

## Why

Dropping a local tool-call future did not notify the MCP server that the request was cancelled, leaving remote work running.

## What changed

- Send a cancellation notification for the request when its response future is dropped, covering both ordinary tool calls and tool-input rounds.
- Preserve write order for stdio and in-process transports so cancellation cannot arrive before its tool request, without waiting for tool responses.

## Testing

Add regression tests for cancellation on drop, request-before-cancellation ordering under reversed send polling and exhausted task budgets, and continued use of the shared connection after cancellation.

## Why

An explicit `final_answer` with empty or whitespace-only text could allow queued agent mail to restart the turn instead of leaving it queued for the next turn.

## What changed

Extend regression coverage for empty and whitespace-only final answers, delivery of queued agent mail on the next turn, and message board notifications arriving before or after an empty final answer.

commits.title: Preserve safe enterprise MCP authentication error details (#56153)
commits.message:
Preserve safe enterprise MCP authentication error details (#56153)

## Why

Enterprise MCP token exchange and sign-in failures can collapse into generic errors, hiding useful diagnostics such as an OAuth `invalid_scope` rejection or a cancelled sign-in.

## What changed

Introduce `EmaErrorDetail` to carry static operation messages and sanitized SDK diagnostics through token-source errors and enterprise login completion. Exchange failures can report the stage, HTTP status, and allowlisted OAuth error code, such as `IdentityProvider: HTTP 400: invalid_scope`, without retaining arbitrary provider text or raw error chains.

Preserve specific discovery, credential storage, cancellation, and account/configuration mismatch errors instead of replacing them with generic failure messages.

## Testing

Extend tests to cover `invalid_scope` diagnostics, specific sign-in completion errors, and exclusion of credentials from diagnostics even when an outer error context contains sensitive text.

commits.title: Add managed network review domains before allow rules (#56154)
commits.message:
Add managed network review domains before allow rules (#56154)

## Why

Managed network policies need to require approval for selected hosts even when an exact or wildcard allow rule matches them.

## What changed

- Add `experimental_network.review_domains` to managed requirements and route matching hosts through the existing network approval flow. Explicit denials retain precedence, and approved connections still undergo DNS and local-address checks.
- Preserve review patterns across environment policy attachments and remote proxy configuration. Reject execution on an exec-server that lacks the `networkProxyReviewDomains` capability when review patterns are present.
- Expose `reviewDomains` through the app-server requirements API and generated schemas, and show `review_domains` in debug configuration output.
- Update approval reasons to say that network access requires approval rather than assuming the host is absent from the allowlist.

## Testing

Extend coverage for review precedence over exact and wildcard allows, explicit denials, DNS checks after local and remote approvals, approval hooks, policy merging, remote configuration round trips, and requirements API serialization.

commits.message:
Add AWS SigV4 signing to network proxy MITM hooks (#56182)

## Why

Allow workloads to make AWS requests with placeholder credentials while keeping real AWS credentials in the trusted proxy process.

## What changed

- Add an `aws_sigv4` hook action with a placeholder access key ID, region, service, HTTPS port, and credential sources from proxy environment variables or files.

- Mark generated credential headers as sensitive and suppress signing SDK trace events that could expose credentials.

## Why

V8's Abseil and protobuf's shared Abseil can be built for different C++ runtimes. Give V8's copy a distinct inline namespace so both can link into one binary without interposing incompatible functions.

## What changed

- Move pinned V8 dependency imports and BUILD overlays into `third_party/v8`, and inject those repositories into V8 through a module-extension bridge with no fallback downloads.
- Build V8's Abseil with a V8-specific inline namespace while preserving protobuf's shared Abseil namespace.
- Apply V8's C++ runtime settings in the Abseil, Highway, and simdutf overlays, and remove the shared `rules_cc` patch.
- Document source dependency ownership and the version, checksum, and overlay review procedure for V8 upgrades.

The URL parser treats backslashes as HTTP(S) path separators, while Git/libcurl does not. This difference can make a marketplace URL appear to match an allowed host pattern while Git connects to a different host.

Reject HTTP(S) URLs containing literal backslashes in userinfo when checking marketplace host patterns. Continue allowing encoded backslashes in userinfo and backslashes in paths or query strings.

Expand regression coverage to verify that denied URLs never invoke the cloner, create the marketplace install directory, or write configuration. Extend host-pattern tests to cover accepted HTTP(S) URL variants.

commits.title: Support bounded request bodies in AWS SigV4 signing (#56277)
commits.message:
Support bounded request bodies in AWS SigV4 signing (#56277)

## Why

The network proxy previously required AWS signing requests to have an empty body or use `UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD`, preventing signing of nonempty payloads.

## What changed

- Buffer and hash request bodies before signing, then forward the original bytes.
- Add `max_body_bytes` with an 8 MiB default and a 16 MiB maximum, plus a 30-second body read timeout.
- Limit concurrent buffering to eight requests with a five-second capacity wait. Retain reservations while forwarded body data remains alive.
- Reject trailers and mismatched content lengths for buffered payloads while preserving streaming for explicitly unsigned payloads.

## Testing

Add coverage for payload hashing and forwarding, body limits and timeouts, fragmented body collection, and buffer reservation lifetimes. Extend signing tests for S3 path and query canonicalization, header replacement, and secret exclusion from trace logs.

commits.title: Track accepted conversation history in rollout traces (#56312)
commits.message:
Track accepted conversation history in rollout traces (#56312)

## Why

Model output alone does not establish that an item entered conversation history. Treating every response item as accepted can include discarded attempts, while relying on a later request misses accepted final output when a turn ends or is interrupted.

## What changed

- Record `HistoryItemAccepted` events and retain Responses item IDs, generating missing IDs consistently across item events.
- Build thread conversation history from request inputs, compaction checkpoints, and explicit acceptance. Keep unaccepted output accessible through its inference call.
- Preserve inference provenance across retries and late response records without overwriting newer request or compaction snapshots.
- Mark turns with errors as failed. Bump trace schemas to version 2 and reject incompatible bundles and event schemas during replay.

## Testing

Add reducer coverage for discarded attempts with identical text, late responses, compaction, inherited context, and legacy bundle rejection. Add CLI integration tests that run `debug trace-reduce` after success, stream failure, and interruption followed by shutdown, including responses without provider item IDs.

commits.title: Make agent-message wakes respect interrupts and Plan mode (#56330)
commits.message:
Make agent-message wakes respect interrupts and Plan mode (#56330)

## Why

A pending agent-message wake can outlive an interrupt or a switch to Plan mode while model discovery is waiting. It must recheck whether it can start before consuming queued messages.

## What changed

- Revalidate reserved wakes after discovery and build the turn with the configuration selected during admission.
- Mark interrupted wake reservations as stopped so later agent messages cannot restart automatic work, while preserving queued messages for explicit turns.
- Keep finishing turns marked as running until completion is persisted, protecting their rollout writer from capacity eviction.

## Testing

Add regression tests for interrupts and Plan-mode changes during discovery, queued-message preservation, explicit follow-ups with `wake_on_agent_messages` disabled, and completion status and persistence with the feature enabled and disabled.

The steering test needs to deliver guidance after the first Responses request starts and ensure it is routed before releasing the blocked response. A steering acknowledgement alone does not establish that routing has completed.

Concurrent tests can reuse a closed file descriptor number, causing cleanup assertions that require `EBADF` to fail even when the inherited directory descriptor was closed.

commits.message:
Add silent append support to message boards (#56461)

## Why

Recording evidence on a message board needs a write operation that does not automatically subscribe the author or notify existing subscribers.

## What changed

- Add `AppendRequest` and `AgentMessageBoard::append` for local and in-memory boards, supporting new channels, existing channels, and thread replies without subscription or notification side effects.
- Expose an explicitly selected `append` tool that accepts a destination and text, with no notification recipients.

- Reject remote appends as unsupported without issuing an HTTP request.

commits.title: Prevent memory imports from racing with consolidation (#56462)
commits.message:
Prevent memory imports from racing with consolidation (#56462)

## Why

Concurrent imports and consolidation can modify the same memory workspace, leaving a partial import across memory versions or interfering with consolidation snapshots and baselines.

## What changed

- Add a cross-process workspace lock shared by memory imports and consolidation.
- Acquire locks for every import destination before modifying any workspace. Return a retryable busy error if a destination is locked, and skip consolidation when its workspace is busy.
- Hold locks through import completion even if the caller drops the future, and through consolidation agent termination and baseline finalization.

## Testing

Add an app-server integration test that blocks an active consolidation, verifies import rejection without partial writes or snapshot changes, then retries successfully and confirms imported resources remain visible to the next consolidation.

commits.title: Add keyboard copy selection to the owned transcript (#50434)
commits.message:
Add keyboard copy selection to the owned transcript (#50434)

## What changed

- Make `/copy` select the latest completed response directly in the owned transcript. Navigate user messages, code blocks, and blockquotes with arrow keys or `j`/`k`, use `g`/`G` to jump to the ends, and press Enter to copy or Escape to close.
- Highlight selected blocks and keep surrounding context visible during navigation and resizing. Preserve source payloads for code and quotes, including rendered Mermaid diagrams and fenced Markdown tables.
- Pause queued submissions until copy mode closes, and report clipboard results in the transcript footer.

## Testing

Add tests for copy routing, keyboard navigation, highlighting and resize behavior, source whitespace and line endings, clipboard completion, and queued-input resumption.

commits.title: Persist additional tool definitions in rollout history (#50435)
commits.message:
Persist additional tool definitions in rollout history (#50435)

## Why

`additional_tools` response items were excluded from rollout persistence, dropping their tool definitions from saved history.

## What changed

- Persist `additional_tools` items in both legacy and paginated history modes.
- Expose the variant in generated JSON schemas, TypeScript types, and Python models, with an optional `id`, a `role`, and arbitrary JSON tool definitions.

## Testing

Add a recorder round-trip test that verifies tool definitions survive recording and loading in both history modes without parse errors.

commits.title: Add a CLI command to uninstall the legacy Windows sandbox (#50437)
commits.message:
Add a CLI command to uninstall the legacy Windows sandbox (#50437)

## What changed

Add `codex sandbox uninstall` to remove machine-wide legacy Windows sandbox accounts and network rules with administrator privileges. Run cleanup without loading configuration, preserving Codex home, sandbox directories, and filesystem permissions. Reject the command on other platforms.

Keep commands after `--` forwarded to the sandbox, including `codex sandbox -- uninstall --help`.

## Testing

Add parsing coverage for the uninstall subcommand and command separator. Add an integration test verifying that help and invalid arguments work with malformed configuration and leave configuration and credentials unchanged.

commits.title: Support ordered response items in world-state context updates (#50441)
commits.message:
Support ordered response items in world-state context updates (#50441)

## Why

World-state sections could return only a single optional text fragment, with message separation controlled by the fragment itself. They could not contribute explicit `ResponseItem` values alongside instructions.

## What changed

- Let sections return ordered `WorldStateUpdate` values containing fragments or response items, with `Prefix`, `Standalone`, or `Mergeable` placement.
- Preserve explicit item boundaries when grouping context updates, and place prefix updates first when assembling initial context.
- Move standalone-message decisions from fragments to world-state updates and retain snapshot handling.

## Testing

Add tests for mixed fragment/item ordering, role and standalone boundaries, initial-context prefix placement, and snapshot restoration without repeated updates.
