commits.title: Load rollout history on a single blocking worker (#51499)
commits.message:
Load rollout history on a single blocking worker (#51499)

## What changed

Move full rollout history reading and parsing into one blocking worker for both plain `.jsonl` and compressed `.jsonl.zst` files. Use the shared cancellation-aware line iterator so canceled loads stop before processing another record, while preserving rollout items, thread IDs, and parse-error counts.

## Testing

Add regression tests for cancellation between records and equivalent history-loading results across plain and compressed files, including Unicode, CRLF line endings, malformed records, empty files, and invalid UTF-8.

commits.title: Add shared task pinning to the agent command center (#51500)
commits.message:
Add shared task pinning to the agent command center (#51500)

## What changed

- Use `p` to pin or unpin the selected task, with a configurable `agents.toggle_pin` binding.
- Display pinned tasks first in a `Pinned` group, preserving shared section order and applying search and status filters.
- Load pins from the shared thread section, including tasks outside the recent-task window, and refresh after pin changes. Disable pinning when the server does not support shared sections.

## Testing

Add coverage for shared pin/unpin state, paginated pin discovery and refreshing pins on reopen, shortcut dispatch and duplicate-action suppression, and pinned-group and custom-help snapshots.

commits.title: Bound relay connection attempts and handle pongs during blocked writes (#51502)
commits.message:
Bound relay connection attempts and handle pongs during blocked writes (#51502)

## Why

A stalled rendezvous WebSocket upgrade can prevent reconnects, while short-lived connections reset reconnect backoff too early. Blocked relay writes also prevent received pongs from clearing their heartbeat deadline.

## What changed

- Bound rendezvous WebSocket connection attempts with `DEFAULT_REMOTE_EXEC_SERVER_CONNECT_TIMEOUT`.
- Retain exponential reconnect backoff across short-lived connections, resetting it only after a connection lasts at least 120 seconds.
- Process pongs during blocked data writes while preserving the in-flight send and its independent write timeout. Prefer queued pongs over an expired heartbeat deadline.
- Abort the relay writer when its owning connection task is dropped.

## Testing

Add coverage for pongs arriving during blocked writes, missing and queued pongs, independent write timeouts, and writer cancellation. Extend reconnect tests to cover stalled WebSocket upgrades without re-registration and backoff reset after a stable session.

commits.title: Expose selected environments to MCP contributors (#51503)
commits.message:
Expose selected environments to MCP contributors (#51503)

## Why

MCP contributors need the complete executor selection to distinguish an unavailable primary executor from a ready secondary. Ready capability roots alone do not preserve pending or failed selections.

## What changed

Add `with_selected_environments` and `selected_environments` to `McpServerContributionContext`, and pass the captured selections during thread MCP resolution and model-step plugin selection. Preserve priority order and pending or failed entries. Use `None` for threadless discovery and `Some(&[])` for an explicitly empty selection.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for executor ordering with pending and failed selections, environment context in model-step plugin selection, and the distinction between absent and explicitly empty selections.

commits.title: Preserve live TUI settings when configuration reloads fail (#51510)
commits.message:
Preserve live TUI settings when configuration reloads fail (#51510)

## Why

Live preferences can be newer than the last successful configuration load. Starting a new thread after a reload failure could overwrite those preferences with stale settings.

## What changed

Carry local settings alongside the new-session configuration, retaining the live settings when reloading fails and applying the staged settings when the new thread starts. During resume and agent selection, replace staged local settings only when the directory-trust check actually reloads configuration.

## Testing

Add a regression test that changes a live rendering preference, writes invalid `config.toml`, and verifies that loading a new thread's configuration preserves the live local settings.

commits.title: Fix Windows 10 drive-letter opens for no-follow filesystem operations (#51511)
commits.message:
Fix Windows 10 drive-letter opens for no-follow filesystem operations (#51511)

## Why

On Windows 10, strict native opens can reject the DOS drive alias itself as a reparse point, preventing no-follow filesystem operations on ordinary drive-letter paths.

## What changed

Retry rejected drive-letter opens relative to a verified local volume root. Require the root to resolve to a physical disk volume directory without reparse attributes, and retain `OBJ_DONT_REPARSE` for paths beneath it so junctions remain blocked.

## Testing

Add Windows tests for file creation and reading through the volume fallback, opening the drive root, and rejecting junction traversal and creation. Validate accepted volume-root names and verify that named pipes are rejected without establishing a client connection.

GitOrigin-RevId: 51ffde4f77d2af45d18dfc4cb026d73a0e69b061

commits.title: Align Windows sandbox temp permissions with the child environment (#51512)
commits.message:
Align Windows sandbox temp permissions with the child environment (#51512)

## Why

Windows temp grants could fall back to host `TEMP`/`TMP` values and bypass read-only or denied subpaths. Sandbox permissions must match the environment passed to the child process.

## What changed

- Resolve `:tmpdir` from absolute `TEMP`/`TMP` paths in the completed workload environment, preserving access modes and missing-path rules without falling back to host values.
- Deduplicate Windows environment keys case-insensitively in a deterministic order so permission resolution and the child environment select the same value.
- Use the resolved temp policy for elevated sandbox overrides across core execution, exec-server, and direct spawning.
- Launch direct-spawn sandbox wrappers with the supplied Codex executable, materializing an inner helper only when it is that executable.

## Testing

Add Windows regression coverage for temp-only writes, read-only and denied carveouts, mixed-case and duplicate environment keys, unavailable temp paths, and empty or missing write-root overrides. Exercise core execution and direct spawning, and extend exec-server RPC coverage to the elevated backend with temp values set through the environment policy.

GitOrigin-RevId: 16b8bd4702cc434fd743a08c75a3e4515780bff3

commits.title: Expose detailed agent tree shutdown failure reports (#51515)
commits.message:
Expose detailed agent tree shutdown failure reports (#51515)

## Why

Agent tree shutdown previously returned a generic error without identifying which operation or thread failed, making cleanup failures difficult to diagnose.

## What changed

- Add `AgentTreeShutdown::wait_detailed()` and public report types while preserving the existing `wait()` result and error message.
- Record operation, optional thread ID, and either an abandoned teardown guard or a failed phase with a payload-free error category across session cleanup, child spawn cleanup, and resident eviction.
- Give each tree a correlation ID, log each failure, and retain up to 64 failures with a count of additional failures omitted. Record failures before releasing tree membership so all completed waiters observe the same report.

## Testing

Add unit coverage for aborted and completed teardown, cloned guard context, concurrent and repeated waiters, omitted failure counts, and report formatting without raw error payloads. Extend integration coverage for successful tree shutdown and persistence writer failures, including compatibility with `wait()`.

GitOrigin-RevId: 68784af28b63e875b00a55d78729f0cc5b01ac15

commits.title: Pass thread persistence intent to attachment uploads (#51517)
commits.message:
Pass thread persistence intent to attachment uploads (#51517)

## Why

Attachment stores need to distinguish uploads from ephemeral threads, which intentionally skip durable persistence.

## What changed

Add `ephemeral` to `UploadRequest` and propagate the turn configuration through image preparation for messages, tool outputs, and history replay. Include the flag in debug output while keeping attachment bytes redacted.

## Testing

Extend the Guardian context-budget test to assert that a persistent Guardian uploads exactly one image with `ephemeral: false`. Update the attachment debug-output assertion to include the new field.

commits.title: Preserve the CLI MXC preference in executor config reads (#51525)
commits.message:
Preserve the CLI MXC preference in executor config reads (#51525)

## Why

Executor config reads omitted the startup `features.prefer_mxc` override, so clients could not see the CLI sandbox preference.

## What changed

- Include the explicit CLI `features.prefer_mxc` value in `environmentConfig/read` as a `session-flags` layer, above project config and below legacy managed file and MDM config.
- Retain only this preference from startup overrides.
- Expose `windows_mxc_allowed_by_config` to share MXC eligibility checks after callers resolve the active permission profile.

Add CLI and remote executor coverage for preference propagation and filtering, plus a unit test verifying that both legacy managed config sources retain precedence.

commits.title: Ignore ripgrep configuration when expanding sandbox deny globs (#51527)
commits.message:
Ignore ripgrep configuration when expanding sandbox deny globs (#51527)

## Why

User ripgrep configuration can suppress the file list used to construct Linux sandbox deny masks. For example, `--quiet` in `RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH` can leave files matching deny globs unmasked.

## What changed

Pass `--no-config` to the ripgrep invocation that expands denied-file globs.

## Testing

Extend the multiple-denied-files regression test with a ripgrep configuration containing `--quiet`, checking that denied files remain unreadable and unwritable while allowed files remain accessible. Skip the ripgrep-specific case when no protected `rg` executable is available.

releaseNotes.body:
## New Features

- GPT-6.1 Sol is now the default model in the bundled and Amazon Bedrock catalogs. (#49318, #49339)
- Amazon Bedrock supports multi-agent V2 and Ultra reasoning on compatible models; Bedrock Mantle also accepts AWS GovCloud regions. (#49345, #49813)
- Sign in to MCP servers from an active terminal session with `/mcp login <name>`. (#49290)
- Choose your microphone, speaker, and microphone input channels for voice conversations, with preferences saved locally. (#49437, #49836)
- Daybreak is opt-in through `--enable cli_daybreak` or `features.cli_daybreak=true`; `daybreak=true` alone is insufficient. By default, controls and indicators are hidden, `/daybreak` is unavailable, and automatic Cyber routing is omitted—even for saved Daybreak threads. Saved preferences remain intact. Opt-in routing requires eligible ChatGPT sign-in, the OpenAI provider, and advertised model/program support. (#49856, #49858, #49859, #49861, #51207)
- Select a Cyber access program per turn with `codex exec --cyber-access-program` or the TypeScript SDK’s `cyberAccessProgram` option. The explicit exec override remains available with `cli_daybreak` disabled and leaves the saved choice unchanged. (#49939, #51207)

## Bug Fixes

- Approved filesystem escalation can now grant broader write access while preserving denied reads and network restrictions. Background tasks retain their originating turn’s permissions. (#49353, #49880)
- Explicit launch permissions survive terminal reconnects and new sessions, while implicit client settings no longer overwrite server or saved-thread web-search settings. (#49809, #49799)
- Elevated Windows terminal sessions can start using an embedded server, and sandboxed PowerShell preserves relative paths beneath protected user profiles. (#49855, #49690)
- Enter correctly submits buffered input after paste detection expires, including in Vim insert mode. (#49810)
- Thread resume includes the latest committed history. Startup detects recoverable SQLite corruption earlier and preserves damaged databases as backups. (#49599, #49701)
- Responses retries and WebSocket-to-HTTP fallback honor server retry guidance, reducing premature failures during overload. (#49441)

## Documentation

- Authentication guidance now accounts for keyring storage instead of implying credentials always reside in `auth.json`. (#49361)

## Chores

notes.body:
## New Features

- GPT-6.1 Sol is now the default model in the bundled and Amazon Bedrock catalogs. (#49318, #49339)
- Amazon Bedrock supports multi-agent V2 and Ultra reasoning on compatible models; Bedrock Mantle also accepts AWS GovCloud regions. (#49345, #49813)
- Sign in to MCP servers from an active terminal session with `/mcp login <name>`. (#49290)
- Choose your microphone, speaker, and microphone input channels for voice conversations, with preferences saved locally. (#49437, #49836)
- Daybreak is opt-in through `--enable cli_daybreak` or `features.cli_daybreak=true`; `daybreak=true` alone is insufficient. By default, controls and indicators are hidden, `/daybreak` is unavailable, and automatic Cyber routing is omitted—even for saved Daybreak threads. Saved preferences remain intact. Opt-in routing requires eligible ChatGPT sign-in, the OpenAI provider, and advertised model/program support. (#49856, #49858, #49859, #49861, #51207)
- Select a Cyber access program per turn with `codex exec --cyber-access-program` or the TypeScript SDK’s `cyberAccessProgram` option. The explicit exec override remains available with `cli_daybreak` disabled and leaves the saved choice unchanged. (#49939, #51207)

## Bug Fixes

- Approved filesystem escalation can now grant broader write access while preserving denied reads and network restrictions. Background tasks retain their originating turn’s permissions. (#49353, #49880)
- Explicit launch permissions survive terminal reconnects and new sessions, while implicit client settings no longer overwrite server or saved-thread web-search settings. (#49809, #49799)
- Elevated Windows terminal sessions can start using an embedded server, and sandboxed PowerShell preserves relative paths beneath protected user profiles. (#49855, #49690)
- Enter correctly submits buffered input after paste detection expires, including in Vim insert mode. (#49810)
- Thread resume includes the latest committed history. Startup detects recoverable SQLite corruption earlier and preserves damaged databases as backups. (#49599, #49701)
- Responses retries and WebSocket-to-HTTP fallback honor server retry guidance, reducing premature failures during overload. (#49441)

## Documentation

- Authentication guidance now accounts for keyring storage instead of implying credentials always reside in `auth.json`. (#49361)

## Chores

- Publishing an older alpha or hotfix no longer moves npm alpha tags backward. (#49704)

commits.title: Enable parallel execution for read-only tools (#52245)
commits.message:
Enable parallel execution for read-only tools (#52245)

## Why

Tools that do not opt into parallel execution acquire an exclusive scheduler lock, serializing independent reads.

## What changed

Allow skill listing and reading, memory listing, reading and searching, conversation history search and reading, plugin listing, agent listing, current time, remaining context, and `get_goal` to run in parallel. Keep goal creation and updates serialized.

## Testing

Add `cloud_skill_reads_run_in_parallel`, which uses a barrier to require two cloud skill reads to overlap and verifies that each returns the expected resource contents.

GitOrigin-RevId: 97b5634f1f84be2ba092be89e6e9c634ca75c07b

commits.title: Add opt-in Guardian trust for orchestrator connector identities (#52250)
commits.message:
Add opt-in Guardian trust for orchestrator connector identities (#52250)

## What changed

Add the disabled-by-default `guardian_trust_orchestrator_connectors` feature flag. When enabled, Guardian V2 accepts connectors with nonblank IDs from the host-owned plugin service orchestrator as a trusted source without requiring a matching user configuration declaration.

Distinguish orchestrator provenance from user configuration in trusted-tool context. Trust remains scoped to the exact server or connector identity and source; descriptions, outputs, other tools, and other connectors remain untrusted.

## Testing

Add coverage for host-owned connector context, rejection of extension-owned Apps lookalikes and blank connector IDs, source-specific trust metadata, and context token limits. Snapshot the connector approval request history.

commits.title: Preserve large arguments in executed tool call metadata (#52268)
commits.message:
Preserve large arguments in executed tool call metadata (#52268)

## Why

Fixed argument limits truncated recorded tool calls even when their metadata fit within the available message budget.

## What changed

- Remove the 8 KiB per-call and 32 KiB per-output argument limits for direct calls and Code Mode.
- Preserve full recorded arguments while retaining message metadata budgets, pending-call limits, and the direct metadata retention limit.
- Rename the normalization helper to `normalize_executed_tool_call_completeness`; it now only clears completeness when calls or tool names were lost.

## Testing

Update regression coverage for large arguments, escaped inputs, reserved-key wrappers, and argument and result metadata preservation across Code Mode waits.

commits.title: Enable text selection in the fullscreen TUI footer (#52270)
commits.message:
Enable text selection in the fullscreen TUI footer (#52270)

## What changed

Allow mouse selection and plain-text copying of rendered status and footer text, honoring `tui.copy_on_select` and existing selection keyboard controls. Keep the selected region stable while other content updates, preserve Unicode and terminal hyperlinks, and clear selections when their region becomes invalid.

Defer warning clicks until a stationary mouse release so dragging selects text without opening the warning viewer. Preserve the composer draft and cursor while selecting footer text.

## Testing

Add unit and snapshot coverage for visible-text copying, Unicode and hyperlinks, selection invalidation, keyboard ownership, and stationary clicks versus drags. Add a fullscreen integration test for warning selection and draft preservation.

commits.title: Add configurable persistent leader shortcuts to the TUI (#52273)
commits.message:
Add configurable persistent leader shortcuts to the TUI (#52273)

## What changed

- Add `tui.keymap.global.leader`, defaulting to `ctrl-x`, and symbolic bindings such as `leader c` that follow the configured prefix. The default prefix yields to existing custom shortcuts and chord prefixes.
- Keep leader shortcut hints open until completion or cancellation, while ordinary chords retain their one-second timeout. Pressing `esc` or repeating the leader cancels the pending shortcut.
- Add leader configuration and a `Use leader...` capture option to `/keymap`, with resolved shortcut labels and conflict validation.
- Cancel pending chords when input targets change, on paste or focus loss, and on mouse actions other than movement.
- Move the default voice mute shortcut from `ctrl-x` to `f9` and update its tests and displayed hints.

- Log review retry scheduling with failure details, attempt limits, backoff, and remaining deadline budget.
- Emit warnings for Guardian V2 background scoring failures with the failure reason, context mode, and duration, even when metrics are unavailable.

commits.title: Preserve UTF-8 byte semantics in network domain matching (#52277)
commits.message:
Preserve UTF-8 byte semantics in network domain matching (#52277)

## Why

Domain wildcards need to retain the byte-based behavior of `globset`. Counting Unicode scalar values changes how `?` matches non-ASCII hosts.

## What changed

Match domain patterns against UTF-8 bytes so `?` consumes exactly one byte. For example, `api??.com` matches `apié.com`. Match hosts through borrowed byte slices, avoiding the per-match character-vector allocation.

Document ASCII case insensitivity and the absence of IDNA conversion: hosts supplied as Punycode require patterns using their Punycode spelling.

## Testing

Compare Unicode wildcard cases against `globset` for both allowlists and denylists, including multibyte characters, combining marks, Punycode, and case sensitivity. Update the exhaustive dynamic-programming comparison and retry-boundary tests to operate on bytes.

GitOrigin-RevId: fae5b3b1ae60b469cd61a44c5c6e245730adc8ba

commits.title: Honor custom OTLP metrics exporters when analytics is disabled (#52278)
commits.message:
Honor custom OTLP metrics exporters when analytics is disabled (#52278)

## Why

Disabling OpenAI analytics also disabled explicitly configured OTLP metrics collectors. Users should be able to export metrics to their own collectors independently of `analytics.enabled`.

## What changed

Apply the analytics preference only to the built-in `statsig` metrics exporter. Keep custom OTLP HTTP and gRPC exporters enabled regardless of that preference, and use `otel.metrics_exporter = "none"` to disable metrics export. Clarify these settings in config documentation and the schema.

## Testing

Cover exporter selection across explicit and default analytics preferences. Update app-server and daemon telemetry tests to verify custom metrics export with analytics disabled, and worktree tests to disable metrics through the exporter setting.

GitOrigin-RevId: 0c61f0f01e2b694db642ac7e7fd1dac9965c7d96

commits.title: Emit one developer notice per incremental namespace update batch (#52295)
commits.message:
Emit one developer notice per incremental namespace update batch (#52295)

## What changed

Move incremental tool guidance out of namespace descriptions and into a developer message preceding each namespace declaration batch after the initial catalog. The notice covers newly added namespaces as well as changed ones, explaining that earlier tools remain available unless explicitly removed and that newer definitions replace earlier ones.

Retain the notice alongside tool declarations in full-history agent forks, and discard it when legacy compaction forks rebuild those declarations.

## Testing

Add unit coverage for multiple new namespaces sharing one notice. Update request-history snapshots for tool changes, removals and restoration, and regular Responses requests. Extend resume and fork tests to cover notice preservation without duplication and removal when rebuilding declarations.

commits.title: Make Bazel release jobs advisory (#52299)
commits.message:
Make Bazel release jobs advisory (#52299)

## Why

Parallel Bazel artifacts are advisory while Cargo remains the release path.

## What changed

- Set `continue-on-error` for Bazel matrix jobs covering builds, Windows symbols and signing, and macOS signing, packaging, and verification.
- Assign the main release build jobs in both workflows to the `bazel` environment with `deployment: false`.

commits.title: Add opt-in credential masking for proxied sandboxed sessions (#52302)
commits.message:
Add opt-in credential masking for proxied sandboxed sessions (#52302)

## What changed

- Add the disabled-by-default `features.credential_masking` flag to enable credential brokerage through an already enabled network proxy, retaining custom credential providers and managed configuration precedence.
- Prevent project configuration from overriding credential masking and apply existing credential-broker protections to project shell settings when masking is enabled.
- Keep brokerage inactive when the proxy is disabled. Warn at startup and after permission-profile changes when masking is inactive because sandboxing or the proxy is disabled, or provider environment keys conflict.

## Testing

Add coverage for configuration precedence, project protections in both configuration loaders, permission-profile transitions, inactive-masking warnings, and shell snapshot masking of built-in and custom credentials.

GitOrigin-RevId: 4bcb293356e8c1524bdaa4f1b95cbc1e935a5271

commits.title: Persist remote-control RPC preferences in managed daemon settings (#52304)
commits.message:
Persist remote-control RPC preferences in managed daemon settings (#52304)

## Why

Durable remote-control RPC changes need to update the managed daemon's launch settings so future launches use the saved preference.

## What changed

- Save non-ephemeral `remoteControl/enable` and `remoteControl/disable` requests to `remoteControlEnabled` in `app-server-daemon/settings.json` for managed daemons.
- Preserve other settings and write updates atomically. Skip persistence when `daemon.lock` is held so concurrent lifecycle operations take precedence without blocking the RPC.
- Leave daemon settings untouched for ephemeral requests and unmanaged servers.

## Testing

Add integration coverage for durable enable and disable, ephemeral requests, and lock contention. Extend the unmanaged-server test to verify that no daemon settings file is created.

GitOrigin-RevId: 2baf261ed62f7c7ad87c9779ffb91c59e923f0f8

commits.title: Track history initialization in Responses turn metadata (#52325)
commits.message:
Track history initialization in Responses turn metadata (#52325)

## What changed

Add `history_initialization` to `x-codex-turn-metadata`, distinguishing `new`, `cleared`, `cold_resume`, `warm_fork`, `cold_fork`, and `supplied_history`.

Classify forks by whether the source runtime is loaded and has not shut down. Preserve the classification for the runtime's lifetime, including warm resumes and compaction. This records how history was initialized; it does not establish whether tool metadata is missing. Reserve the field against client-supplied overrides.

## Testing

Extend coverage for warm and cold forks, cold resumes, warm reconnects, supplied history, WebSocket metadata serialization, and reserved-field filtering.

GitOrigin-RevId: 468153512a84d0f4d4ea742198a29e0fa3873a72

commits.title: Remove per-content source attribution metadata (#52329)
commits.message:
Remove per-content source attribution metadata (#52329)

## What changed

- Remove `ContentItemMetadata`, provenance and namespace types, and the `content_item_metadata` protocol field while retaining `content_item_kinds` classifications.
- Simplify context fragments, extension contributions, and hook output to carry content without source attribution. Return MCP tool results directly without an attribution wrapper.
- Render context-window hints together in a single text fragment.

## Testing

Update Responses and Responses Lite request assertions to expect content-kind classifications without per-content attribution, and adapt context, hook, and extension tests to the simplified types.

commits.title: Clamp wrapped source ranges before remapping terminal hyperlinks (#52330)
commits.message:
Clamp wrapped source ranges before remapping terminal hyperlinks (#52330)

## Why

Wrapping can retain a cursor sentinel one byte past the end of the input. Using that range to slice source text during hyperlink remapping can panic.

## What changed

Clamp wrapped range boundaries to the input length before calculating hyperlink columns and recording logical source ranges, keeping both aligned with the visible text.

## Testing

Add a regression test that extends a wrapped range past the input boundary and verifies that the line, hyperlinks, and logical source are preserved.

commits.title: Preserve inherited context in prediction forks (#53678)
commits.message:
Preserve inherited context in prediction forks (#53678)

## Why

Prediction forks need to retain their parent's context even when it exceeds the automatic compaction threshold. Compaction or context resets can otherwise replace the history used for the prediction.

## What changed

- Apply a thread-local `AutoCompactionDisabled` policy to experimental prediction forks without changing model or skill budgets.
- Skip automatic compaction before, during, and after turns, including context-limit recovery, and suppress new token-budget reminders.
- Reject `new_context` requests for these threads and report context-limit failures without compacting their history.

## Testing

Add regression tests for legacy and paginated prediction forks across compaction thresholds, unchanged parent compaction and skill/tool inputs, context-limit failures, and rejected context resets. Add a request-history snapshot verifying inherited context and reminders survive without compaction or additional reminders after a tool call.

commits.title: Account for replay caches in encrypted compaction budgets (#53691)
commits.message:
Account for replay caches in encrypted compaction budgets (#53691)

## Why

Encrypted compaction payloads can include sampled-token replay caches that increase their size roughly threefold. Budgeting them as ordinary text can reject checkpoints that fit the model context budget.

## What changed

Use a shared estimate of one token per twelve ciphertext bytes, rounded up, for encrypted `Compaction` and `ContextCompaction` items in history and Guardian context budgeting. Guardian continues to count framing and metadata separately.

Check parent compactions against the configured token budget and a separate hard wire-size limit. Preserve the complete encrypted checkpoint when it fits. The token estimate remains a heuristic and can underestimate legacy checkpoints without replay caches.

## Testing

Add coverage for token-estimate rounding, parent compaction token and wire-size limits, and reviewer continuation with a cached compaction preserved intact.

Keep the displayed transcript snapshot and reading position paused during selection and after exiting the mode. Add entry and exit methods; this change does not yet bind mode entry to a user-facing key.

commits.title: Interrupt and drain canceled classifier responses before socket reuse (#53698)
commits.message:
Interrupt and drain canceled classifier responses before socket reuse (#53698)

## Why

Canceled classifier requests need bounded cleanup that preserves received token usage and returns only safe WebSocket connections to the pool.

## What changed

- Own classifier response streams and connection leases together, interrupting dropped responses with a one-second cleanup deadline.
- Require a matching interruption acknowledgement and response completion before reusing a canceled response's socket. Retire sockets on rejection, invalid acknowledgements, or timeout while preserving any received completion and token usage.
- Skip requests canceled before dispatch and return their unused sockets to the pool.
- Distinguish cancellation from ordinary steering, which continues draining without requiring an interruption acknowledgement.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for cancellation, acknowledgement ordering and failures, cleanup timeouts, socket reuse, and token accounting under backpressure. Extend steering tests to cover rejected and missing acknowledgements.

Pending classifications can outlive the `max_tool_call_lag` window in which their scores are reusable, keeping metadata waits or classifier transports active after the result becomes stale.

## What changed

- Treat expiry as supersession, preserving cached scores and the last completed conversation checkpoint and transcript cursor.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for lag boundaries, active wrapper discounts, transport cancellation before and after early scores, expired requests skipping preparation, and conversation history and transcript deltas surviving cancellation.

commits.title: Fix cancellation of macOS user-verification prompts (#53790)
commits.message:
Fix cancellation of macOS user-verification prompts (#53790)

## Why

Keychain signing reconstructs its own authentication context, so invalidating the caller's context does not reliably cancel the context that owns the biometric prompt.

## What changed

Evaluate the stored key's access-control policy explicitly with `LAContext` before signing. On cancellation, invalidate that context and wait for its authorization callback before releasing the lifecycle lock, rejecting any late success. Reload the key with the authorized context and disable further interaction so signing cannot open another prompt.

## Testing

Update unit tests to cover waiting for cancellation completion and rejecting completed authorization after cancellation. Add an ignored macOS hardware test and setup instructions covering persisted Secure Enclave key reuse, signature verification, cancellation, retry signing, and cleanup.

commits.title: Retain rollout migration locks across worker cancellation (#53794)
commits.message:
Retain rollout migration locks across worker cancellation (#53794)

## Why

Cancelling an async migration caller can leave its blocking compression or decompression worker running. Releasing migration locks before that worker finishes allows other writers or migrations to access files still being processed.

## What changed

Share maintenance, cross-process writer, and local writer locks with blocking workers during migration and recovery. Keep those locks held until file work completes, releasing cross-process locks before allowing local writers to proceed.

## Testing

Add a regression test for cancelled compression and decompression callers that verifies locks remain held until the worker finishes and the output is complete. Preserve the Unix check that decompression temporaries have owner-only permissions.

commits.title: Refresh Guardian reviews when review context changes (#53797)
commits.message:
Refresh Guardian reviews when review context changes (#53797)

## Why

Assistant messages delivered during a pending Guardian review can change its evidence. Previously, these context changes aborted the review instead of triggering a fresh assessment.

## What changed

Treat changes to local or root review context as stale authorization so Guardian retries with updated evidence. Cancellation and history resets still abort the review.

## Testing

Extend local and worker delivery tests to cover refreshed allow and deny decisions, verify that the new review includes the delivered message, and ensure commands execute exactly once after approval and never on stale approval or denial.

commits.title: Wire background compaction into the turn lifecycle (#53800)
commits.message:
Wire background compaction into the turn lifecycle (#53800)

## What changed

- Launch background compaction at eligible pre-turn, mid-turn, and post-turn checkpoints when `AsyncCompaction` is enabled, capturing the current world state and client routing state.
- Adopt ready results at compaction checkpoints while preserving newer messages, tool outputs, and world-state updates. Continue normally if an optional result is rejected.
- Run one foreground compaction if an adopted result still exceeds the context limit.
- Prevent cancelled turns from launching new background work while preserving already-running work for later reuse.

## Testing

Add unit and scenario coverage for stale history and account changes, cancellation, pending-result reuse and fallback, retained tool outputs, compaction event pairing, and token usage accounting. Add a context snapshot covering a collaboration-mode change while compaction runs.

commits.title: Add safe diagnostics to workspace routing configuration errors (#53805)
commits.message:
Add safe diagnostics to workspace routing configuration errors (#53805)

## Why

Workspace routing reported generic requirements load and reload failures, hiding the cause. Raw configuration errors can contain secrets, so exposing their messages directly is unsafe.

## What changed

Include a safe reason in configuration load and reload errors: file locations or non-file line and column numbers, cloud error categories and HTTP status codes, known network policy denials, or OS error details. Exclude raw parser messages, configuration contents, and backend-supplied policy names and IDs.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for configuration locations, cloud failures, and network policy denials. Verify that malformed local and cloud configuration reports useful errors without exposing secret values or policy identifiers, and still prevents workspace routing from falling back to startup configuration.

commits.title: Support daemon installation from Windows WinGet packages (#53811)
commits.message:
Support daemon installation from Windows WinGet packages (#53811)

## Why

WinGet archives place the CLI and code mode host at the package root, while daemon installation expects them under `bin/`. This layout mismatch prevents installing the daemon from a WinGet CLI package.

## What changed

Validate WinGet packages in their original layout before converting the staged copy to the daemon layout. Move the executables under `bin/`, update the package entrypoint and optional voice manifest checksum key, and hash the final tree for release reuse. Leave the source package unchanged.

## Testing

Add a Windows integration test covering daemon startup, repeated `update --from-cli --yes` calls, rewritten manifests, and rejection of an incomplete package without changing the selected release or source manifests.

commits.message:
Apply feature overrides when restarting the app-server daemon (#53751)

## Why

`codex app-server daemon restart` previously reused saved settings without applying feature flags supplied on the command line.

## What changed

Apply `--enable`, `--disable`, and boolean `-c features.*` overrides during an explicit restart and persist them for subsequent restarts. Accept nested `enabled` values, normalize feature aliases, and replace conflicting saved aliases while preserving unrelated settings.

Reject invalid feature toggles before stopping the daemon or saving settings.

item.text: 0.163.0. New Features Open /config to search preferences across categories, change supported settings immediately, and see which changes require a restart. ( #52990 , #53429 ) Send a follow-up while Codex is responding to steer it immediately. Interrupting a turn also stops active Code Mode cells and their nested tool calls. ( #51812 , #51835 ) Configure a leader key in /keymap . The default is Ctrl+X , shortcut hints stay open until you choose or cancel, and voice mute moves to F9 . ( #52273 ) Restart a managed background server from /daemon . Codex warns about work the restart could interrupt, then reconnects automatically. ( #53173 ) Codex can run independent read-only tools in parallel, including skill, memory, and conversation-history lookups. ( #52245 ) Daybreak is enabled by default for eligible accounts. codex exec can also select it with an OpenAI API key when the server offers access. ( #53701 , #53717 ) Bug Fixes Resuming a saved thread restores its permissions and network approvals, while respecting explicit overrides and current managed policy. ( #53150 , #53419 , #53424 ) The network proxy now checks permission before a DNS lookup, rejects duplicate Host headers, and prevents credential aliases from bypassing inspection hooks. ( #51650 , #52661 , #53506 ) Return to an existing side conversation with /side after switching threads. Answers to pending prompts also go back to the thread that asked. ( #52184 , #53436 ) On Windows, Ctrl+V and Shift+Insert paste text as well as images. On WSL, repeated pastes reuse the clipboard reader, and copy attempts time out instead of hanging. ( #53224 , #52967 , #53453 ) Local commands finish promptly when a child keeps an output pipe open. Remote commands preserve late-arriving output so the final poll can still collect it. ( #52652 , #53331 , #53622 ) codex exec no longer prints the same file diff again after an unrelated command. ( #53444 ) Documentation Updated the bundled OpenAI Docs guidance for migrations to the GPT-6 family, including model-specific reasoning, tool use, and data residency considerations. ( #51768 ) Clarified how the Linux sandbox uses bubblewrap for filesystem isolation and seccomp for syscall filtering. ( #52610 ) Chores Codex now uses its standard shell executor and no longer bundles a patched zsh . Configurations using the retired shell flags receive a migration notice. ( #52160 , #52213 ) Reduced Linux and macOS release package size by stripping symbols from packaged binaries while preserving them in the original build outputs. releaseNotes.body:
## New Features

- Open `/config` to search preferences across categories, change supported settings immediately, and see which changes require a restart. (#52990, #53429)
- Send a follow-up while Codex is responding to steer it immediately. Interrupting a turn also stops active Code Mode cells and their nested tool calls. (#51812, #51835)
- Configure a leader key in `/keymap`. The default is `Ctrl+X`, shortcut hints stay open until you choose or cancel, and voice mute moves to `F9`. (#52273)
- Restart a managed background server from `/daemon`. Codex warns about work the restart could interrupt, then reconnects automatically. (#53173)
- Codex can run independent read-only tools in parallel, including skill, memory, and conversation-history lookups. (#52245)
- Daybreak is enabled by default for eligible accounts. `codex exec` can also select it with an OpenAI API key when the server offers access. (#53701, #53717)

## Bug Fixes

- Resuming a saved thread restores its permissions and network approvals, while respecting explicit overrides and current managed policy. (#53150, #53419, #53424)
- The network proxy now checks permission before a DNS lookup, rejects duplicate `Host` headers, and prevents credential aliases from bypassing inspection hooks. (#51650, #52661, #53506)
- Return to an existing side conversation with `/side` after switching threads. Answers to pending prompts also go back to the thread that asked. (#52184, #53436)
- On Windows, `Ctrl+V` and `Shift+Insert` paste text as well as images. On WSL, repeated pastes reuse the clipboard reader, and copy attempts time out instead of hanging. (#53224, #52967, #53453)
- Local commands finish promptly when a child keeps an output pipe open. Remote commands preserve late-arriving output so the final poll can still collect it. (#52652, #53331, #53622)
- `codex exec` no longer prints the same file diff again after an unrelated command. (#53444)

## Documentation

- Updated the bundled OpenAI Docs guidance for migrations to the GPT-6 family, including model-specific reasoning, tool use, and data residency considerations. (#51768)
- Clarified how the Linux sandbox uses bubblewrap for filesystem isolation and seccomp for syscall filtering. (#52610)

## Chores

- Codex now uses its standard shell executor and no longer bundles a patched `zsh`. Configurations using the retired shell flags receive a migration notice. (#52160, #52213)
- Reduced Linux and macOS release package size by stripping symbols from packaged binaries while preserving them in the original build outputs. (#52178)

commits.title: Bind plugin hook approval to plugin contents (#54619)
commits.message:
Bind plugin hook approval to plugin contents (#54619)

## Why

A plugin's scripts can change without changing its hook declaration. Declaration-only approval therefore lets changed plugin code run under an existing hook approval.

## What changed

- Fingerprint plugin bundle contents and include the content hash in the approval value returned by `hooks/list`. Persist it as `trusted_content_hash`, keeping `trusted_hash` compatible with older clients.
- Verify contents before each command or MCP hook execution, within the hook's timeout, and require renewed approval when approved contents change.
- Migrate legacy declaration-only approvals to a shared, immutable content baseline per plugin and config home.
- Exclude generated Python bytecode, `.venv`, and `.egg-info` entries from fingerprints. Run app-server hook listing on blocking tasks.

## Testing

Extend integration coverage for plugin upgrades and rollbacks requiring approval, same-turn script changes preventing further hook execution, shared legacy approval baselines, and generated Python artifacts preserving trust.

GitOrigin-RevId: faaf7658210d8adb2534ddd614c72ec993920840

commits.title: Resolve stable releases dynamically for exec-server compatibility tests (#54623)
commits.message:
Resolve stable releases dynamically for exec-server compatibility tests (#54623)

## What changed

Replace fixed release pins for app-server/exec-server compatibility tests with the latest stable version and the stable release published closest to 60 days ago. Exclude drafts and prereleases, and prefer the higher version when publication dates are equally close.

Resolve release versions and SHA-256 asset digests before Linux Bazel CI runs, passing them through `CODEX_COMPAT_RELEASES` to the release archive repositories. Reuse the argument comment lint action so it also prepares compatibility releases. Add bounded retries for transient GitHub release reads.

## Testing

Add unit coverage for stable release filtering, version ordering, nearest publication dates, tie-breaking, and deduplication when both selections resolve to the same release.

GitOrigin-RevId: 5a8cf8bdabd77ab3fa89bbb711367b5d9ce8044b

commits.title: Preserve disconnect reasons in Noise handshake errors (#54637)
commits.message:
Preserve disconnect reasons in Noise handshake errors (#54637)

## Why

Noise handshake failures before connection readiness returned a generic error even when the transport had reported a specific disconnect reason. No `RpcClient` was reading the connection event channel at that point.

## What changed

Read the pending disconnect event when a Noise rendezvous handshake fails and append its reason to the handshake error when available.

## Testing

Add a regression test covering unexpected text frames and relay stream resets, checking that each produces the expected transport reason in the handshake error.

GitOrigin-RevId: 9b8ef9c8dcba75b46d51dc67784af46d4ca74b85

commits.title: Stream rollout records during thread history materialization (#54639)
commits.message:
Stream rollout records during thread history materialization (#54639)

## Why

Thread history materialization allocated a buffer for the entire unread rollout suffix before processing records, increasing memory use for large rollouts.

## What changed

Read records incrementally with a buffered reader bounded to the captured file end. Reuse the line buffer, preserve trailing partial records for the next pass, and report unexpected EOF if the rollout shrinks during reading.

## Testing

Extend the partial-line boundary test with 64 KiB of padding per record to verify byte offsets and deferred processing until the final newline is durable.

GitOrigin-RevId: c0426e3e364748b117285b248f6988a4fe064b94

commits.title: Retry npm release publishing and match macOS verification runners (#54641)
commits.message:
Retry npm release publishing and match macOS verification runners (#54641)

## What changed

- Attempt each `npm publish` up to three times, with 10- and 20-second delays and fresh OIDC credentials on each attempt. Continue skipping already-published versions.
- Enable verbose npm logging and retain debug logs as artifacts for seven days, including on failure.
- Use `macos-15-intel` to verify provisioned `x86_64-apple-darwin` packages, while keeping `aarch64-apple-darwin` verification on `macos-15-xlarge`.

GitOrigin-RevId: 1876c66993ecd8cdb44088ab17a3363d21135ec4

- Migrate legacy declaration-only approvals to a shared, immutable content baseline per plugin and config home.
- Exclude generated Python bytecode, `.venv`, and `.egg-info` entries from fingerprints. Run app-server hook listing on blocking tasks.

## Testing

Extend integration coverage for plugin upgrades and rollbacks requiring approval, same-turn script changes preventing further hook execution, shared legacy approval baselines, and generated Python artifacts preserving trust.

commits.title: Preserve disconnect reasons in Noise handshake errors (#54637)
commits.message:
Preserve disconnect reasons in Noise handshake errors (#54637)

## Why

Noise handshake failures before connection readiness returned a generic error even when the transport had reported a specific disconnect reason. No `RpcClient` was reading the connection event channel at that point.

## What changed

Read the pending disconnect event when a Noise rendezvous handshake fails and append its reason to the handshake error when available.

## Testing

Add a regression test covering unexpected text frames and relay stream resets, checking that each produces the expected transport reason in the handshake error.

commits.title: Stream rollout records during thread history materialization (#54639)
commits.message:
Stream rollout records during thread history materialization (#54639)

## Why

Thread history materialization allocated a buffer for the entire unread rollout suffix before processing records, increasing memory use for large rollouts.

## What changed

Read records incrementally with a buffered reader bounded to the captured file end. Reuse the line buffer, preserve trailing partial records for the next pass, and report unexpected EOF if the rollout shrinks during reading.

## Testing

Extend the partial-line boundary test with 64 KiB of padding per record to verify byte offsets and deferred processing until the final newline is durable.

commits.title: Make remote-control conflict retry tests deterministic (#54647)

Make remote-control conflict retry tests deterministic (#54647)

## What changed

Wait for the rejected socket to close before advancing Tokio's clock through
capped retry delays. Keep socket I/O on real time so pending handshakes cannot

rejection restarts fast retries, and assert that recovery preserves the expected

commits.title: Prefer resource-specific scopes during MCP OAuth discovery (#54653)
commits.message:
Prefer resource-specific scopes during MCP OAuth discovery (#54653)

## Why

Authorization server metadata can advertise scopes unrelated to the MCP resource. Using that list for discovery can request broader scopes than the resource requires.

## What changed

Update `rmcp` and use its initial scope selection during OAuth discovery: prefer scopes from the initial `WWW-Authenticate` challenge, fall back to protected resource metadata, and include `offline_access` when supported. Stop using the authorization server's general scope list as the discovered resource scopes.

## Testing

Add coverage for challenge scope precedence, resource metadata fallback, scope normalization, and exclusion of unrelated authorization server scopes. Add a no-browser login regression test for a preregistered client whose authorization server advertises neither scopes nor dynamic registration.

commits.title: Allow dynamic tool calls to execute in parallel (#54654)
commits.message:
Allow dynamic tool calls to execute in parallel (#54654)

## Why

Dynamic tool calls should remain independent while waiting for client responses, so one pending call does not block another from reaching the client.

## What changed

Enable parallel execution in `DynamicToolHandler`, allowing code mode programs to issue concurrent dynamic tool calls with `Promise.all`.

## Testing

Add a code mode regression test that waits for two dynamic tool requests before responding, resolves them in reverse order, and verifies that `Promise.all` preserves the expected result order.

commits.title: Honor MCP tool-list changes within a turn (#54656)
commits.message:
Honor MCP tool-list changes within a turn (#54656)

## Why

MCP servers can expose new tools during discovery. Refreshing the catalog after a tool-list notification lets Codex discover and call those tools in the same turn.

## What changed

- Add the disabled-by-default `mcp_tool_list_changed` feature for ordinary MCP servers.
- Track notifications in transport order and refresh catalogs before subsequent discovery or tool binding. Coalesce concurrent refreshes and retry listings invalidated by notifications, including during pagination.
- Retain the previous catalog on refresh failure, apply a retry cooldown, and invalidate affected startup caches. Allow notification refreshes to proceed while admitted calls finish.

## Testing

Add coverage for same-turn discovery and invocation in direct and Code Mode, notifications during startup and pagination, disabled behavior, cache invalidation, and concurrent refreshes with timeout recovery.

## Testing

Add coverage for conservative SQLx error classification, mutation error mappings, session initialization categories, and shutdown diagnostics that omit raw error payloads.

commits.title: Add an opt-in tool for copying files between environments (#54674)

Add an opt-in tool for copying files between environments (#54674)

## What changed

Add the `codex-multi-env-copy-file` extension, exposing `multi_env_copy_file` when registered by the host. Copy files between distinct selected environments without loading their contents into model context, and return `bytes_copied` on completion.

Require absolute paths in each environment's native path convention and enforce each endpoint's sandbox policy and permission grants. Stream file contents where supported, with a buffered fallback for older executors. Reject same-environment copies and report I/O error kinds without exposing connection details. Warn that failed writes may leave a truncated or partially written target.

commits.title: Distinguish MCP approval cancellation reasons (#54679)
commits.message:
Distinguish MCP approval cancellation reasons (#54679)

## Why

MCP tool calls reported every aborted approval as "user cancelled MCP tool call", including interrupted requests and automatic cancellations in `exec` mode.

## What changed

Carry `user`, `interrupted`, or `non_interactive` cancellation reasons through MCP approval metadata and resolution. Mark explicit TUI cancellations as user actions, interrupted requests as interruptions, and automatic `exec` cancellations as non-interactive.

Use the reason to report when a call was cancelled before approval or because interactive approval is unavailable in `exec` mode. Preserve the existing cancellation message for clients that omit the reason.

## Testing

Update tests to verify that a closed approval response carries the interruption reason and that `exec` cancellation responses include the non-interactive reason.

commits.title: Keep TUI session selections bound to their backend (#54681)
commits.message:
Keep TUI session selections bound to their backend (#54681)

## Why

A thread ID alone does not identify the backend that owns a session. Resume and fork selections must retain that ownership across connection replacement so they cannot operate on another backend, even when thread IDs match.

## What changed

- Add a process-local `BackendId` to app-server sessions and session targets, preserving it across reconnects and auxiliary picker connections.
- Reject selections from a different backend before changing session state or sending resume, fork, or unarchive requests.
- Disable local-daemon fallback to an embedded server for auxiliary pickers and after selecting a session, while retaining fallback for fresh startup.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for foreign selections with matching thread IDs, startup resume and fork rejection before requests, shared ownership across picker connections, and fallback eligibility.

commits.title: Preserve MCP tool-list metadata in server status (#54686)
commits.message:
Preserve MCP tool-list metadata in server status (#54686)

## Why

MCP tool discovery discarded response-level `_meta`, leaving server-status clients unable to inspect metadata associated with the tool catalog.

## What changed

- Preserve opaque `_meta` from the first `tools/list` page through catalog refreshes and caches.
- Expose it as `toolListMeta` in `McpServerStatus`, with `null` when unavailable, and update generated schemas and bindings.
- Scope cached Apps catalog metadata to discovery settings, including client capabilities and extensions, while retaining tools from older caches without metadata.
- Restrict server capabilities in status snapshots to the selected servers.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for listing legacy cached Apps tools during failed startup, and update protocol serialization expectations for nullable `toolListMeta`.

commits.title: Honor home deletion preferences during Windows uninstall (#54708)
commits.message:
Honor home deletion preferences during Windows uninstall (#54708)

## What changed

Read `desktop.uninstall_codex_home` from the owner's current `config.toml` before recursively deleting a desktop-created Codex home during Windows sandbox uninstall.

- Preserve the home by default for ordinary installations; retain the deletion default for OEM preinstalls when no preference is set.
- Let an explicit boolean preference override either default. Preserve the home when configuration is unreadable, malformed, or contains an invalid preference.
- Capture OEM metadata before Windows removes it during uninstall, and revoke sandbox permissions on retained homes.

## Testing

Add unit tests for missing preferences, explicit overrides, malformed or invalid configuration, and configuration read failures across both installation defaults.

commits.title: Close arg0 lock files before removing temporary directories (#54739)
commits.message:
Close arg0 lock files before removing temporary directories (#54739)

## Why

Removing a directory while its lock file is open can leave `.nfs*` entries on NFS and prevent cleanup.

## What changed

- Drop the `Arg0PathEntryGuard` lock file before its temporary directory.
- On Unix, rename stale helper directories while locked, then close the lock before deleting them. This prevents initializers from publishing at the old path during cleanup.

## Testing

Extend the guard lifetime test to all platforms and assert that its directory is removed after main returns. Strengthen the janitor test to check that cleanup leaves the temporary root empty.

commits.message:

## What changed

- Display the leading `/` in the prompt marker instead of the editable text, sharing prefix state with shell mode's `!`.
- Preserve command prefixes and text element offsets across submission, queuing, history, and external editing. Keep prefixes literal in plain-text composers.

commits.message:

## Why

Schema strings and sequences do not grow after construction, and most schema nodes do not contain maps. Retaining collection capacity and inline optional maps adds unnecessary memory overhead.

## What changed

Distinguish retryable thread-store errors from unknown write outcomes (#54664)

## What changed

Add `ThreadStoreError::Retryable` for transient failures known to be safe to retry and `ThreadStoreError::OutcomeUnknown` for writes that may already have committed. Recovery remains the operation owner's responsibility; neither category automatically triggers retries.

Preserve existing app-server error mappings and fatal session startup behavior, and report the new categories in shutdown diagnostics without exposing raw error payloads.

## Testing

Add coverage for conservative SQLx error classification, mutation error mappings, session initialization categories, and shutdown diagnostics that omit raw error payloads.

commits.title: Add an opt-in tool for copying files between environments (#54674)
commits.message:
Add an opt-in tool for copying files between environments (#54674)

## What changed

Add the `codex-multi-env-copy-file` extension, exposing `multi_env_copy_file` when registered by the host. Copy files between distinct selected environments without loading their contents into model context, and return `bytes_copied` on completion.

Require absolute paths in each environment's native path convention and enforce each endpoint's sandbox policy and permission grants. Stream file contents where supported, with a buffered fallback for older executors. Reject same-environment copies and report I/O error kinds without exposing connection details. Warn that failed writes may leave a truncated or partially written target.

## Testing

Add integration tests for binary transfers in both directions, local and remote executors, path validation, opt-in tool visibility, endpoint permissions and grants, and unavailable or disconnected executors. Verify that copied contents stay outside model context.

commits.title: Distinguish MCP approval cancellation reasons (#54679)
commits.message:
Distinguish MCP approval cancellation reasons (#54679)

## Why

MCP tool calls reported every aborted approval as "user cancelled MCP tool call", including interrupted requests and automatic cancellations in `exec` mode.

## What changed

Carry `user`, `interrupted`, or `non_interactive` cancellation reasons through MCP approval metadata and resolution. Mark explicit TUI cancellations as user actions, interrupted requests as interruptions, and automatic `exec` cancellations as non-interactive.

Use the reason to report when a call was cancelled before approval or because interactive approval is unavailable in `exec` mode. Preserve the existing cancellation message for clients that omit the reason.

## Testing

Update tests to verify that a closed approval response carries the interruption reason and that `exec` cancellation responses include the non-interactive reason.

GitOrigin-RevId: be2a5f7fef539b5db2add53b46aea27e2b8a66fc

commits.title: Keep TUI session selections bound to their backend (#54681)
commits.message:
Keep TUI session selections bound to their backend (#54681)

## Why

A thread ID alone does not identify the backend that owns a session. Resume and fork selections must retain that ownership across connection replacement so they cannot operate on another backend, even when thread IDs match.

## What changed

- Add a process-local `BackendId` to app-server sessions and session targets, preserving it across reconnects and auxiliary picker connections.
- Reject selections from a different backend before changing session state or sending resume, fork, or unarchive requests.
- Disable local-daemon fallback to an embedded server for auxiliary pickers and after selecting a session, while retaining fallback for fresh startup.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for foreign selections with matching thread IDs, startup resume and fork rejection before requests, shared ownership across picker connections, and fallback eligibility.

GitOrigin-RevId: 05a3ca0a901a8dc24337d130548aa2c048b4d586

commits.title: Preserve MCP tool-list metadata in server status (#54686)
commits.message:
Preserve MCP tool-list metadata in server status (#54686)

## Why

MCP tool discovery discarded response-level `_meta`, leaving server-status clients unable to inspect metadata associated with the tool catalog.

## What changed

- Preserve opaque `_meta` from the first `tools/list` page through catalog refreshes and caches.
- Expose it as `toolListMeta` in `McpServerStatus`, with `null` when unavailable, and update generated schemas and bindings.
- Scope cached Apps catalog metadata to discovery settings, including client capabilities and extensions, while retaining tools from older caches without metadata.
- Restrict server capabilities in status snapshots to the selected servers.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for listing legacy cached Apps tools during failed startup, and update protocol serialization expectations for nullable `toolListMeta`.

commits.title: Honor home deletion preferences during Windows uninstall (#54708)
commits.message:
Honor home deletion preferences during Windows uninstall (#54708)

## What changed

Read `desktop.uninstall_codex_home` from the owner's current `config.toml` before recursively deleting a desktop-created Codex home during Windows sandbox uninstall.

- Preserve the home by default for ordinary installations; retain the deletion default for OEM preinstalls when no preference is set.
- Let an explicit boolean preference override either default. Preserve the home when configuration is unreadable, malformed, or contains an invalid preference.
- Capture OEM metadata before Windows removes it during uninstall, and revoke sandbox permissions on retained homes.

## Testing

Add unit tests for missing preferences, explicit overrides, malformed or invalid configuration, and configuration read failures across both installation defaults.

commits.title: Close arg0 lock files before removing temporary directories (#54739)
commits.message:
Close arg0 lock files before removing temporary directories (#54739)

## Why

Removing a directory while its lock file is open can leave `.nfs*` entries on NFS and prevent cleanup.

## What changed

- Drop the `Arg0PathEntryGuard` lock file before its temporary directory.
- On Unix, rename stale helper directories while locked, then close the lock before deleting them. This prevents initializers from publishing at the old path during cleanup.

## Testing

Extend the guard lifetime test to all platforms and assert that its directory is removed after main returns. Strengthen the janitor test to check that cleanup leaves the temporary root empty.

commits.title: Render slash command prefixes as composer prompt markers (#54742)
commits.message:
Render slash command prefixes as composer prompt markers (#54742)

## What changed

- Display the leading `/` in the prompt marker instead of the editable text, sharing prefix state with shell mode's `!`.
- Preserve command prefixes and text element offsets across submission, queuing, history, and external editing. Keep prefixes literal in plain-text composers.
- Track composer-owned slash command elements separately, omit them from exported draft elements, and refresh them when command availability changes.

Add regression coverage for slash prompt cursor placement, prefix deletion, history search highlighting, dynamic command availability, and Vim Replace restoration, including Unicode text. Update rendering snapshots for the slash prompt marker.

commits.title: Reduce memory overhead in tool JSON schemas (#54754)
commits.message:
Reduce memory overhead in tool JSON schemas (#54754)

## Why

Schema strings and sequences do not grow after construction, and most schema nodes do not contain maps. Retaining collection capacity and inline optional maps adds unnecessary memory overhead.

## What changed

Store `JsonSchema` strings and sequences as boxed strings and slices, and box optional property and definition maps. Adapt constructors, schema consumers, and existing test expectations to the new representation while preserving the serialized JSON Schema format.

commits.message:
Upgrade `zip` to 9.0.0 and update plugin archive extraction (#54761)

## Why

Curated plugin archives should preserve executable permissions without applying setuid, setgid, or sticky bits.

## What changed

- Upgrade `zip` from 2.4.2 to 9.0.0, retaining the previous feature set and selecting the existing `bzip2-sys` backend explicitly. Update the Cargo and Bazel lockfiles.
- Adapt plugin extraction to fallible entry names and apply Unix permissions through the open output file, using the mode filtered by `zip`.

## Testing

Add a Unix regression test that encodes special permission bits directly in an archive entry and verifies that the extracted file has mode `0o755`.

commits.title: Make remote-control conflict retry tests deterministic (#54647)
commits.message:
Make remote-control conflict retry tests deterministic (#54647)

## What changed

Wait for the rejected socket to close before advancing Tokio's clock through
capped retry delays. Keep socket I/O on real time so pending handshakes cannot
auto-advance their own timeouts.

commits.title: Prefer resource-specific scopes during MCP OAuth discovery (#54653)
commits.message:
Prefer resource-specific scopes during MCP OAuth discovery (#54653)

## Why

Authorization server metadata can advertise scopes unrelated to the MCP resource. Using that list for discovery can request broader scopes than the resource requires.

## What changed

Update `rmcp` and use its initial scope selection during OAuth discovery: prefer scopes from the initial `WWW-Authenticate` challenge, fall back to protected resource metadata, and include `offline_access` when supported. Stop using the authorization server's general scope list as the discovered resource scopes.

## Testing

Add coverage for challenge scope precedence, resource metadata fallback, scope normalization, and exclusion of unrelated authorization server scopes. Add a no-browser login regression test for a preregistered client whose authorization server advertises neither scopes nor dynamic registration.

commits.title: Allow dynamic tool calls to execute in parallel (#54654)
commits.message:
Allow dynamic tool calls to execute in parallel (#54654)

## Why

Dynamic tool calls should remain independent while waiting for client responses, so one pending call does not block another from reaching the client.

## What changed

Enable parallel execution in `DynamicToolHandler`, allowing code mode programs to issue concurrent dynamic tool calls with `Promise.all`.

## Testing

Add a code mode regression test that waits for two dynamic tool requests before responding, resolves them in reverse order, and verifies that `Promise.all` preserves the expected result order.

commits.title: Honor MCP tool-list changes within a turn (#54656)
commits.message:
Honor MCP tool-list changes within a turn (#54656)

## Why

MCP servers can expose new tools during discovery. Refreshing the catalog after a tool-list notification lets Codex discover and call those tools in the same turn.

## What changed

- Add the disabled-by-default `mcp_tool_list_changed` feature for ordinary MCP servers.
- Track notifications in transport order and refresh catalogs before subsequent discovery or tool binding. Coalesce concurrent refreshes and retry listings invalidated by notifications, including during pagination.
- Retain the previous catalog on refresh failure, apply a retry cooldown, and invalidate affected startup caches. Allow notification refreshes to proceed while admitted calls finish.

## Testing

Add coverage for same-turn discovery and invocation in direct and Code Mode, notifications during startup and pagination, disabled behavior, cache invalidation, and concurrent refreshes with timeout recovery.

commits.title: Keep TUI session selections bound to their backend (#54681)

Add regression coverage for foreign selections with matching thread IDs, startup resume and fork rejection before requests, shared ownership across picker connections, and fallback eligibility.

commits.title: Keep TUI session selections bound to their backend (#54681)

## Why

A thread ID alone does not identify the backend that owns a session. Resume and fork selections must retain that ownership across connection replacement so they cannot operate on another backend, even when thread IDs match.

## What changed

- Add a process-local `BackendId` to app-server sessions and session targets, preserving it across reconnects and auxiliary picker connections.
- Reject selections from a different backend before changing session state or sending resume, fork, or unarchive requests.
- Disable local-daemon fallback to an embedded server for auxiliary pickers and after selecting a session, while retaining fallback for fresh startup.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for foreign selections with matching thread IDs, startup resume and fork rejection before requests, shared ownership across picker connections, and fallback eligibility.

commits.title: Add an opt-in tool for copying files between environments (#54674)

Add an opt-in tool for copying files between environments (#54674)

## What changed

commits.title: Distinguish MCP approval cancellation reasons (#54679)
commits.message:
Distinguish MCP approval cancellation reasons (#54679)

## Why

MCP tool calls reported every aborted approval as "user cancelled MCP tool call", including interrupted requests and automatic cancellations in `exec` mode.

## What changed

Carry `user`, `interrupted`, or `non_interactive` cancellation reasons through MCP approval metadata and resolution. Mark explicit TUI cancellations as user actions, interrupted requests as interruptions, and automatic `exec` cancellations as non-interactive.

Use the reason to report when a call was cancelled before approval or because interactive approval is unavailable in `exec` mode. Preserve the existing cancellation message for clients that omit the reason.

## Testing

Update tests to verify that a closed approval response carries the interruption reason and that `exec` cancellation responses include the non-interactive reason.

commits.title: Keep TUI session selections bound to their backend (#54681)
commits.message:
Keep TUI session selections bound to their backend (#54681)

## Why

A thread ID alone does not identify the backend that owns a session. Resume and fork selections must retain that ownership across connection replacement so they cannot operate on another backend, even when thread IDs match.

## What changed

- Add a process-local `BackendId` to app-server sessions and session targets, preserving it across reconnects and auxiliary picker connections.
- Reject selections from a different backend before changing session state or sending resume, fork, or unarchive requests.
- Disable local-daemon fallback to an embedded server for auxiliary pickers and after selecting a session, while retaining fallback for fresh startup.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for foreign selections with matching thread IDs, startup resume and fork rejection before requests, shared ownership across picker connections, and fallback eligibility.

Add regression coverage for listing legacy cached Apps tools during failed startup, and update protocol serialization expectations for nullable `toolListMeta`.

Removing a directory while its lock file is open can leave `.nfs*` entries on NFS and prevent cleanup.

Unknown fields in TUI keymaps and profile TUI settings fail deserialization even when strict config validation is disabled.

commits.title: Support typed content in contextual prompt fragments (#54776)
commits.message:
Support typed content in contextual prompt fragments (#54776)

## Why

Contextual fragments and extension-owned world-state sections currently return strings, limiting them to text content.

## What changed

- Return `ContentItem` from fragment bodies and rendering, preserving classification and attribution. Apply text markers only to `InputText`; pass other content through unchanged.
- Allow extension prompt and world-state contributions to carry typed content, and preserve media in context-window hints.
- Hash non-text world-state fragments by their serialized content and role while retaining the existing text hashing behavior.
- Add shared content-to-tool-output conversion that preserves image references, image detail, and audio.

## Testing

Add coverage for typed world-state hashing and preservation of image content and attribution. Expand code-mode output tests to cover input text, output text, file-backed and inline images, and audio.

commits.title: Add negotiated zstd compression to app-server WebSockets (#54930)
commits.message:
Add negotiated zstd compression to app-server WebSockets (#54930)

## What changed

- Negotiate compression over TCP and local sockets with `x-codex-app-server-compression: zstd-stream-v1`. Keep JSON text messages when compression is not negotiated.
- Send compressed JSON as binary messages, retaining a separate zstd stream per direction across messages. Export reusable negotiation and codec helpers.
- Limit decompressed messages to 64 MiB and compression windows to 1 MiB. Close compressed connections on decoding errors or unexpected text messages.
- Add audit and deny ignores for the unmaintained `zvariant`, `zbus_names`, and `zvariant_derive` versions pulled in through `zbus`.

## Testing

Add codec tests for retained history, fallback, size limits, malformed data, and oversized compression windows. Add TCP and local-socket round-trip tests covering negotiation, persistent streams, and ping/pong handling, plus TCP fallback for absent or unsupported offers.

commits.title: Share additional tool declarations across response item clones (#54945)
commits.message:
Share additional tool declarations across response item clones (#54945)

## Why

Cloning `ResponseItem::AdditionalTools` deep-copies its tool declarations for history and request copies.

## What changed

Store `tools` in an `Arc<[serde_json::Value]>` so clones share immutable declarations. Update constructors and existing test fixtures to use the shared representation.

commits.title: Preserve model catalog caches across header credential rotation (#54946)
commits.message:
Preserve model catalog caches across header credential rotation (#54946)

## Why

Rotating header credentials should not discard the model catalog when a stable account ID is available.

## What changed

- Use the account ID from `CodexAuth::Headers` instead of opaque auth headers in the catalog cache identity. Provider settings remain part of the key.
- Retain credential-sensitive keys when the account ID is missing or the provider uses an explicit API key, bearer token, or command auth.
- Document that hosts using header auth must isolate model managers and cache storage by user and catalog-varying request context, since an account ID can represent a shared workspace.

## Testing

Update the auth-rotation test fixture to omit stable account metadata, preserving coverage for catalog invalidation when opaque credentials change.

commits.title: Gate app-server WebSocket compression behind a feature flag (#54949)
commits.message:
Gate app-server WebSocket compression behind a feature flag (#54949)

## What changed

Add `features.app_server_websocket_compression`, disabled by default. TCP WebSocket and Unix-domain socket listeners now negotiate zstd compression only when the feature is enabled and the client offers the supported protocol. Otherwise, connections use plain text messages.

Include the feature in the configuration schema and allow its override during TUI daemon startup.

## Testing

Extend transport tests to cover enabled and disabled compression with supported, unsupported, and absent client offers on both transports. Add an app-server integration test that verifies startup configuration controls negotiation and the message format used for initialization responses.
