commits.title: Allow agent messages to wake idle root sessions behind a feature flag (#54961)
commits.message:
Allow agent messages to wake idle root sessions behind a feature flag (#54961)

## Why

A worker can finish after its parent has returned a final answer. Agent messages without `trigger_turn` previously needed an outstanding durable sleep to wake an idle session.

## What changed

Add the disabled-by-default `wake_on_agent_messages` feature to start a new root turn when agent mail arrives through direct delivery or the host mailbox. Reuse the previous turn context for messages without `trigger_turn`. Keep these automatic wakes disabled for interrupted sessions, Plan mode, and child agents.

## Testing

Add coverage for both delivery paths waking a completed root exactly once, child completion waking a parent after its final answer, and the interruption, Plan mode, and child-agent boundaries.

commits.title: Add observation-only model request lifecycle hooks (#55144)
commits.message:
Add observation-only model request lifecycle hooks (#55144)

## What changed

- Add `PreModelRequest` and `PostModelRequest` hooks around model request attempts, including retries. Pass model, session, turn, and optional subagent context; report completion, failure, or cancellation with errors and token usage when available.
- Treat hook output as diagnostic data without allowing it to veto requests or alter model context. Wait for synchronous post-request hooks before dispatching tools, while asynchronous hooks allow streaming tool dispatch to continue.
- Apply memory-consolidation hook filtering and expose the new events through configuration, protocol schemas, generated clients, and the hooks browser.

## Testing

Add integration coverage for failures and retries, ignored control directives, cancellation, synchronous and asynchronous tool ordering, interrupted-turn resume and token accounting, and memory-consolidation filtering. Update hook schema fixtures and hooks browser snapshots.

commits.title: Prune unused standalone releases after successful installation (#55149)
commits.message:
Prune unused standalone releases after successful installation (#55149)

## What changed

Clean up older standalone releases after verifying the installed command, while holding the install lock. Retain the current and previously selected releases, along with releases used by running Codex processes or bundled helpers.

Record selection history for all standalone installs and preserve it on no-op installs. Only remove validated, installer-owned release directories; skip cleanup when filesystem or process inspection cannot establish that removal is safe. Recheck process usage after moving a release aside and restore it if it is in use.

## Testing

Add installer regression coverage for running helpers, helpers started during cleanup, repeated installs, failed installs, downgrades, and preservation of unowned directories and symlinks.

commits.title: Bucket admitted Guardian request metrics by input size (#55226)
commits.message:
Bucket admitted Guardian request metrics by input size (#55226)

## Why

Guardian request counts grouped by input size should reflect admitted sampling inputs without counting synchronous transport retries more than once.

## What changed

- Add a shared `token_bucket` label to admitted total-input observations in `codex.guardian.context.request_tokens` for synchronous and asynchronous reviews. Use inclusive upper bounds in 20k-token steps through 240k, followed by 256k and overflow buckets.
- Record synchronous request tokens after budget admission, once per sampling step, including the complete input. A fresh step counts again even when its input is identical.
- Preserve asynchronous component histograms for oversized classifications, but omit `token_bucket` so rejected inputs do not contribute to counts grouped by that label.

## Testing

Add coverage for bucket boundaries, synchronous retry deduplication and budget rejection, asynchronous retained-history reuse and reset, and admitted versus oversized classification metrics.

commits.title: Batch thread history materialization into SQLite (#55244)
commits.message:
Batch thread history materialization into SQLite (#55244)

## Why

History catch-up collected the entire durable rollout prefix before applying it in one SQLite transaction. Large rollouts therefore required buffering all projection steps and committing them together.

## What changed

Stream projection batches through a bounded queue and commit each batch with its checkpoint. Flush between complete records after reaching 1 MiB of source data or 256 projection steps, keeping ordinal gaps with their following records and allowing oversized records to remain intact.

Wait for batches before opening SQLite transactions so an idle reader does not hold the writer. Preserve committed progress across later failures or cancellation, allowing retries to resume from the last checkpoint.

## Testing

Add coverage for reader and writer failures under backpressure, atomic batch rollback, retries without replaying committed records, and unrelated writes while projection is paused. Verify that producer disconnection and consumer cancellation retain committed progress.

commits.title: Preserve rollout access metadata across compression and restoration (#55252)
commits.message:
Preserve rollout access metadata across compression and restoration (#55252)

## Why

Replacing rollout files can lose Unix ownership or macOS ACLs, changing who can read or append to a transcript. An ACL can also permit appending while denying explicit timestamp updates.

## What changed

- Preserve Unix ownership, permissions, modification times, and macOS ACLs before publishing compressed or restored rollouts, and verify the replacement can be reopened.
- Abort replacement on metadata failures, reject macOS delete-deny ACLs to keep temporary files removable, and detect Unix access metadata changes through `ctime` checks.
- Use managed restoration temporary files whose names avoid stale `*.tmp` cleanup.
- Allow appending when refreshing the rollout's modification time returns `PermissionDenied`.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for macOS ACL preservation, inherited ACL removal, deletion-protected rollouts, append access despite denied timestamp changes, Unix group preservation, and restoration temporary files surviving stale-file cleanup.

## Why

Dual-write prepares v2 memories while v1 is selected. Once v2 is selected, running the v1 pipeline is no longer needed.

## What changed

commits.title: Start dormant MCP servers for hook calls (#55263)
commits.message:
Start dormant MCP servers for hook calls (#55263)

## Why

MCP tool hooks need to invoke model-hidden tools even when a subagent's cached server has not started. Their timeout must also cover server startup.

## What changed

- Let cached servers with allowed model-hidden tools remain dormant until called.
- Wait for the selected server when executing an MCP hook, leaving unrelated cached servers dormant, and apply the hook timeout to the entire operation.
- Capture tool namespace attribution after startup and retain it only while catalog revisions remain unchanged.
- Validate the server, environment, and tool filter before starting a server or capturing attribution.

## Testing

Extend integration coverage for cached subagent hooks under both startup readiness modes, startup timeouts without context injection, and namespace attribution for hook and token-budget context while keeping tools hidden from the model. Verify that a direct call starts a cached server whose tools are hidden from model exposure.

commits.message:

## What changed

Look up metadata directly in the active catalog for both remote and static model managers. Share catalog selection across remote catalog accessors and metadata lookup, preserving auth identity checks, API-key discovery policy, provider matching rules, and configuration overrides.

Extend coverage for custom catalog configuration overrides, metadata fallback after disabling API-key discovery, and fallback after an auth identity change.

commits.title: Honor per-thread unload delays in app-server (#55270)
commits.message:
Honor per-thread unload delays in app-server (#55270)

## Why

Thread unload timing used the server-wide delay, ignoring per-thread configuration overrides. Clients need to control how long individual idle, unsubscribed threads remain loaded.

## What changed

- Resolve unload timing from each loaded thread's `thread_unload_delay_secs` configuration. Setting it to `0` allows immediate unloading once the thread has no subscribers or activity.
- Allow this runtime retention override in `experimentalPredictionMode` forks while continuing to reject other configuration overrides. Reject negative values and delays too large to schedule.
- Replace the source-specific immediate-unload behavior with explicit configuration.

## Testing

Extend integration coverage for per-thread delays, unloading after active turns finish, fork overrides, and invalid prediction-fork delays. Verify that immediate unloading preserves persistent history and that cold resumes and ordinary nested forks use their default delay instead of retaining the previous runtime's override.

commits.title: Stabilize daemon reconnect and Rosetta package startup tests (#55274)
commits.message:
Stabilize daemon reconnect and Rosetta package startup tests (#55274)

## Why

A replacement daemon PID can appear before the TUI observes the disconnect, allowing stale UI content to make the startup test advance too early. Cold Rosetta translation can also consume the startup deadlines for freshly extracted Intel macOS packages on Apple Silicon.

## What changed

- Wait for the reconnect transcript clear before sending `/status` in the daemon startup test.
- Warm both packaged CLI and app-server entrypoints with `--help` when testing `x86_64-apple-darwin` packages on `arm64` hosts. Give each warmup 180 seconds and fail fixture setup if either entrypoint cannot run.

commits.title: Fall back when macOS rejects high stdio descriptors (#55278)
commits.message:
Fall back when macOS rejects high stdio descriptors (#55278)

## Why

On macOS, spawn file actions reject valid descriptors at or above `OPEN_MAX` even when `RLIMIT_NOFILE` permits them. This can prevent child processes from starting when their stdio descriptors exceed that limit.

## What changed

Use the compatibility backend when `posix_spawn_file_actions_adddup2` returns `EBADF` for stdio setup and `SpawnFallback::Compatible` is enabled. Preserve the error for `SpawnFallback::ReturnError`.

## Testing

Add a macOS regression test that forces high stdio descriptors and checks strict-mode errors, fallback stdio and exit status, process groups, and descriptor isolation without changing the parent's descriptor.

commits.title: Track MCP enterprise auth cancellation across config reloads (#55287)
commits.message:
Track MCP enterprise auth cancellation across config reloads (#55287)

## Why

Configuration loading can finish before a pending startup is visible to the thread manager. Reloads need a cancellation scope that also covers these configuration snapshots.

## What changed

- Capture an enterprise managed authentication (EMA) cancellation token before loading configuration and carry it through config layers, role overrides, runtime refreshes, and `McpConfig`.
- Cancel the previous scope on MCP or user configuration reloads and cloud config loader changes, then create a fresh scope for subsequent loads.
- Cancel the session's token when enterprise MCP authentication is disabled or a refresh leaves it unavailable.

## Testing

Extend the MCP reload test to verify that existing thread and pending startup tokens are cancelled while a fresh startup receives an uncancelled token.

commits.title: Recheck EMA request authority at HTTP boundaries (#55288)
commits.message:
Recheck EMA request authority at HTTP boundaries (#55288)

## Why

Authorization can change during token renewal before a revocation watcher runs. Requests must check that their authority is still current before dispatch.

## What changed

- Let `EmaRequestAuthority` accept a cancellation token and a synchronous authority check, revoking itself when the check fails.
- Recheck authority after authentication and after receiving HTTP responses for both regular and streaming requests.
- Add `CloudConfigBundleBinding::invalidated()` to wait until a captured policy binding is no longer current.

## Testing

Update tests to cover ownership changing during token renewal without explicit revocation, preventing HTTP dispatch, and parent-token cancellation ending an existing response stream.

commits.title: Keep only the latest adjacent reasoning effort update in requests (#55293)
commits.message:
Keep only the latest adjacent reasoning effort update in requests (#55293)

## Why

Turn recovery and retries after a server overload can leave consecutive reasoning effort updates in history when settings change without an intervening message. Requests should use the latest update in each consecutive run.

## What changed

Coalesce adjacent `configuration_update` items when building Responses requests with reasoning effort overrides enabled, retaining the latest update. Preserve saved history and updates separated by other input items.

## Testing

Extend integration coverage for recovery with unchanged or changed effort, retries after a server overload, and WebSocket continuation and replay after coalescing. Verify that requests retain the latest adjacent update while saved history keeps all updates.

commits.message:

## What changed

Introduce a shared `Auth` abstraction that supplies sensitive authorization headers and the client's redirect policy. Preserve the existing static API key allocation and default redirect behavior, and return an empty `502` response if header acquisition fails.

Unify the stdin authentication entry point around platform-specific `read_from_stdin` helpers.

commits.title: Add GitHub Actions OIDC token acquisition to the responses API proxy (#55297)
commits.message:
Add GitHub Actions OIDC token acquisition to the responses API proxy (#55297)

## What changed

Add a `GithubOidc` implementation of `SubjectTokenSource` that requests a fresh token using a bearer credential read from stdin. Validate HTTPS request URLs and replace the audience query parameter while preserving other parameters. CLI integration is not included.

Add a token HTTP client that disables redirects and request logging, applies timeouts, and bounds response bodies. Keep token response buffers in zeroizing storage and exclude credentials, request URLs, and response bodies from errors.

Generalize the locked stdin credential reader for bounded OIDC bearer tokens while preserving API key validation.

## Testing

Add tests for fresh token acquisition, short reads, credential size limits, injection rejection, redirect refusal, and credential-safe errors and logs. Extend API key tests to retain the stricter character restrictions.

commits.title: Add renewable federated auth primitives to the Responses API proxy (#55298)
commits.message:
Add renewable federated auth primitives to the Responses API proxy (#55298)

## What changed

Add a federated `Auth` variant that exchanges JWT subject tokens for OpenAI access tokens using identity provider and service account IDs. Serialize concurrent exchanges, cache credentials, and renew proactively with a fresh subject token.

Validate token types, bearer credentials, payload sizes, and lifetimes. Bound caching by both relative and absolute expiry, discard cached credentials before renewal, and disable redirects for federated requests. Keep credential buffers zeroizing and diagnostics free of secrets.

## Testing

Add HTTP fixture tests for concurrent cache reuse, renewal with fresh subjects, expiry across host suspension, failed renewal, oversized payloads, invalid subjects, and unsupported or missing issued token types.

commits.title: Refresh rejected proxy credentials and back off failed renewals (#55299)
commits.message:
Refresh rejected proxy credentials and back off failed renewals (#55299)

## Why

The Responses API proxy could reuse a federated credential after an upstream `401`, and concurrent requests could each retry a failed token exchange.

## What changed

- Invalidate the rejected credential so the next request obtains a fresh token. Forward the `401` without replaying the request or waiting for an ongoing renewal; leave credentials intact on `403`.
- Track rejection per token issuance so a late `401` cannot invalidate a newer credential.
- Back off failed exchanges exponentially from 1 to 30 seconds, starting when the exchange fails. Reject requests during backoff without reusing the old token, and reset the delay after a successful exchange.

## Testing

Add tests for response forwarding without replay, late and concurrent rejections, shared renewal failures, backoff timing and reset, and credential-safe renewal errors without following redirects.

commits.title: Add one-shot app-server startup configuration discovery (#55300)
commits.message:
Add one-shot app-server startup configuration discovery (#55300)

## What changed

Add `codex app-server --print-startup-config` to validate local and cloud-backed configuration and emit the app-server version and configuration requirements as JSON without initializing environments, thread storage, or plugins. Configuration failures produce structured JSON errors and a nonzero exit status.

Support `--startup-sign-out` to remove account credentials and reload signed-out requirements, including recovery when cloud policy is unavailable. Reject sign-out for host-owned external authentication. Accept `--startup-client-info` to identify configuration and authentication requests.

Reuse configuration loading and account cleanup logic between startup discovery and the running app server.

## Testing

Add CLI integration coverage for configuration validation, project login restrictions, managed cloud requirements and failures, sign-out recovery, external authentication protection, and independence from locked or invalid history databases.

## What changed

- Use V2 discovery inventories for plugin MCP contributions when supplied, including empty or failed inventories; retain legacy discovery when no V2 snapshot is supplied.
- Merge plugins by canonical identity, using cloud metadata and enablement for remote plugins and attaching executor installations only when versions match. Preserve configured executor-local plugins and executor enablement when cloud data is unavailable.
- Keep installation order stable across refreshes and run merged MCP declarations on the first retained executor installation while preserving attribution for the others.
- Carry local and remote identities through selected-plugin snapshots, skill attribution, and active-plugin telemetry. Track disabled plugin IDs alongside disabled roots.
- Preserve a complete cloud catalog when a partial refresh arrives, and cap tool-description plugin attribution at 1,024 bytes while retaining all plugin associations.

## Testing

commits.title: Route skill reads by alias source (#55303)
commits.message:
Route skill reads by alias source (#55303)

## Why

Skill aliases already identify their source, but `skills.read` searched the cloud catalog before the executor catalog even for executor aliases.

## What changed

Parse package locators to recognize cloud (`c0/...`), executor (`e0/...`), and host (`r0/...`) aliases. Restrict cloud and executor alias lookups to the matching catalog, while retaining the existing search order for other package strings.

Share the source-to-prefix mapping between alias generation and parsing, and preserve the string representation and tool schema for package locators.

## Testing

## Why

The Responses API proxy could reuse a federated credential after an upstream `401`, and concurrent requests could each retry a failed token exchange.

## What changed

- Invalidate the rejected credential so the next request obtains a fresh token. Forward the `401` without replaying the request or waiting for an ongoing renewal; leave credentials intact on `403`.

- Back off failed exchanges exponentially from 1 to 30 seconds, starting when the exchange fails. Reject requests during backoff without reusing the old token, and reset the delay after a successful exchange.

commits.message:

## Why

The Responses API proxy could reuse a federated credential after an upstream `401`, and concurrent requests could each retry a failed token exchange.

## What changed

- Invalidate the rejected credential so the next request obtains a fresh token. Forward the `401` without replaying the request or waiting for an ongoing renewal; leave credentials intact on `403`.
- Track rejection per token issuance so a late `401` cannot invalidate a newer credential.
- Back off failed exchanges exponentially from 1 to 30 seconds, starting when the exchange fails. Reject requests during backoff without reusing the old token, and reset the delay after a successful exchange.

## Testing

commits.message:
Add configured thread environment inheritance for subagents (#55327)

## Why

Temporary environment attachments for a parent's turn should not become a child's persistent environment configuration or survive child eviction.

## What changed

- Add the default-disabled `subagent_thread_environments` feature flag. When enabled, subagents inherit configured thread environments captured with the spawning step instead of active turn selections.
- Track configured bindings separately from turn attachments, preserving pending configuration ownership when turn selections change.
- Retain configured bindings across child eviction and reload, excluding temporary attachments. Preserve the child's workspace when the parent switches workspaces, while enforcing current roots and permissions when the parent still configures the same workspace.

## Testing

Extend coverage for both multi-agent versions, forked children, empty configured environments, pending configuration, and legacy inheritance. Add eviction and reload cases covering temporary attachments, workspace changes, deferred executor startup, and permission validation.

commits.title: Expose skill installations and stabilize package aliases (#55330)
commits.message:
Expose skill installations and stabilize package aliases (#55330)

## Why

A skill can be available from Cloud and multiple executor environments. Reading its instructions needs to expose where supporting files live and allow discovery of locations omitted by response limits. Package aliases also need to keep identifying the same roots as catalogs change.

## What changed

- With executor capability discovery V2, add `skills.installations` to list enabled locations with source filtering and pagination, without reading skill contents.
- Let `skills.read` select Cloud or a specific executor environment through `source`. Return bounded installation metadata and an `installations_truncated` flag so callers can retrieve omitted locations.
- Share bounded, append-only alias assignments between catalog rendering and tools within a live thread. Preserve each step's alias snapshot and render only root mappings used by its catalog entries.
- Use discovery-root metadata when constructing executor skill locators, with a fallback when it is absent. Preserve the legacy read response and tool set outside discovery V2.

## Testing

Add coverage for installation filtering and pagination, response budgets, source-specific reads and cursors, and alias stability across catalog and plugin changes. Add an end-to-end scenario that discovers an omitted installation and reads its instructions from the selected environment.

commits.message:
Handle response body failures in OpenAI docs downloads (#55379)

## Why

Response body reads could outlive the manual download timeout or fail outside the existing fallback and retry handlers.

## What changed

- Read successful manual response bodies within the fetch timeout and transport fallback so stalled or failed reads fall back to `curl`. Leave `HEAD` responses unconsumed.
- Await model metadata response bodies inside the retry handler so read failures use the existing three-attempt retry loop.

## Testing

Add regression tests for manual body timeouts and truncated bodies falling back to `curl` before caching, plus model metadata body failures succeeding on retry or stopping after three attempts. All four tests pass with `node --test codex-rs/skills/tests/openai_docs_downloads.test.mjs`.

commits.title: Preserve thread metadata before rollout files are materialized (#55380)
commits.message:
Preserve thread metadata before rollout files are materialized (#55380)

## Why

A live thread can have updated SQLite metadata before its rollout file exists.
Reading metadata from the missing file loses creation details such as fork and
parent relationships and triggers unnecessary filesystem discovery and retries.

## What changed

- Read deferred `SessionMeta` through the rollout writer, ordered with persistence.
  Return no in-memory metadata once the rollout is materialized or resumed.
- Combine that creation metadata with SQLite metadata for reads that exclude
  history, and use it to determine the canonical history mode during updates.
- Keep untouched threads without a stored record unavailable for fork and resume.

## Testing

Add coverage for metadata reads and updates before persistence in both legacy and
paginated history modes, including equality with metadata read after persistence.
Verify the recorder exposes creation metadata only while deferred, and expand
fork/resume rejection tests across history modes and resume turn inclusion.

Reject replaceable symlinks in pre-sandbox executable lookup (#55384)

## Why

A read-only executable target does not make its lookup path trustworthy: a symlink or ancestor directory may still be replaceable through writes allowed by the filesystem policy.

## What changed

Check the original lookup path, resolved parent aliases, and canonical target before selecting a pre-sandbox executable such as `bwrap`. Account for sticky directory ownership when deciding whether a child can be replaced, while preserving read-only mount carveouts.

Resolve `PATH` entries individually, including relative entries when the working directory contains a colon.

Add regression tests for writable symlinks to read-only executables and symlinked search directories into writable roots. Extend search-path coverage to relative entries and a working directory containing a colon, and update the protected system installation test to use a direct executable path.

commits.title: Record OAuth provenance and login identity for account tokens (#55397)
commits.message:
Record OAuth provenance and login identity for account tokens (#55397)

## Why

Token refresh needs the issuer and client ID used at login. Unverified token claims cannot establish that authority, and OAuth error bodies may echo credentials.

## What changed

- Save `oauth_provenance` and a new `login_owner_id` on browser and device-code login. Preserve the login identifier through token rotation.
- Refresh using the recorded issuer and client ID, retaining the existing endpoint override and fallback behavior for legacy records. Clear provenance when an override changes the endpoint or when a response without token rotation encounters a concurrently replaced refresh token.
- Keep both metadata fields optional for older records without inferring provenance from token claims.
- Remove backend token error details from structured logs and refresh error messages.
- Box large futures in token refresh, MCP initialization, and embedded app-server test startup to reduce surrounding async frame sizes.

## Testing

Add coverage for legacy record compatibility and metadata round trips, browser and device-code login persistence, refresh using recorded OAuth settings, metadata preservation through rotation, and provenance clearing for a superseded refresh token.

commits.title: Retry TUI startup after a server shutdown refusal (#55409)
commits.message:
Retry TUI startup after a server shutdown refusal (#55409)

## Why

A remote server can refuse the initial `thread/start` while shutting down. An explicit refusal establishes that no thread was created, allowing the TUI to retry without risking duplicate startup submissions.

## What changed

- Wait for the draining connection to close, reconnect within a shared two-minute deadline, and retry startup once.
- Preserve the initial prompt, confirmed draft, model, and reasoning effort across recovery. Keep drafts editable and allow cancellation of a pending submission.
- Restore input without submitting if recovery fails or startup is refused again. Continue treating a lost startup reply as uncertain and avoid automatic resubmission.

## Testing

## Why

A new OAuth login can belong to the same account as an earlier session, while token refreshes can change credentials within one session. Auth consumers need to distinguish these cases when deciding whether a runtime can be reused.

## What changed

- Add `source_generation` to `AuthChangeState` and expose `AuthManager::auth_change_state_for` to check whether selected credentials still match the manager's current source.
- Preserve source continuity across OAuth refreshes only when session, issuer, and identity claims match. Advance the source revision for new sessions, credential replacements, and logout.
- Keep agent identity persistence from replacing cached credentials with credentials read from disk; credential publication remains managed by `AuthManager`.

## Testing

Add tests for refresh continuity, new logins, identity and workspace changes, sessionless tokens, API key replacement, logout, and identity persistence followed by an explicit credential reload.

commits.title: Check daemon feature overrides and prompt for mismatch recovery (#55442)
commits.message:
Check daemon feature overrides and prompt for mismatch recovery (#55442)

## Why

A fixed feature allowlist excluded other boolean feature overrides from daemon use. Feature mismatches could also silently fall back to embedded mode, while automatic startup could persist enabled overrides without confirmation.

## What changed

- Allow boolean feature overrides without a fixed allowlist and compare explicit overrides with the daemon's reported settings. Ignore removed features, treat unreported features as disabled, and include only mismatches in restart settings.
- Preserve saved daemon settings during automatic startup. Prompt on feature mismatches even when embedded fallback is allowed, letting users run without the daemon, confirm a managed-daemon restart, or cancel.

commits.title: Preserve thread metadata before rollout files are materialized (#55380)
commits.message:
Preserve thread metadata before rollout files are materialized (#55380)

## Why

A live thread can have updated SQLite metadata before its rollout file exists.
Reading metadata from the missing file loses creation details such as fork and
parent relationships and triggers unnecessary filesystem discovery and retries.

## What changed

- Read deferred `SessionMeta` through the rollout writer, ordered with persistence.
  Return no in-memory metadata once the rollout is materialized or resumed.
- Combine that creation metadata with SQLite metadata for reads that exclude
  history, and use it to determine the canonical history mode during updates.
- Keep untouched threads without a stored record unavailable for fork and resume.

## Testing

Add coverage for metadata reads and updates before persistence in both legacy and
paginated history modes, including equality with metadata read after persistence.
Verify the recorder exposes creation metadata only while deferred, and expand
fork/resume rejection tests across history modes and resume turn inclusion.

## Why

A read-only executable target does not make its lookup path trustworthy: a symlink or ancestor directory may still be replaceable through writes allowed by the filesystem policy.

## What changed

Check the original lookup path, resolved parent aliases, and canonical target before selecting a pre-sandbox executable such as `bwrap`. Account for sticky directory ownership when deciding whether a child can be replaced, while preserving read-only mount carveouts.

Resolving a history page's rollout lineage performs a separate filesystem lookup for each ancestor. Ancestors stored alongside the current rollout can share a lookup traversal.

commits.title: Record OAuth provenance and login identity for account tokens (#55397)
commits.message:
Record OAuth provenance and login identity for account tokens (#55397)

## Why

Token refresh needs the issuer and client ID used at login. Unverified token claims cannot establish that authority, and OAuth error bodies may echo credentials.

## What changed

- Save `oauth_provenance` and a new `login_owner_id` on browser and device-code login. Preserve the login identifier through token rotation.
- Refresh using the recorded issuer and client ID, retaining the existing endpoint override and fallback behavior for legacy records. Clear provenance when an override changes the endpoint or when a response without token rotation encounters a concurrently replaced refresh token.
- Keep both metadata fields optional for older records without inferring provenance from token claims.
- Remove backend token error details from structured logs and refresh error messages.
- Box large futures in token refresh, MCP initialization, and embedded app-server test startup to reduce surrounding async frame sizes.

## Testing

Add coverage for legacy record compatibility and metadata round trips, browser and device-code login persistence, refresh using recorded OAuth settings, metadata preservation through rotation, and provenance clearing for a superseded refresh token.

commits.title: Retry TUI startup after a server shutdown refusal (#55409)
commits.message:
Retry TUI startup after a server shutdown refusal (#55409)

## Why

A remote server can refuse the initial `thread/start` while shutting down. An explicit refusal establishes that no thread was created, allowing the TUI to retry without risking duplicate startup submissions.

## What changed

- Wait for the draining connection to close, reconnect within a shared two-minute deadline, and retry startup once.
- Preserve the initial prompt, confirmed draft, model, and reasoning effort across recovery. Keep drafts editable and allow cancellation of a pending submission.
- Restore input without submitting if recovery fails or startup is refused again. Continue treating a lost startup reply as uncertain and avoid automatic resubmission.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for successful reconnection with exactly one prompt submission, repeated refusal, disconnect event ordering, and draft cancellation, editing, and paste provenance during recovery.

- Add `source_generation` to `AuthChangeState` and expose `AuthManager::auth_change_state_for` to check whether selected credentials still match the manager's current source.
- Preserve source continuity across OAuth refreshes only when session, issuer, and identity claims match. Advance the source revision for new sessions, credential replacements, and logout.
- Keep agent identity persistence from replacing cached credentials with credentials read from disk; credential publication remains managed by `AuthManager`.

## Testing

Add tests for refresh continuity, new logins, identity and workspace changes, sessionless tokens, API key replacement, logout, and identity persistence followed by an explicit credential reload.

A read-only executable target does not make its lookup path trustworthy: a symlink or ancestor directory may still be replaceable through writes allowed by the filesystem policy.

## What changed

Check the original lookup path, resolved parent aliases, and canonical target before selecting a pre-sandbox executable such as `bwrap`. Account for sticky directory ownership when deciding whether a child can be replaced, while preserving read-only mount carveouts.

Cancelled or timed-out Guardian reviews can admit transcript evidence without completing a review. Reusing that session can leave subsequent reviews without the evidence they need.

Resolving a history page's rollout lineage performs a separate filesystem lookup for each ancestor. Ancestors stored alongside the current rollout can share a lookup traversal.

commits.title: Record OAuth provenance and login identity for account tokens (#55397)
commits.message:
Record OAuth provenance and login identity for account tokens (#55397)

## Why

Token refresh needs the issuer and client ID used at login. Unverified token claims cannot establish that authority, and OAuth error bodies may echo credentials.

## What changed

- Save `oauth_provenance` and a new `login_owner_id` on browser and device-code login. Preserve the login identifier through token rotation.
- Refresh using the recorded issuer and client ID, retaining the existing endpoint override and fallback behavior for legacy records. Clear provenance when an override changes the endpoint or when a response without token rotation encounters a concurrently replaced refresh token.
- Keep both metadata fields optional for older records without inferring provenance from token claims.
- Remove backend token error details from structured logs and refresh error messages.
- Box large futures in token refresh, MCP initialization, and embedded app-server test startup to reduce surrounding async frame sizes.

## Testing

Add coverage for legacy record compatibility and metadata round trips, browser and device-code login persistence, refresh using recorded OAuth settings, metadata preservation through rotation, and provenance clearing for a superseded refresh token.

A temporary exec-server transport loss could emit a thread environment disconnect notification while the session was still recovering.

## Why

A remote server can refuse the initial `thread/start` while shutting down. An explicit refusal establishes that no thread was created, allowing the TUI to retry without risking duplicate startup submissions.

## What changed

- Wait for the draining connection to close, reconnect within a shared two-minute deadline, and retry startup once.
- Preserve the initial prompt, confirmed draft, model, and reasoning effort across recovery. Keep drafts editable and allow cancellation of a pending submission.
- Restore input without submitting if recovery fails or startup is refused again. Continue treating a lost startup reply as uncertain and avoid automatic resubmission.

## Why

A new OAuth login can belong to the same account as an earlier session, while token refreshes can change credentials within one session. Auth consumers need to distinguish these cases when deciding whether a runtime can be reused.

## What changed

- Add `source_generation` to `AuthChangeState` and expose `AuthManager::auth_change_state_for` to check whether selected credentials still match the manager's current source.
- Preserve source continuity across OAuth refreshes only when session, issuer, and identity claims match. Advance the source revision for new sessions, credential replacements, and logout.
- Keep agent identity persistence from replacing cached credentials with credentials read from disk; credential publication remains managed by `AuthManager`.

## Testing

commits.title: Guard auth persistence and reloads against concurrent login changes (#55646)
commits.message:
Guard auth persistence and reloads against concurrent login changes (#55646)

## Why

An in-flight token refresh or auth reload can outlive a login change or logout. Its result must not overwrite credentials for a different login or restore stale cached auth.

## What changed

- Serialize in-process auth storage reads and writes that participate in credential updates.
- Verify the stored login before persisting refreshed tokens or agent identity records, while allowing older clients to drop login metadata when the refresh token still matches.
- Reject stale auth reload results using generation checks, and invalidate pending reads on logout even when the cache is already empty.
- Keep account grant reads strict when the keyring is unavailable, while preserving ordinary auth fallback behavior.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for stale reloads after logout, login replacement during refresh, legacy metadata loss, keyring recovery with rotated tokens, and refresh persistence failures.

commits.title: Avoid panics after background compaction fails before a checkpoint (#55581)

Polling a failed background compaction consumes the closed oneshot receiver.

Remove the receiver from session state before polling it, restoring it only when
its result is still pending. Discard closed receivers so compaction can fall back
normally.

checkpoint and automatic compaction falls back successfully.

commits.title: Avoid panics after background compaction fails before a checkpoint (#55581)
commits.message:
Avoid panics after background compaction fails before a checkpoint (#55581)

## Why

Polling a failed background compaction consumes the closed oneshot receiver.
Keeping that receiver in session state can cause a later await to panic instead
of falling back to foreground compaction.

## What changed

Remove the receiver from session state before polling it, restoring it only when
its result is still pending. Discard closed receivers so compaction can fall back
normally.

## Testing

Add a regression scenario where background compaction fails before the next
checkpoint and automatic compaction falls back successfully.

commits.title: Guard auth persistence and reloads against concurrent login changes (#55646)
commits.message:
Guard auth persistence and reloads against concurrent login changes (#55646)

## Why

An in-flight token refresh or auth reload can outlive a login change or logout. Its result must not overwrite credentials for a different login or restore stale cached auth.

## What changed

- Serialize in-process auth storage reads and writes that participate in credential updates.
- Verify the stored login before persisting refreshed tokens or agent identity records, while allowing older clients to drop login metadata when the refresh token still matches.
- Reject stale auth reload results using generation checks, and invalidate pending reads on logout even when the cache is already empty.
- Keep account grant reads strict when the keyring is unavailable, while preserving ordinary auth fallback behavior.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for stale reloads after logout, login replacement during refresh, legacy metadata loss, keyring recovery with rotated tokens, and refresh persistence failures.

commits.title: Avoid panics after background compaction fails before a checkpoint (#55581)
commits.message:
Avoid panics after background compaction fails before a checkpoint (#55581)

## Why

Polling a failed background compaction consumes the closed oneshot receiver.
Keeping that receiver in session state can cause a later await to panic instead
of falling back to foreground compaction.

## What changed

Remove the receiver from session state before polling it, restoring it only when
its result is still pending. Discard closed receivers so compaction can fall back
normally.

## Testing

Add a regression scenario where background compaction fails before the next
checkpoint and automatic compaction falls back successfully.

## Testing

Add coverage for all three policies across turns, including unchanged session and thread headers. Extend subagent coverage to verify inheritance of the default and omitted-key policies.

commits.title: Propagate authentication header failures before sending requests (#55607)
commits.message:
Propagate authentication header failures before sending requests (#55607)

## Why

Synchronous auth header construction could silently return no credentials when managed authentication became unavailable. Callers need an error to avoid sending requests with missing or partial authentication.

## What changed

- Make `AuthProvider::add_auth_headers`, `to_auth_headers`, and auth header telemetry fallible, and propagate failures through request and WebSocket setup.
- Return a transient error when managed authentication is unavailable, and preserve network policy denials through auth error conversion.
- Retry transient MCP authentication errors while treating build errors and policy denials as terminal.
- Cancel local MCP event streams before resolving authentication so cleanup still works when credentials become unavailable.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for rejected partial authentication, async header resolution, terminal auth errors without sending requests, managed account changes, MCP retry classification, and local stream cancellation after authentication becomes unavailable.

commits.title: Reserve a sibling rollout candidate slot for the first ancestor (#55627)
commits.message:
Reserve a sibling rollout candidate slot for the first ancestor (#55627)

## Why

Sibling rollout prefetching returns no paths when its candidate set omits the first ancestor. With more than 64 sibling rollouts, the candidate limit could exclude that ancestor and prevent prefetching.

## What changed

Pass the first ancestor ID into candidate collection and reserve the final slot for it until it is found, preserving the 64-candidate limit.

## Testing

commits.title: Add runtime assertion authentication modes and an auth provider (#55636)

## What changed

Add `RuntimeAuthProvider` to resolve request authentication through the runtime auth manager. Support `dual_header` mode, which sends a bearer credential alongside `x-openai-agent-assertion`, and `assertion_only` mode, which uses `Authorization: AgentAssertion …`.

Add coverage for both modes with API key and ChatGPT credentials, stale header replacement, fresh assertions, credential refresh without runtime replacement, registration failures, and configuration parsing and merging.

commits.title: Make pending injections interrupt agent waits and sleep (#55644)
commits.message:
Make pending injections interrupt agent waits and sleep (#55644)

## Why

Input injected before `wait_agent` or `clock.sleep` begins must still interrupt the wait and reach the next model request.

## What changed

Track notifying response-item injections as pending steering activity. Reset that state when pending input is consumed or cleared so later passive context does not interrupt waits.

## Testing

Extend wait and sleep tests to cover injections queued before the wait and delivered while waiting, alongside user steering. Add queue coverage for pending injection detection and reset after consumption.

commits.title: Fix in-process app-server shutdown with full queues (#55645)
commits.message:
Fix in-process app-server shutdown with full queues (#55645)

## Why

When unread events block notification delivery and the client request queue is full, shutdown can hang waiting to enqueue its shutdown message before reaching its timeouts.

## What changed

Drop the event receiver at the start of `InProcessClientHandle::shutdown` to unblock notification delivery before waiting for space in the request queue.

## Testing

Add a regression test that fills both queues with real requests and notifications, then verifies shutdown completes within the configured timeout budget.

commits.title: Guard auth persistence and reloads against concurrent login changes (#55646)
commits.message:
Guard auth persistence and reloads against concurrent login changes (#55646)

## Why

An in-flight token refresh or auth reload can outlive a login change or logout. Its result must not overwrite credentials for a different login or restore stale cached auth.

## What changed

- Serialize in-process auth storage reads and writes that participate in credential updates.
- Verify the stored login before persisting refreshed tokens or agent identity records, while allowing older clients to drop login metadata when the refresh token still matches.
- Reject stale auth reload results using generation checks, and invalidate pending reads on logout even when the cache is already empty.
- Keep account grant reads strict when the keyring is unavailable, while preserving ordinary auth fallback behavior.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for stale reloads after logout, login replacement during refresh, legacy metadata loss, keyring recovery with rotated tokens, and refresh persistence failures.

## What changed

- Add `CodeModeCellTiming` notifications for yielded executions, terminal waits, and unavailable cells, with thread, call, and cell identifiers.
- Measure how long completed results remain buffered before retrieval and carry `result_buffered_for` through the runtime, stdio protocol, and gRPC response metadata. Immediate delivery reports zero; waits without a completed result report no buffering measurement.

Add `MessageLifecycleContributor` hooks to capture extension state when local agent control publishes a message and notify contributors when the recipient commits it to history, before sampling.

Carry shared delivery state through submissions, input queues, and mailbox eviction with `PendingAgentMessage`. commits.title: Omit reasoning and compaction from Decisions snapshot comparisons (#55666)
commits.message:
Omit reasoning and compaction from Decisions snapshot comparisons (#55666)

## Why

Decisions snapshot comparisons reject requests containing reasoning or compaction, while conversation comparisons already omit those items. A parent compaction also causes snapshot comparisons to be rejected.

## What changed

- Share filtering of reasoning, compaction, and context compaction across both comparison modes, and ignore parent compaction when building the Decisions request.
- Distinguish malformed request setup from unsupported input items. Record setup errors as failures and unsupported input items as skipped comparisons.

## Testing

Extend the HTTP contract test to cover both comparison modes with reasoning, compaction, context compaction, and parent compaction while preserving message content. Update assertions for the distinct setup and unsupported-input errors.

commits.title: Enable app routing for remote curated Agent Plugins (#55667)
commits.message:
Enable app routing for remote curated Agent Plugins (#55667)

## Why

Agent Plugin manifests previously skipped app declarations, including service-generated declarations installed with remote curated plugins. This prevented those plugins from using app routing and suppressing matching direct MCP connections.

## What changed

- Recognize app declarations for Agent Plugins from `openai-curated-remote` across loading, capability summaries, plugin details, tool suggestions, and install authentication.
- Apply app routing to suppress same-name MCP servers when an app route is available. Keep unrelated MCP servers available and preserve direct MCP access in API-key mode.
- Keep app declarations inactive for Agent Plugins from other marketplaces.

## Testing

Add coverage for marketplace and authentication routing, service-generated app declarations during installation with both manifest formats, and app tools reaching turns. Verify that disabling Apps does not restore matching direct MCP connections.

commits.title: Improve diagnostics for compressed rollout read failures (#55545)
commits.message:
Improve diagnostics for compressed rollout read failures (#55545)

## Why

Undecodable compressed rollouts need diagnostic details and their original bytes preserved for investigation.

## What changed

- Log compressed file size, first-frame content size, decoded byte count, and whether the open file changed when a compressed rollout read fails. Limit warnings to once per process per minute and exclude paths and contents.
- Allow diagnostic reports to attach the raw `.jsonl.zst` archive after a decoding failure when no preferred plain rollout exists. Retain attachment size limits and append `.zst` to filename overrides when needed.

## Testing

Add coverage for truncated streams, incomplete trailing frame headers, files truncated after opening, and diagnostic uploads that preserve undecodable archives with size limits and filename overrides.

commits.title: Add scoped leases for persisted account OAuth grants (#55546)
commits.message:
Add scoped leases for persisted account OAuth grants (#55546)

## What changed

- Expose `AccountOAuthGrantLease` to prevent this auth manager's token refreshes from rotating account credentials during an identity-provider exchange. Releasing the lease returns an `AccountOAuthGrant` that callers can recheck before accepting asynchronous results.
- Validate grants against cached login ownership and persisted credentials, requiring OAuth provenance and complete account identity. Reject stale grants and propagate storage failures, including unavailable keyrings in `Auto` mode.
- Track `login_generation` separately from account ownership and use it to invalidate enterprise MCP authentication. Losing login metadata invalidates the login while preserving same-account network policy; a new login to the same account advances both generations.

## Testing

Extend auth refresh coverage to verify refresh blocking and wakeup on lease release, invalidation after token rotation or persisted login replacement, metadata loss and restoration, and logout while a lease is held.

## Why

An in-flight token refresh or auth reload can outlive a login change or logout. Its result must not overwrite credentials for a different login or restore stale cached auth.

## What changed

- Serialize in-process auth storage reads and writes that participate in credential updates.
- Verify the stored login before persisting refreshed tokens or agent identity records, while allowing older clients to drop login metadata when the refresh token still matches.
- Reject stale auth reload results using generation checks, and invalidate pending reads on logout even when the cache is already empty.
- Keep account grant reads strict when the keyring is unavailable, while preserving ordinary auth fallback behavior.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for stale reloads after logout, login replacement during refresh, legacy metadata loss, keyring recovery with rotated tokens, and refresh persistence failures.

A persisted login replacement can leave the auth cache holding the previous login, even for the same account. Enterprise MCP authorization must detect that replacement before continuing to use enterprise credentials.

commits.title: Fix TUI permission selection and session state handling (#55682)
commits.message:
Fix TUI permission selection and session state handling (#55682)

## Why

Queued prompts can resume before a pending permissions menu opens, and local
`/permissions` commands can bypass guards for outstanding permission changes.
Attaching to a different project can also retain model access information from
the launch directory.

## What changed

- Route `/permissions` through app permission guards and hold queued prompts
  while the menu is pending. Settle the hold when opening is rejected, discovery
  is invalidated, or a covering request is resolved.
- Apply the custom permission profile selection check beyond embedded servers.
- Refresh API-key model access when the first attached session changes the
  working directory, including with an embedded server. Propagate the widget's
  model catalog to the app and server even when the model response matches the
  widget's already-updated catalog.
- Skip sessions reported as `thread not loaded` during name lookup for all
  server types instead of falling back to unverified list metadata.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for permission guards, queued prompts across successive
permission menus, invalidated and covered menus, model catalog propagation,
project changes on initial attachment, and name lookup across server pages with
unreadable entries.

commits.title: Bound managed app-server and updater stderr logging (#55856)
commits.message:
Bound managed app-server and updater stderr logging (#55856)

## Why

Managed stderr logs previously retained a tail only before a new launch, allowing logs to grow during a long-running process. Direct stderr writes could also block lifecycle operations on disk I/O.

## What changed

- Route managed app-server and updater logs through a shared nonblocking worker with a bounded queue. Drop records when the queue is full or a record exceeds 16 KiB, and avoid waiting for the worker at shutdown.
- Prune live logs when they exceed 1 MiB, preserving the latest 256 KiB in `.log.previous` before truncating the current file. Keep inherited stderr handles usable after truncation.
- Pause predecessor pruning during Windows updater handoff and resume it after a failed handoff only when ownership has been restored.
- Keep ordinary stderr output when managed logging has not been initialized.

## Testing

Add regression tests for stalled workers and queue overflow, tail retention, inherited append and nonappend handles, and pruning exclusion during updater handoff.

commits.title: Fix enterprise MCP credential selection and reauthentication (#55859)
commits.message:
Fix enterprise MCP credential selection and reauthentication (#55859)

## What changed

- Prefer an eligible account grant over saved enterprise credentials, with a fallback to saved enterprise sign-in during initial connection if the account grant is rejected.
- Remember rejected account grants per enterprise MCP registration across threads and report authentication failures as requiring reauthentication. Keep administrator configuration errors distinct from sign-in failures.
- Compare account grants independently of access and ID token rotation, recheck the latest identity eligibility after exchange, and retry once when the refresh grant changes.
- Make MCP authentication status reflect usable account grants, saved enterprise credentials, and completed connection failures.

## Testing

Extend regression coverage for enterprise sign-in failures and recovery, MCP authentication status, account grant identity across token refreshes, and retries after transient credential failures.

commits.title: Recheck account login ownership for enterprise MCP (#55680)
commits.message:
Recheck account login ownership for enterprise MCP (#55680)

## Why

A persisted login replacement can leave the auth cache holding the previous login, even for the same account. Enterprise MCP authorization must detect that replacement before continuing to use enterprise credentials.

## What changed

- Check cached and persisted account login ownership before enterprise MCP connections and around token exchanges, revoking authorization when ownership changes.
- Recheck account ownership and login generation before committing enterprise sign-in credentials.
- Compare complete token data when checking whether an account OAuth grant is still current, and expose grant token access and credential comparison helpers.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for detecting a same-account login replacement without updating cached auth, rejecting enterprise MCP use after replacement, and keeping ordinary MCP usable while an enterprise account storage read is blocked.

commits.title: Fix TUI permission selection and session state handling (#55682)
commits.message:
Fix TUI permission selection and session state handling (#55682)

## Why

Queued prompts can resume before a pending permissions menu opens, and local
`/permissions` commands can bypass guards for outstanding permission changes.
Attaching to a different project can also retain model access information from
the launch directory.

## What changed

- Route `/permissions` through app permission guards and hold queued prompts
  while the menu is pending. Settle the hold when opening is rejected, discovery
  is invalidated, or a covering request is resolved.
- Apply the custom permission profile selection check beyond embedded servers.
- Refresh API-key model access when the first attached session changes the
  working directory, including with an embedded server. Propagate the widget's
  model catalog to the app and server even when the model response matches the
  widget's already-updated catalog.
- Skip sessions reported as `thread not loaded` during name lookup for all
  server types instead of falling back to unverified list metadata.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for permission guards, queued prompts across successive
permission menus, invalidated and covered menus, model catalog propagation,
project changes on initial attachment, and name lookup across server pages with
unreadable entries.

commits.title: Add account credential support to EMA token exchange helpers (#55685)
commits.message:
Add account credential support to EMA token exchange helpers (#55685)

## What changed

- Add an account IdP identity resolver that checks ID-token bindings against trusted issuer and client provenance before discovering the refresh-token endpoint. An expired ID token does not by itself invalidate the refresh grant.
- Generalize `EmaIdpIdentity` and token exchange requests to carry caller-owned credential leases. Invoke a `finish_idp` callback after the IdP exchange and before resource authorization server I/O so callers can release their refresh guards at that boundary.
- Reject empty expected OIDC issuers and client IDs, and expose an unverified issuer hint solely for explaining legacy login migration.

commits.title: Clean up failed and abandoned marketplace staging directories (#55689)
commits.message:
Clean up failed and abandoned marketplace staging directories (#55689)

## Why

Failed marketplace adds can leave temporary checkouts behind, and interrupted adds or upgrades can leave abandoned staging directories.

## What changed

- Share a staging guard across marketplace adds and upgrades so temporary checkouts are removed on completion or failure, including config-write rollback.
- Reclaim up to four abandoned directories per cleanup pass during add and upgrade operations. Use file locks to preserve active checkouts and operating-system-specific names to avoid reclaiming another platform's staging directories.
- Skip symlinks and unrelated entries, and report cleanup failures as warnings.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for failed adds, CLI and automatic-upgrade cleanup, cross-process ownership and abandonment, lock contention, bounded cleanup, and symlink handling.

commits.message:
Reclaim aged legacy marketplace staging directories (#55690)

## Why

Legacy marketplace checkouts have no owner lock and were skipped by staging cleanup. Age thresholds allow cleanup to reclaim them while leaving recent clones from older binaries alone.

Extend cleanup tests to cover both legacy age thresholds, preservation of recent legacy clones and live locked checkouts, and skipping legacy symlinks.

commits.title: Refine enterprise MCP auth errors and request authority checks (#55691)
commits.message:

## What changed

- Classify token-source failures by credential kind and exchange stage, with sign-in or administrator guidance that omits provider error text. Treat resource authorization failures separately from enterprise identity failures when deciding whether authentication is required.
- Add policy-bound request authority checks that return `RequestNotSent` when policy is updating or unavailable, while allowing admitted responses to finish. Support child authorities that isolate connection revocation and share response draining.

## Testing

Extend regression coverage for policy suspension during token renewal, completion of admitted requests, recovery with fresh authority, and transport retry classification. commits.title: Preserve enterprise MCP authorization across runtime refreshes (#55696)
commits.message:
Preserve enterprise MCP authorization across runtime refreshes (#55696)

## Why

Configuration reloads must cancel stale enterprise MCP startups while preserving access for running threads that still pass validation. Replacing a runtime during `thread/revert` must also leave the replacement able to use enterprise tools.

## What changed

- Separate pending startup cancellation from published thread lifetimes, with independent startup state for forks and replacement runtimes.
- Retain eligible enterprise MCP connections across refreshes and explicit reconnects while applying updated tool restrictions and approvals. Do not create replacement enterprise connections after initial startup.
- Revoke enterprise authorization when a thread is removed, drain requests when access is disabled, and revoke a connection's authority when token renewal requires authentication.

## Testing

Extend regression coverage to verify enterprise tool calls survive `thread/revert`, inherited fork configurations are cancelled after a reload, and enterprise calls fail after logout while ordinary MCP calls remain available.

commits.title: Resolve MCP backend identity from runtime events in rollout traces (#55710)
commits.message:
Resolve MCP backend identity from runtime events in rollout traces (#55710)

## Why

MCP callable namespaces and tool names can differ from their backend identities or match built-in tool names. Classifying calls by name can misidentify MCP calls and incorrectly parse namespaced `write_stdin` calls as terminal operations.

## What changed

Resolve `ToolCallKind::Mcp` from the runtime invocation's server and tool as soon as the runtime starts, before MCP correlation assignment. Preserve the caller-facing summary and raw invocation, and skip built-in runtime handling for MCP calls.

Only create dispatch-based `write_stdin` terminal operations for calls without a namespace.

## Testing

Add replay regression coverage for prefixed and unprefixed MCP aliases, names that match built-in tools, and `write_stdin` arguments with and without a session ID. Verify backend classification, preserved callable identity and dispatch lifecycle, and the absence of terminal operations and sessions.

commits.title: Allow unified exec to fall back when credential masking is unavailable (#55719)
commits.message:
Allow unified exec to fall back when credential masking is unavailable (#55719)

## Why

Disabled or failed protected shell snapshots prevent commands from running when credential masking is enabled.

## What changed

Restore unmasked credentials and continue execution when a protected shell snapshot is unavailable. Log and emit a warning explaining that the command will run with unmasked credentials.

## Testing

Extend `brokered_shell_snapshot_fallback` coverage for disabled and failed snapshots, including managed feature settings. Verify the warning, successful execution with restored credentials, continued filesystem sandbox and network policy enforcement, and masking recovery after snapshot storage is repaired.

commits.title: Avoid redundant clones when sending app-server notifications (#55723)
commits.message:
Avoid redundant clones when sending app-server notifications (#55723)

## Why

Targeted notification delivery and broadcast routing clone the message for every recipient, then discard the original.

## What changed

Use `std::iter::repeat_n` to move the original message to the last recipient, avoiding one clone per nonempty recipient list while preserving delivery behavior.

## Testing

Expand notification tests to cover empty, single, and multiple recipient lists, checking payloads, target order, and shared timestamps. Add broadcast coverage for zero, one, and two eligible recipients, verifying that uninitialized clients, clients without the required experimental API support, and clients that opted out are skipped.

commits.title: Share prepared MCP tool definitions across sessions (#55724)
commits.message:
Share prepared MCP tool definitions across sessions (#55724)

## Why

Sessions using the same MCP catalog can repeat schema normalization and retain duplicate tool specifications.

## What changed

Split immutable MCP tool metadata and normalized specifications from per-handler caches, and reuse matching definitions within each `McpManager`. Require matching tool metadata, agent-plugin mode, and schema budget before reuse.

Keep shared definitions behind weak references and prune expired entries on cache misses so completed sessions do not keep their schemas alive. Build definitions outside the shared index lock.

commits.title: Preserve code cell response metadata in rollout traces (#55725)
commits.message:
Preserve code cell response metadata in rollout traces (#55725)

## Why

Reducing code cell lifecycle events discarded their response payload references and lost the initial response status when the runtime status changed.

## What changed

Store the initial response status and separate raw payload IDs for the initial response and final result on `CodeCell`. Carry payload references through queued lifecycle events so they survive replay when the source item arrives later.

## Testing

Extend lifecycle tests to verify distinct initial and final payload IDs and the preserved initial status for yielded cells that complete and failed cells whose lifecycle events precede their source item.

commits.title: Add a critical-path utility for exclusive duration attribution (#55804)
commits.message:
Add a critical-path utility for exclusive duration attribution (#55804)

## What changed

Add `codex-utils-critical-path` to track shared dependency paths and attribute time to inference, automatic review, user waits, tools, overhead, and unknown work. Parallel joins retain the later-finishing branch, preserving its full history without double-counting overlapping work.

Clip attribution to the requested interval and count unrecorded gaps as overhead. Bound retained history by collapsing it into unknown work at the depth limit, with nonrecursive destruction and bounded debug output.

## Testing

Add unit tests for parallel joins, nested dependencies, ties, user waits, interval clipping, overlapping segments, history exhaustion, and safe formatting and concurrent release on small stacks.

commits.title: Measure Guardian review latency once with a monotonic clock (#55846)
commits.message:
Measure Guardian review latency once with a monotonic clock (#55846)

## Why

Guardian review metrics derived duration from wall-clock timestamps, while analytics measured elapsed time when tracking the result. Clock changes and delayed tracking could produce inconsistent latencies.

## What changed

Capture one monotonic duration at review completion and pass it to both metrics and analytics. Preserve wall-clock timestamps for event ordering, and saturate analytics latency conversion at `u64::MAX`.

## Testing

Add a regression test covering skewed wall-clock timestamps and delayed tracking, verifying that the duration metric uses the captured interval and completion timestamps are preserved.

commits.title: Bound retained turn analytics and clean up closed threads (#55847)
commits.message:
Bound retained turn analytics and clean up closed threads (#55847)

## Why

Dropped lifecycle facts can leave incomplete turns retaining analytics metadata indefinitely.

## What changed

- Limit retained turns to 256, evicting the oldest turn and its associated tool and review state when capacity is reached.
- Forward `ThreadClosed` notifications to analytics and discard the closed thread's turn and review state, including reviews received without turn lifecycle facts.

## Testing

Add regression tests covering metadata release after capacity eviction, continued reporting of new complete turns, cleanup isolated to the closed thread, and ignored approval responses after thread closure.

Refine enterprise MCP auth errors and request authority checks (#55691)

## What changed

- Classify token-source failures by credential kind and exchange stage, with sign-in or administrator guidance that omits provider error text. Treat resource authorization failures separately from enterprise identity failures when deciding whether authentication is required.
- Add policy-bound request authority checks that return `RequestNotSent` when policy is updating or unavailable, while allowing admitted responses to finish. Support child authorities that isolate connection revocation and share response draining.
- Recheck account validity after acquiring the credential invalidation lock and check cancellation before deleting a rejected credential.

## Testing

Extend regression coverage for policy suspension during token renewal, completion of admitted requests, recovery with fresh authority, and transport retry classification. Expand provider-error tests to cover `unauthorized_client` and `invalid_client` while checking that credential text is not exposed.

commits.title: Preserve enterprise MCP authorization across runtime refreshes (#55696)
commits.message:
Preserve enterprise MCP authorization across runtime refreshes (#55696)

## Why

Configuration reloads must cancel stale enterprise MCP startups while preserving access for running threads that still pass validation. Replacing a runtime during `thread/revert` must also leave the replacement able to use enterprise tools.

## What changed

- Separate pending startup cancellation from published thread lifetimes, with independent startup state for forks and replacement runtimes.
- Retain eligible enterprise MCP connections across refreshes and explicit reconnects while applying updated tool restrictions and approvals. Do not create replacement enterprise connections after initial startup.
- Revoke enterprise authorization when a thread is removed, drain requests when access is disabled, and revoke a connection's authority when token renewal requires authentication.

## Testing

Extend regression coverage to verify enterprise tool calls survive `thread/revert`, inherited fork configurations are cancelled after a reload, and enterprise calls fail after logout while ordinary MCP calls remain available.

commits.title: Resolve MCP backend identity from runtime events in rollout traces (#55710)
commits.message:
Resolve MCP backend identity from runtime events in rollout traces (#55710)

## Why

MCP callable namespaces and tool names can differ from their backend identities or match built-in tool names. Classifying calls by name can misidentify MCP calls and incorrectly parse namespaced `write_stdin` calls as terminal operations.

## What changed

Resolve `ToolCallKind::Mcp` from the runtime invocation's server and tool as soon as the runtime starts, before MCP correlation assignment. Preserve the caller-facing summary and raw invocation, and skip built-in runtime handling for MCP calls.

Only create dispatch-based `write_stdin` terminal operations for calls without a namespace.

## Testing

Add replay regression coverage for prefixed and unprefixed MCP aliases, names that match built-in tools, and `write_stdin` arguments with and without a session ID. Verify backend classification, preserved callable identity and dispatch lifecycle, and the absence of terminal operations and sessions.

## Why

Targeted notification delivery and broadcast routing clone the message for every recipient, then discard the original.

commits.title: Bound managed app-server and updater stderr logging (#55856)
commits.message:
Bound managed app-server and updater stderr logging (#55856)

## Why

Managed stderr logs previously retained a tail only before a new launch, allowing logs to grow during a long-running process. Direct stderr writes could also block lifecycle operations on disk I/O.

## What changed

- Route managed app-server and updater logs through a shared nonblocking worker with a bounded queue. Drop records when the queue is full or a record exceeds 16 KiB, and avoid waiting for the worker at shutdown.
- Prune live logs when they exceed 1 MiB, preserving the latest 256 KiB in `.log.previous` before truncating the current file. Keep inherited stderr handles usable after truncation.
- Pause predecessor pruning during Windows updater handoff and resume it after a failed handoff only when ownership has been restored.
- Keep ordinary stderr output when managed logging has not been initialized.

## Testing

Add regression tests for stalled workers and queue overflow, tail retention, inherited append and nonappend handles, and pruning exclusion during updater handoff.

- Compare account grants independently of access and ID token rotation, recheck the latest identity eligibility after exchange, and retry once when the refresh grant changes.
- Make MCP authentication status reflect usable account grants, saved enterprise credentials, and completed connection failures.

## Testing

Extend regression coverage for enterprise sign-in failures and recovery, MCP authentication status, account grant identity across token refreshes, and retries after transient credential failures.

commits.title: Skip conversation scoring superseded by newer scores and history (#55913)
commits.message:
Skip conversation scoring superseded by newer scores and history (#55913)

## Why

A delayed conversation classification can reach execution after a newer request has already published a score and committed history, leaving it with no useful work to contribute.

## What changed

Pass the classification's sampling timestamp into conversation requests and check for newer scores and retained history before starting inference. Return `Superseded` only when both have advanced; keep requests that can still contribute either a score or history.

## Testing

Add regression tests covering supersession of scores and history separately and together, including a classification delayed by permissions. Verify skipped requests send no inference request and preserve cached scores, approvals, and score progress.

commits.title: Preserve thread model settings across resume and revert (#55923)
commits.message:
Preserve thread model settings across resume and revert (#55923)

## Why

Resuming a thread can replace saved model settings with global defaults. A selected service tier can also be lost when the current model does not support it.

## What changed

- Restore saved service tier, reasoning summary, and personality on resume unless the caller explicitly overrides them, respecting thread ownership of settings snapshots.
- Retain the selected service tier for persistence, settings notifications, and resume comparisons while filtering the effective tier against the current model's capabilities.
- Carry the runtime model, service tier, and personality into thread revert reconstruction.
- Persist initial thread settings before user input during MCP startup so an interrupted first turn retains its settings checkpoint.

## Testing

Extend regression coverage for cold resume and explicit overrides, unsupported service tiers, settings preservation during revert, and settings checkpoints before user input when MCP startup is interrupted.
